jobs.title: Trust Investigator - Scaled Investigations
jobs.description:
At LinkedIn, our approach to flexible work is centered on trust and optimized for culture, connection, clarity, and the evolving needs of our business. The work location of this role is hybrid, meaning it will be performed both from home and from a LinkedIn office on select days, as determined by the business needs of the team.

This position will be hybrid in LinkedIn’s Omaha, NE office.

About the Team

We are seeking a Trust Investigator to join our Scaled Investigations Team. This role applies investigative tradecraft at scale to uncover coordinated, persistent, and high-impact abuse targeting LinkedIn members, and to drive the resulting enforcement and detection improvements. The work spans detection and mitigation of fake account networks, account takeover and credential abuse, payment and subscription fraud, and the scam infrastructure behind them.

Investigations generally begin with a single lead and expand through pivot analysis across account, device, and behavioral signals. Investigators own this work from the initial lead through enforcement, and surface the detection gaps that allowed the abuse to reach members. Their findings identify the product and model gaps that inform engineering investment.

Investigators on this team work with platform-scale data and have latitude to build their own tooling. We are looking for a self-starter who takes ownership over their work and enjoys being part of a fast-paced, collaborative, global team that values results.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead investigations into coordinated campaigns and abuse networks, expanding from an initial lead through pivot analysis across account, device, and behavioral signals.
• Track persistent abuse patterns and the actors behind them, including how they adapt after enforcement.
• Proactively hunt for undetected abuse and generate investigative leads using internal platform signals, open-source research, and threat intelligence.
• Define and validate detection logic from case findings, partner with Engineering, Product teams, and Data Science on implementation, and evaluate detection performance after deployment.
• Drive large-scale enforcement and takedown actions, including backtesting detection logic, validating targets before enforcement, and measuring false positives after action.
• Triage and route front-line signals and alerts, and provide escalation support and investigative analysis on high-severity incidents.
• Produce threat intelligence reports, briefings, and risk recommendations that identify product, policy, and model gaps exposed by investigations and inform strategic investment in our defenses.
• Use AI-assisted workflows, agents, and notebooks to scale investigation and analysis, and evaluate the quality and accuracy of AI output.
• Write SQL queries to access and analyze large-scale platform data, identify abuse patterns, test investigative hypotheses, and support enforcement and detection decisions.
• Build tooling, playbooks, and documentation that scale investigative methodology across the team.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's Degree in cyber security, criminal justice or other related technical disciplines, or equivalent technical experience
• 3+ years of experience investigating account, behavior, or content abuse, preferably within a trust and safety, social media, or online platform context
• Experience independently writing SQL queries to access and analyze large-scale datasets in support of investigations
• Experience using Python or another scripting language to automate investigative workflows.
• Experience with open-source investigation techniques and familiarity with a variety of internet research tools
• Experience synthesizing complex data sets into clear and actionable insights for diverse audiences

Preferred Qualifications

• BS and 5+ years of relevant work experience, MS and 4+ years of relevant work experience, or PhD and 2+ years of relevant work experience.
• 5+ years of experience in threat investigations, preferably within a trust and safety, social media, or online platform context
• A combination of investigative and technical skills, with the ability to define detection logic from case findings and work with Engineering, Product teams, and Data Science to implement detection rules
• Demonstrated AI skill development, including prompt and context engineering, agent use, and quality and accuracy review of AI output, with a record of applying AI to improve investigative workflows
• Experience conducting proactive threat and fraud hunting against large scale threats
• Experience with enforcement at scale, including bulk action preparation and false positive validation
• Technical acumen and the ability to translate data and investigative outcomes into actionable insights for Engineering, AI partners, and senior leadership
• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to inspire and influence across all levels of the organization
• Familiarity with frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK and cyber kill chain, and the ability to adapt them to platform abuse

Suggested Skills

• Trust Investigations of coordinated & complex abuse
• Platform Abuse Prevention
• Threat Hunting
• AI-Assisted Investigation
• Data Analysis (SQL, Python)

You will Benefit from our Culture

We strongly believe in the well-being of our employees and their families. That is why we offer generous health and wellness programs and time away for employees of all levels. LinkedIn is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices.

The pay range for this role is $109,000 to $180,000 Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, depth of experience, certifications, and specific work location. This may be different in other locations due to differences in the cost of labor.

The total compensation package for this position may also include annual performance bonus, stock, benefits and/or other applicable incentive compensation plans. For more information, visit https://careers.linkedin.com/benefits.

jobs.title: Fry Cook (Full Time)
jobs.description:
About The Role:

The Fry Cook is responsible for the production of food at various work stations.  They will control the quality and accuracy of all items (i.e., meats, vegetables, starches, bread products, etc.)  They also help to ensure cleanliness of the kitchen and safe operation of all equipment.

What You'll Do:

• Accurately prepares all food necessary for service. Works closely with front of the house staff on timing, presentation and quality to ensure guest satisfaction.
• Checks and controls the proper storage of product, especially on all fresh produce, checking on portion control, to maintain product quality and reduce waste.
• Keeps all refrigeration, storage and working areas in clean, working condition in order to comply with all regulations. Ensures all equipment is in good working condition for safe and efficient operation.
• Prepares requisitions for supplies or food items needed for production in the kitchen or any outlet/restaurant on a daily basis.
• Performs general/routine cleaning tasks using standard hotel cleaning products as assigned by supervisor to adhere to health standards.
• Keep floors dry and clean to avoid slip/fall accidents.
• Perform other duties as requested, such as moving supplies and equipment, cleaning up spills, etc., to ensure safe working environment.
• Successful at operating various kitchen posts such as prepping, frying, broiling, sautéing, plating, cold dishes, etc.
• Performs work when necessary at varying stations such as carving, grilling, action stations, plating, etc.

What You Bring:

• High school diploma or equivalent
• Advanced cooking experience required.
• Knowledge of food safety, sanitation, chemical handling, proper food storage, and temperature control standards.
• Understanding of cooking fundamentals, including frying, sautéing, grilling, soup and sauce preparation, cold food preparation, plating, and basic baking and butchery techniques.
• Ability to identify quality ingredients and maintain high standards when handling meats, seafood, produce, and other food products.
• Ability to follow instructions, learn quickly, and adapt in a fast-paced kitchen environment.
• Strong time management skills with the ability to work efficiently under pressure.
• Proficiency in operating, cleaning, and safely using commercial kitchen equipment and utensils.
• Basic math skills for recipes, measurements, portioning, and food preparation.
• Ability to read, write, speak, and understand English to communicate effectively with team members and guests.
• Ability to stand for extended periods and frequently bend, twist, reach, and move throughout the kitchen.
• Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds regularly and assist with moving heavier items using proper equipment and safe lifting techniques.
• Ability to work safely in varying temperatures, including hot kitchen environments and cold storage areas.
• Strong teamwork skills and the ability to work respectfully and effectively with a diverse workforce.

Preferred Experience

• 1-3 years of Fry Cook experience or equivalent
• Culinary schooling or related apprenticeship

jobs.title: Staff Product Designer
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets by automating and streamlining the work of assurance and audit practitioners, specifically in cybersecurity, privacy, and financial audits. Put simply, we build software for the people who enable trust between businesses.

We’re based in San Francisco, CA, but built as a remote-first company that enables you to do your best work from anywhere. We’re backed by top investors, including Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, Floodgate, Y Combinator, DNX Ventures, Global Founders Capital, Justin Kan, Elad Gil, and more.

We value diversity—in backgrounds and experiences. We need people from all backgrounds and walks of life to help build the future of audit and advisory. Fieldguide’s team is inclusive, driven, humble, and supportive. We are deliberate and self-reflective about the kind of team and culture we are building, seeking teammates who are not only strong in their own aptitudes, but who also care deeply about supporting each other’s growth.

As an early-stage startup employee, you’ll have the opportunity to help build the future of business trust. We make audit practitioners’ lives easier by consolidating up to 50% of their work and improving work-life balance. If you share our values and enthusiasm for building a great culture and product, you’ll find a home at Fieldguide.



 


ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Staff Product Designer to join the Fieldguide team. You’ll own complex, ambiguous problem spaces end-to-end, partner deeply with Product and Engineering, and help shape the design direction of a core Fieldguide product.

We move incredibly fast at Fieldguide, and we’re looking for designers who can operate at that cadence. This team ships frequently, iterates in tight loops, and makes progress amid ambiguity. You should be comfortable balancing speed with craft, incorporating AI into your daily design practice, and designing AI-assisted workflows directly into the product. This is a high-impact role for someone excited to own unclear problems, drive momentum, and help modernize audit workflows that customers depend on every day.




WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Lead end-to-end design for complex, ambiguous audit workflows, from problem definition through shipped solutions

 - Partner closely with Product and Engineering to shape strategy, influence roadmaps, and deliver high-quality, scalable implementations

 - Drive design execution with minimal direction, operating effectively in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment

 - Translate customer needs, research insights, and business goals into clear user journeys, interaction models, and polished UI

 - Balance speed and iteration with usability, consistency, and long-term product quality

 - Advocate for users while accounting for technical, regulatory, and business constraints

 - Own a significant product area or customer journey, anticipating downstream impacts across workflows and personas

 - Set a high bar for craft and influence by contributing to the design system, mentoring peers, and serving as a trusted design voice.
   
   


WHO YOU ARE:

 - 10+ year of experience in a Product Design role, ideally focused on complex, B2B SaaS products

 - You operate as a strategic IC — you don't just solve problems, you decide which problems matter

 - You think several steps ahead, anticipating how decisions in one area ripple across others

 - You're comfortable influencing senior PM and Engineering leaders, not just your immediate collaborators

 - Experience shaping how AI-assisted workflows get designed at a systemic level, not just within a single flow

 - You've coached or mentored other designers and can articulate why, not just what

 - You set a bar for craft and consistency that others look to as the standard

 - You can hold a long-term point of view while still shipping incrementally
   
   


BONUS POINTS:

 - Experience designing for audit, accounting, compliance, or other regulated domains

 - Track record of shaping design strategy across multiple teams, not just a single product area

 - Experience building or scaling design systems, standards, or team-wide processes

 - Background in workflow-heavy, document-centric, or B2B SaaS products

 - Experience coaching or managing designers, formally or informally

 - Familiarity with accessibility standards and inclusive design practices at scale
   
   


MORE ABOUT FIELDGUIDE:

Fieldguide is a values-based company. Our values are:

 - Fearless - Inspire & break down seemingly impossible walls.

 - Fast - Launch fast with excellence, iterate to perfection.

 - Lovable - Deliver happiness & 11 star experiences.

 - Owners - Execute & run the business with ownership.

 - Win-win - Create mutual value & earn trust for life.

 - Inclusive - Scale the best ideas with inclusive teams.


SOME OF OUR BENEFITS INCLUDE:

 - Competitive compensation packages with meaningful ownership

 - Flexible PTO

 - 401k

 - Wellness benefits starting on your first day

 - Technology & Work from Home reimbursement

 - Flexible work schedules

jobs.title: 2027 Technical Growth and Capture Intern/Co-op
jobs.description:
Advanced Space | Internship/Co-op | On-site

We’re going to the Moon. Want to help win the work that gets us there?

About the Role

At Advanced Space, we’re enabling humanity’s return to the Moon and building the technologies that will take us to Mars and beyond. We’re hiring an engineering student who wants to work on the business side of space as a Technical Growth and Capture Intern/Co-op.

You’ll join our Growth and Capture team, the group that finds, shapes, and wins the company’s new work. You’ll learn how a mission goes from a customer’s problem to a signed contract, and we’ll train you in our capture process from day one.

This is not an engineering position. You won’t design orbits or write flight software. Instead, you’ll support the people who win that work, so you’ll need the technical background to understand what our engineers do and explain why it matters to a customer.

We’re looking for the student with business cards or the grad student who owns a suit. If you’re an engineer who’s genuinely excited about business, customers, and strategy, this is the role for you.

This position starts in January 2027 or June 2027 and runs for at least one semester, with the potential to convert to a full-time Opportunity Lead role. It is open to U.S. citizens only, and candidates must be able to obtain a U.S. Government security clearance.

About Advanced Space

Advanced Space exists to enable the sustainable exploration, development, and settlement of space through innovative software, mission services, and technology solutions. As the owner and operator of NASA’s CAPSTONE™ mission and the Prime Contractor for AFRL’s Oracle mission, we’re helping shape the future of cislunar exploration while supporting commercial, civil, and national security customers.

Our team combines deep technical expertise with an entrepreneurial mindset. We move quickly, collaborate across disciplines, and empower every team member to make meaningful contributions. We are customer obsessed and mission focused; when we see it, we solve it; we are one team, motivated by our vision; and we bring technical excellence and inexhaustible curiosity.

What You’ll Actually Do

Build and maintain customer and opportunity records.
Keep track of who our customers are, what they need, and where each pursuit stands.

Support Opportunity Leads.
Help our Opportunity Leads move pursuits from first contact through proposal and award.

Qualify opportunities.
Use our structured qualification method to assess who makes the decision, what the customer needs, and whether we can win.

Research customers and markets.
Dig into customers, programs, budgets, and competitors to help shape our strategy.

Prepare for conferences and customer meetings.
Get the team ready for key engagements, then capture what was learned and route it to the right people.

Support proposals and contract packages.
Help assemble proposals and contract modification packages, including compliance checks, schedules, reviews, and submissions.

Turn conversations into action.
Translate customer and technical discussions into clear notes and follow-up actions.

Who Thrives Here

• You’re pursuing or nearing completion of a bachelor’s or master’s degree in engineering.

• You have a demonstrated interest in business, shown through what you’ve done and not just what you say.

• You write clearly and are comfortable speaking with customers and senior engineers.

• You’re a U.S. citizen and able to obtain a U.S. Government security clearance.

• You’re able to work on site at our Westminster, Colorado headquarters. This is not a remote position.

• You’re available to start in January 2027 or June 2027 for at least one semester.

• You take ownership. When you see a challenge, you work with the team to solve it.

Bonus Points if You Have Experience With

• Aerospace or systems engineering

• Coursework or projects in orbital mechanics, small spacecraft, or mission operations

• Student organization leadership, a business minor, sales or customer-facing work, or a startup or competition team

• Availability to work full time as a co-op during the spring semester (we can work around a class schedule if needed)

Success is Measured By

• Keeping customer and opportunity records accurate and up to date.

• Providing reliable, timely support to Opportunity Leads.

• Producing useful research on customers, programs, budgets, and competitors.

• Contributing to well-organized, compliant proposals and contract packages.

• Learning and applying our capture process.

• Demonstrating that you can contribute to our capture process as a future full-time Opportunity Lead.

Why Join Advanced Space

• Learn how real space missions are won, from a customer’s problem to a signed contract.

• Get trained in our capture process from day one.

• Work alongside experienced Opportunity Leads, engineers, and company leadership.

• Build a path to a full-time Opportunity Lead role.

• Join a team that’s passionate about delivering innovation to orbit and beyond.

Compensation & Benefits

• Paid position: $21-$27 per hour (based on education level and experience)

• Spring: full-time co-op preferred; we can work around classes if needed

• Summer: full time

• After the term: potential to continue part time if still a student, or convert to full time if graduated

Advanced Space is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace for all employees. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.

• Lead and oversee the day-to-day operations of the People & Culture function, aligning people strategies with business objectives and service culture priorities
• Serve as a strategic advisor to the General Manager and Executive Committee, providing guidance on organizational effectiveness, workforce planning, and leadership development
• Champion a culture of engagement by fostering an environment of trust, open communication, accountability, recognition, and inclusion
• Drive colleague engagement initiatives, including survey action planning, listening strategies, and targeted interventions that improve retention, morale, and performance
• Act as a steward of the organization’s service culture by embedding service standards, emotional intelligence, and guest-centric behaviors into hiring, onboarding, training, performance management, and recognition programs
• Coach and develop leaders at all levels to strengthen leadership capability, accountability, and consistency in delivering both colleague and guest experiences
• Partner with department leaders to translate colleague feedback, operational insights, and business metrics into actionable people strategies and measurable outcomes

• Ensure full compliance with federal, state, and local employment laws, collective bargaining agreements, and company policies; proactively mitigate risk through audits, training, and process improvements
• Direct and oversee workplace investigations, disciplinary actions, and terminations with a focus on fairness, consistency, and risk management
• Manage compensation, benefits, leave programs, and wellness initiatives to support a competitive and compliant colleague value proposition
• Oversee occupational health & safety programs, ensuring a safe and compliant work environment for all colleagues
• Utilize HRIS and people analytics to monitor trends, identify risks, and inform strategic decision-making across engagement, turnover, productivity, and service metrics
• Lead the development and management of the annual People & Culture budget, including forecasting, cost control, and resource allocation
• Continuously challenge the status quo by identifying opportunities to improve processes, elevate the colleague experience, and strengthen service delivery
• Support and lead colleague events and recognition programs that reinforce culture, celebrate success, and build community

We are seeking a Cybersecurity Engineer focused on Product Security to help design, assess, and secure our next-generation sensor platforms and supporting software ecosystems. This role will work closely with Software Engineering, Embedded Systems, Hardware Engineering, Infrastructure, and Program teams to ensure security is integrated throughout the product lifecycle — from architecture and development through deployment and operational support.

The ideal candidate has experience securing complex software and hardware systems within defense, aerospace, or other highly regulated environments. This individual will lead software security architecture efforts, perform threat modeling and risk assessments, support compliance initiatives, and help establish secure engineering standards across the organization.

This is a highly collaborative and hands-on role with direct impact on the security and resiliency of mission-critical technologies deployed in operational environments.

Responsibilities:

• Product Security Engineering Design and implement secure software and hardware system architectures for mission-critical platforms and supporting infrastructure Partner with engineering teams to integrate security requirements throughout the software development lifecycle (SDLC) Conduct architecture reviews and identify security risks across software, embedded, cloud, and hardware systems Develop secure design standards, engineering guidance, and product security best practices Support secure development initiatives including code review, dependency management, secrets management, and vulnerability remediation

• Threat Modeling & Risk Assessment Lead threat modeling exercises for software, embedded systems, hardware platforms, and supporting infrastructure Conduct cybersecurity risk assessments for products, systems, and operational environments Identify attack surfaces, trust boundaries, and potential exploitation paths Work with engineering teams to prioritize and remediate identified security risks Develop mitigation strategies for cybersecurity threats impacting deployed systems and sensitive technologies

• Compliance & Security Authorization Support cybersecurity compliance initiatives and product authorization efforts including: RMF (Risk Management Framework) ATO (Authority to Operate) Export control and regulated data handling requirements Assist with development of system security documentation, security controls, SSPs, and assessment artifacts Support internal and external security audits, assessments, and accreditation activities Collaborate with government, customer, and program stakeholders on security requirements and authorization activities

• Security Testing & Validation Assist with security testing activities including vulnerability assessments, penetration testing coordination, and validation of remediation efforts Support secure configuration and hardening efforts across software, operating systems, and embedded environments Review software and system telemetry to identify potential security weaknesses or anomalous behavior Collaborate with Security Operations and Infrastructure teams to improve enterprise and product security visibility

• Cross-Functional Collaboration Work closely with Software, Embedded, Hardware, DevOps, and Infrastructure teams to balance security, performance, and operational requirements Contribute to the development of scalable product security processes and governance Support customer and internal security reviews related to deployed technologies and operational environments Mentor engineering teams on secure development and security-by-design principles

Minimum Requirements:

• 5+ years of experience in cybersecurity engineering, product security, application security, or related engineering roles

• Experience with software security design and secure system architecture principles

• Hands-on experience conducting threat modeling and cybersecurity risk assessments

• Knowledge of secure software development lifecycle (SSDLC) practices and application security concepts

• Familiarity with cybersecurity frameworks and compliance standards including: RMF NIST 800-53 NIST 800-171 CMMC DFARS

• Experience supporting security authorization activities such as ATO processes and security documentation development, and eMASS

• Understanding of cloud, endpoint, network, and identity security concepts

• Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and technical communication skills

• Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced startup environment

• Must be a U.S. Citizen eligible for government facilities and sensitive information

• Ability to obtain additional security clearances as required by contract

Preferred Requirements:

• Active Security Clearance

• Experience supporting defense, aerospace, government contracting, or regulated technology environments

• Experience securing embedded systems, sensor platforms, or edge computing technologies

• Familiarity with export control requirements including ITAR and EAR

• Experience with secure DevSecOps pipelines and automation practices

• Experience with Microsoft GCC High environments and regulated cloud architectures

• Firmware development experience

• BIOS/UEFI security or development experience

• Hardware security design experience

• Trusted Platform Module (TPM), secure boot, cryptographic hardware, or supply chain security knowledge

• Experience with scripting or automation using Python, PowerShell, or Bash

• Security certifications such as CISSP, CSSLP, GSEC, Security+, or equivalent

Why CHAOS?

• Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company

• Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more

• Our Perks: Free daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code

• Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses

• Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices

Salary Range: $135,000 - $200,000

The stated compensation range reflects only the targeted base compensation range and excludes additional earnings such as bonus, equity, and benefits. If your compensation requirements fall outside of the range, we still encourage you to apply. The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations.

Recruiting Agencies: CHAOS Industries does not accept unsolicited resumes or outreach. Unsolicited submissions will not be reviewed or compensated.

jobs.title: Lead – Administration & Workspace
jobs.description:
InMobi (Corporate)

InMobi Group is a global technology company shaping the future of agentic commerce and advertising. Through its ecosystem of businesses — including InMobi Advertising and flagship consumer platform Glance — InMobi leverages data, machine learning, and generative AI to help brands reach audiences more precisely and consumers discover products more intuitively. Glance, which is pioneering new models of agentic commerce, is owned and operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of InMobi Pte. Ltd.

InMobi Advertising

InMobi Advertising, part of global technology company InMobi, is an agentic advertising platform helping brands and merchants achieve their business outcomes. Through its proprietary intelligence, AI-led solutions, and vast consumer reach — including flagship consumer platform Glance — InMobi Advertising delivers the omnichannel performance defining what's next in advertising and commerce. Glance is owned and operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of InMobi Pte. Ltd. To learn more, visit advertising.inmobi.com.

Glance

Glance is an intelligent shopping agent, redefining the commerce experience. Powered by proprietary agentic intelligence and generative AI, Glance delivers a hyper-personalized consumer experience across mobile and TV — shaping the new era of shopping. Glance is operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of global technology leader InMobi, and is backed by Mithril Capital, Google and Jio Platforms. To learn more, visit glance.com.

Overview of the Role:

As our Administration and Workspace Lead, you’ll own the day-to-day administration and facilities operations of our San Mateo, CA office. You'll make sure employees have a safe, well-maintained workplace and office services they can count on, while keeping expenses, vendor documentation, and operational reporting accurate and within approved budgets.

You’ll be the primary local contact for all workplace matters, coordinating service providers and partnering closely with our global Workspace team, HR, IT, Finance, Procurement, Legal, and building management. This is a hands-on lead role that calls for independent judgment, proactive follow-through, and a strong service mindset.

If you take pride in creating a workplace where everything runs smoothly, and people feel taken care of from the moment they walk in, this role is for you.

Location: This position is based onsite in our San Mateo, California office.

The Impact You’ll Make:

Office Operations & Facilities

• Lead daily office operations, conducting regular walkthroughs and maintaining an action tracker for repairs, employee requests, and service issues

• Coordinate preventive maintenance and repairs with building management and qualified vendors, covering facilities, furniture, lighting, air conditioning, plumbing, pantry equipment, and other workplace assets

• Keep workstations, meeting rooms, reception areas, and shared spaces ready for use, and coordinate room bookings and office arrangements for meetings and leadership visits

• Maintain the visibility and condition of InMobi signage, logos, and approved branding throughout the office

• Keep stationery, office supplies, and pantry items well stocked through inventory checks, reorder levels, and consumption tracking

Vendor & Landlord Management

• Serve as the local point of contact for the landlord, building management, and vendors supporting cleaning, catering, maintenance, security, pest control, transportation, and other office services

• Obtain and compare quotes, recommend the right service providers, and coordinate onboarding through the company’s approval and procurement processes

• Ensure signed agreements are in place for every engaged vendor, and maintain accessible records of contracts, service scope, pricing, contact details, and supporting documents

• Track lease and vendor contract obligations, renewal dates, notice periods, and service commitments, escalating upcoming decisions to Workspace leadership and Legal well in advance

• Review vendor performance, address recurring service gaps, and arrange approved backup options to minimize disruption

Payments, Budgets & Expense Reporting

• Coordinate timely payment of rent, maintenance charges, utilities, and approved vendor bills by securing accurate invoices and required approvals and following up with Finance

• Maintain complete payment records for audit and reconciliation, including invoices, approvals, purchase orders where applicable, receipts, and payment acknowledgments

• Prepare monthly office expense reports and forecasts, track spending against the approved budget, explain variances, and obtain approval before making additional commitments

• Tag expenses clearly by location, purpose or occasion, category, and budget owner, and partner with HR and Finance to distinguish HR expenses from Workspace expenses

• Reconcile office credit card transactions with receipts and business purposes, submit documentation on time, and follow up on missing or disputed transactions

• Identify practical savings through vendor reviews, demand planning, and reduced waste, while maintaining agreed service standards

Meals, Pantry & Employee Experience

• Manage employee breakfast and lunch arrangements, including headcount planning, vendor coordination, delivery schedules, food quality, and employee feedback

• Coordinate dietary requirements and allergen information with meal providers, and ensure meals are handled and served appropriately

• Keep drinking water, coffee machines, snacks, and pantry essentials available, replenished, and maintained, monitoring expiration dates to avoid unnecessary waste

• Gather employee feedback on facilities and services, respond to concerns, and keep people updated until issues are resolved

Travel, Visitors & Events

• Assist employees and visiting colleagues with approved hotel bookings, car services, and other local travel arrangements in line with company policy

• Plan monthly employee engagement activities with HR and the Workspace team, reflecting local culture and employee interests within approved budgets

• Coordinate local and international celebrations, office events, and leadership visits once the required admin and budget approvals are in place

• Communicate approved regional holidays and relevant office service changes to employees by email, in coordination with HR

Safety, Security & Emergency Readiness

• Maintain a safe and secure workplace through regular checks, prompt reporting of hazards, and coordination with building management, Security, and relevant internal teams

• Coordinate fire drills, evacuation readiness, emergency contact lists, and employee awareness of emergency procedures, keeping exits and emergency access routes clear

• Track inspections and servicing of fire safety equipment with building management and qualified providers, arranging refills or replacements when due and retaining service records

• Keep a well-stocked first-aid kit available, check expiration dates regularly, arrange replenishment, and coordinate with designated trained responders when assistance is needed

• Maintain an emergency escalation plan covering employee safety incidents, building issues, and major service disruptions, documenting incidents and tracking corrective actions

• Provide after-hours emergency coordination, including weekends and holidays when required, under an agreed escalation and coverage arrangement, escalating promptly and coordinating backup support

Cleaning, Hygiene & Pest Management

• Supervise routine housekeeping and weekly deep cleaning, using checklists that cover work areas, meeting rooms, restrooms, pantry areas, and shared spaces

• Monitor hygiene standards, waste collection, and housekeeping quality, following up promptly on deficiencies and maintaining cleaning records

• Coordinate pest-control inspections or service visits every two weeks, and arrange treatment or fumigation when qualified providers assess it as necessary, with appropriate approvals and employee communication

• Schedule disruptive cleaning or treatment activities to minimize interruption, and follow the provider’s instructions for safe access and re-entry

Onboarding & Offboarding Support

• Partner with HR to prepare welcome kits, workplace access, seating, and local office orientation for new hires

• Work with IT and HR to coordinate laptop delivery and setup before each new hire’s start date, tracking readiness and escalating delays to the responsible team

• Support HR with meeting room bookings and office arrangements for induction sessions

• Coordinate with HR and IT to collect laptops, access cards, and other company assets from departing employees, maintaining handover records and obtaining confirmation from the responsible teams

Policy Compliance & Operational Reporting

• Follow company policies and coordinate with relevant internal specialists and vendors to meet applicable local requirements for office operations

• Maintain organized records of contracts, expenses, inventories, safety checks, and service schedules, handling employee and business information confidentially

• Share regular updates with Workspace leadership on service performance, budgets, employee concerns, risks, and outstanding actions, recommending improvements and tracking their implementation

The Experience We Need:

Education & Experience

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification; an MBA or a qualification in hospitality, facilities management, or business administration is preferred

• 5+ years of relevant experience in office administration, workplace operations, facilities management, or hospitality

• Experience independently managing office services and coordinating multiple vendors, with prior lead or supervisory experience preferred

• Experience supporting a US corporate office, including working with local vendors and building management, is preferred

• Hands-on experience with expense tracking, invoice documentation, budgets, contract administration, and employee service requests

Skills & Working Style

• Strong written and verbal English, with the ability to communicate clearly with employees, vendors, leadership, and global teams

• Solid working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint, including the ability to maintain expense trackers, analyze spending, and prepare clear operational updates

• Strong organization and attention to detail, with the ability to manage competing requests without losing follow-through

• Sound judgment in prioritizing urgent issues, making decisions within delegated authority, and escalating risks early

• A professional, approachable service style, with discretion when handling confidential information

• The ability to guide service providers, negotiate practical solutions, and hold vendors accountable for agreed standards

• Availability for on-site office support and coordination across time zones, with flexibility for planned events and emergency coverage under agreed arrangements

At InMobi, you’ll be surrounded by people who…

• Think big and act fast: We’re entrepreneurial, thrive in ambiguity, and love solving high-impact problems

• Are passionate, fanatically driven, and take immense pride in their work: We care deeply about the impact we create and continuously push our potential

• Own their outcomes: We take responsibility, make bold decisions, and execute with confidence

• Embrace freedom with accountability: We value autonomy and understand that trust comes with responsibility

• Believe in lifelong learning: We welcome feedback, challenge ourselves to grow, and aren’t afraid to take smart risks

Award-winning culture, best-in-class benefits

Our compensation philosophy enables us to provide a competitive salary that drives high performance while balancing business needs and pay parity. We determine compensation based on a wide variety of factors, including role, nature of experience, skills, and location.

The base salary (fixed) for this role ranges from $105,500 to $120,000 USD (min to max of base salary). This salary range is applicable to our offices located in California and New York*.

*Our ranges may vary based on the final location or region of the roles, in accordance with the geographical differentiation in pay scales in the country.

In addition to cash compensation, based on the position, an InMobian can receive equity in the form of ESOPs (Employee Stock Option Plan). We believe that our employees/personnel should have the ability to own a part of the entity they are a part of. Therefore, the entity employing you may elect to provide such stock to you. Ownership of stock enables us to treat our employer company as our own and base our decisions on the company’s best interests. To encourage a spirit of shared ownership, we grant InMobians relevant company stock(s). As you contribute to the growth of your company, certain stocks may be issued to you in recognition of your contribution.

A quick snapshot of our U.S. benefits:

• Competitive salary and ESOP grant (where applicable)

• High-quality medical, dental, and vision insurance (including company-matched HSA)

• 401(k) company match

• Generous combination of vacation time, sick days, special occasion time, and company-wide holidays

• Substantial maternity and paternity leave benefits and compassionate work environment

• Flexible working hours to suit everyone

• Wellness stipend for a healthier you!

• Free lunch is provided in our offices daily

• Pet-friendly work environment and robust pet insurance policy - because we love our animals!

• Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

If this sounds like the kind of team, role, values, benefits, and challenges that excite you, we’d love to hear from you. Go for it!

InMobi is an equal opportunity employer

InMobi is a place where everyone can grow. Howsoever you identify, and whatever background you bring with you, we invite you to apply if this sounds like a role that would make you excited to work.

InMobi provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type.  All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

The InMobi Culture

At InMobi, culture isn’t a buzzword; it's an ethos woven by every InMobian, reflecting our diverse backgrounds and experiences.

We thrive on challenges and seize every opportunity for growth. Our core values — thinking big, being passionate, showing accountability, and taking ownership with freedom — guide us in every decision we make.

We believe in nurturing and investing in your development through continuous learning and career progression with our InMobi Live Your Potential program.

InMobi is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the hiring process and in the workplace.

Visit https://www.inmobi.com/company/careers to better understand our benefits, values, and more!

jobs.title: Clinical Quality Specialist
jobs.description:
Join the dynamic journey at Vynca, where we're passionate about transforming care for individuals with complex needs.

We’re more than just a team; we're a close-knit community. Our shared commitment to caring for each other and those we serve is what sets us apart. Guided by our unwavering core values: Excellence, Compassion, Curiosity, and Integrity, we forge paths of success together. Join us in this transformative movement where you can contribute to making a profound difference every day.

At Vynca, our mission is to provide comprehensive care for more quality days at home.



About the Job
The Clinical Quality Specialist for the Enhanced Care Management (ECM) program is a newly created role supporting all aspects of ECM quality. This position conducts internal chart audits across Vynca’s contracted health plans, provides clinical oversight of care management documentation, and translates audit findings into operational and educational improvement in partnership with ECM Operations and the Training and Development team. The role requires active clinical licensure and combines independent chart review with cross-functional collaboration, and flexes into training delivery as program needs require. This is a highly visible position that directly supports audit readiness for health plan and regulatory review while advancing internal standards beyond what any single plan measures.

At this time we are only considering applicants in the following states: California, Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Nevada, North Carolina, Oregon, Texas, Utah and Washington.




What you'll do

Internal Auditing and Monitoring

 - Conduct internal chart audits of Lead Care Managers across contracted health plans, applying each plan’s own audit criteria alongside Vynca internal quality standards.

 - Maintain audit cadence in accordance with the ECM Internal Audit Cadence Stanard Operation Procedure, including elevated cadence for new hires and staff on performance improvement plans.

 - Select audit samples according to defined chart composition requirements, including discharge and enrollment mix and minimum enrollment tenure.

 - Document findings objectively with supporting evidence locations so internal audit records can be used to respond to health plan documentation requests.

 - Analyze results at the criterion, category, Lead Care Manager, and health plan level to identify trends, areas of opportunity, and emerging risk.

 - Participate in inter-rater calibration exercises to confirm scoring consistency across auditors.

 - Support audit readiness for health plan and regulatory audits, including self-audit submissions and corrective action plan (CAP) responses.

 - Maintain the master audit record and reporting surfaces used for monthly and quarterly quality review.

Secondary Clinical Review and Clinical Oversight

 - Provide secondary clinical review of comprehensive assessments, care management plans, and transitional care documentation for clinical appropriateness, completeness, and defensibility, in addition to the oversight provided by Clinical Managers.

 - Provide clinical oversight as needed, including coverage and escalation support where Clinical Manager oversight is unavailable or additional clinical review is warranted.

 - Serve as a clinical resource to Lead Care Managers on complex member scenarios, escalation pathways, and documentation of clinical decision-making.

 - Support interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary care team activity, including documentation of clinical oversight requirements.

 - Review clinical content within training materials, assessments, and job aids for accuracy and alignment with scope of practice.

 - Escalate identified clinical risk, member safety concerns, or quality-of-care issues through appropriate channels.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

 - Partner with ECM Operations leadership to translate audit findings into workflow change, documentation standards, and targeted remediation.

 - Collaborate with Clinical and Program Managers on performance improvement plans, including audit-based evidence, progress monitoring, and tier and titration decisions.

 - Partner with Training and Development Specialists to convert identified gaps into curriculum updates, education huddle content, and remediation training.

 - Support the Compliance department on ECM audit readiness, regulatory monitoring, and quality assurance and performance improvement (QAPI) activities.

 - Communicate results, trends, and at-risk staff to Clinical and Program Managers and to Directors.

Training and Education Support

 - Flex into training delivery as program needs require, including onboarding, ongoing education, and post-remediation reinforcement for Lead Care Managers.

 - Develop and deliver audit-related education, including criteria walkthroughs, documentation standards, and findings review sessions.

 - Contribute to the design and maintenance of knowledge checks, test-out assessments, and competency validation tools.

 - Support preceptor and shadowing activities as a clinical subject matter resource.

General Duties

 - Maintain organized, audit-ready documentation of all internal quality activities.

 - Monitor CalAIM policy changes, Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) guidance, and health plan criteria updates, and assess their impact on audit tools and documentation standards.

 - Support the build and maintenance of plan-specific audit tools as health plan contracts are added or criteria change.

 - Support ad-hoc quality initiatives, policy development, and special projects as assigned.



Your experience and qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree required. Master’s in Nursing, Social Work, Public Health, or Health Care Administration preferred.

 - Active, unrestricted California clinical licensure required (RN, LCSW, LMFT, LPCC, or equivalent), or the ability to obtain California licensure within the first six months of employment.

 - 5+ years of experience in care management, case management, or direct clinical practice.

 - 1+ years of experience in quality auditing, chart review, utilization review, or quality assurance and performance improvement (QAPI) activities.

 - Previous experience with documentation integrity, including review of clinical documentation for accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and defensibility under audit.

 - Willing and able to work Monday through Friday 8:30am to 5pm Pacific Time.

 - Experience working with Medi-Cal populations, ECM, or CalAIM programs is highly desirable.

 - Working knowledge of clinical documentation standards, care plan development, and transitional care requirements.

 - Strong analytical skills with the ability to identify patterns across data and translate findings into actionable recommendations.

 - Exceptional written communication skills, particularly for documenting audit findings objectively and defensibly.

 - Ability to deliver difficult feedback constructively while maintaining professional credibility with clinical staff.

 - Proficiency with Google Suite, electronic health records, and virtual collaboration platforms (e.g., Zoom, Microsoft Teams).

 - Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple priorities and competing deadlines within a dynamic setting.

 - Cultural competence and the ability to interact effectively with diverse populations.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish.

 - Familiarity with the CalAIM initiative, Enhanced Care Management, and community-based care models.

 - Experience conducting or responding to health plan delegation audits, including corrective action plans.

 - Certification in healthcare quality (CPHQ) or healthcare compliance (CHC).

 - Experience with training delivery, curriculum development, or adult learning principles.

 - Experience with trauma-informed care, motivational interviewing, or other relevant therapeutic approaches.

 - Advanced spreadsheet skills, including formula-driven tracking and reporting tools.


ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

 - The hiring process for this role may consist of applying, followed by a phone screen, online assessment(s), interview(s), an offer, and background/reference checks.

 - Background Screening: A background check, which may include a drug test or other health screenings depending on the role, will be required prior to employment.

 - Job Description Scope: This job description is not exhaustive and may include additional activities, duties, and responsibilities not listed herein.

 - Vaccination Requirement: Employees in patient, client, or customer-facing roles must be vaccinated against influenza. Requests for religious or medical accommodations will be considered but may not always be approved.

 - Employment Eligibility: Compliance with federal law requires identity and work eligibility verification using E-Verify upon hire.

 - Equal Opportunity Employer: At Vynca Inc., we embrace diversity and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace. We value all applicants regardless of race, color, religion, age, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, disability, genetic information, citizenship status, or membership in any other protected group under federal, state, or local law.

 - Environmental Conditions and Physical Requirements: Works with Vynca patients/clients remotely and/or in-person. Successfully performs the essential duties and responsibilities of the position through the use of physical activities as described below:
   
   - Regularly requires sitting, standing, walking, talking, use of hands, listening, and observing.
   
   - Regularly requires working at a computer for an entire shift (with appropriate breaks).
   
   - Regularly requires use of laptop and video-conferencing technology.
   
   - Occasionally requires reaching, stooping, bending, kneeling, and lifting items weighing 25 pounds or less.
   
   - Occasional travel may be required to perform job duties, attend training, or company events.

jobs.title: Sr. Human Resources Business Partner
jobs.description:
Join the dynamic journey at Vynca, where we're passionate about transforming care for individuals with complex needs.

We’re more than just a team; we're a close-knit community. Our shared commitment to caring for each other and those we serve is what sets us apart. Guided by our unwavering core values: Excellence, Compassion, Curiosity, and Integrity, we forge paths of success together. Join us in this transformative movement where you can contribute to making a profound difference every day.

At Vynca, our mission is to provide comprehensive care for more quality days at home.



At Vynca, we're transforming care for people with serious illnesses- ensuring that individuals receive the right care, at the right time, in the setting that’s best for them. Our People team plays a key role in supporting that mission by driving a people-first, performance-focused culture across our remote, fast-growing organization.

As a Senior HR Business Partner at Vynca, you’ll play a key role in shaping a high-performing, mission-driven culture. You’ll partner with leaders across clinical operations, tech, and corporate functions to deliver strategic people solutions that drive employee engagement, retention, and growth. This is a hands-on, strategic role that blends day-to-day HR support with broader organizational impact.

The ideal candidate will have experience working in a high-growth company, especially one balancing mission and scale.



At this time we are only considering applicants in the following states with a strong preference for those CST based: Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Nevada, North Carolina, Oregon, Texas, Utah and Washington.



What You’ll Do

 - Strategic Advising: Serve as a thought partner to Vynca’s functional leaders, providing guidance on organizational design, team effectiveness, change management, and leadership development.

 - Employee Relations: Manage sensitive employee relations matters with discretion, fairness, and alignment to Vynca’s values. Coach managers through performance conversations and conflict resolution.

 - Talent Enablement: Support performance reviews, career pathing, manager capability building, and team development efforts.

 - Workforce Planning: Collaborate with leaders and Talent Acquisition on headcount planning, role clarity, and succession planning to support growth and scalability.

 - Culture & Engagement: Champion initiatives that foster inclusion, well-being, and a strong sense of purpose. Lead follow-through on engagement survey actions.

 - Compliance & Policy: Ensure policies and practices are compliant across multi-state operations, particularly in highly regulated environments (e.g., California).

 - Data-Informed Decisions: Use people analytics to inform strategy, identify trends, and develop targeted interventions.

Your experience & qualifications

 - 7+ years of experience working as a People Partner, HR Manager, HR Program Manager or similar role.

 - Experience working in a remote-first, multi-state organization.

 - Experience in healthcare, value-based care, or tech-enabled clinical services.

 - 4+ years experience supporting clinical teams.

 - Deep understanding of employment law and HR compliance in multi-state environments.

 - 4+ years experience navigating California, Colorado, Illinois, New Jersey, and Washington employment laws and regulations to support leaders with employment decisions.

 - A strong understanding of the employee lifecycle and how to tailor programs for a growing workforce - from onboarding to leadership development.

 - Skilled at building relationships, coaching leaders, navigating complex people issues, and compliance in a highly regulated or healthcare-related field.

 - Comfort using data to guide conversations, drive initiatives, and influence decisions.

 - A collaborative, coaching-oriented approach to working with people at all levels of the organization.

jobs.description:

America's industrial base runs on systems built in the 1980s.

Billions of dollars in critical components (F-35 parts, industrial assemblies, electronics, bolts, and hoses) still move through email threads, excel sheets, and disconnected ERPs.

We're replacing that with an AI-native platform that makes aerospace, electronics, industrial, and defense supply-chain operations nearly autonomous. Faster quoting. Faster procurement. Full visibility. Real operational intelligence for the companies our nation depends on.

 - YC W25 company. Top 5% growth in batch

 - Raised $10M+ from investors including Paul Graham, SV Angel, Pear VC, and CRV

 - Team of 20 co-live in our Warsaw & SF Hacker Houses

 - 7 figure ARR transacting ~$50M a week through our system

Call with engineer → 1hr technical test → Call with founder → fly out to SF HQ (on us) → offer.

jobs.title: Workplace Operations Manager
jobs.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

Role Overview:

We’re looking for an organized, resourceful and highly proactive Workplace Operations Manager to own the employee experience of our Los Angeles offices.

You’ll be the hands-on leader of our LA workplace: running day-to-day office operations, the vendors and services that keep things moving, and the programs that make it a place people want to be. You’ll bring structure to a fast-moving environment, anticipate what employees and teams need, and build the systems and standards that let our LA workplace scale as we grow.

This is a role for someone who’s just as comfortable shaping the long-term strategy for our LA workplace as they are restocking the cups in the kitchen. No task is beneath you, and no problem is too big.

You’ll coordinate across internal teams and external partners to keep services reliable, spaces well run, and stakeholders aligned. In addition to daily operations, you’ll take ownership of operational initiatives that improve the workplace, such as launching new service programs, tightening vendor processes, or improving how information and documentation are managed.

This role could make sense for you if:

• You thrive in a fast-paced environment and enjoy keeping a busy workplace running smoothly

• You’re energized by both the big picture of the employee experience and the operational details that make it work

• You instinctively create systems, documentation, and processes where none exist

• You’re comfortable managing multiple vendors, priorities, and stakeholders at once

• You communicate clearly, follow through consistently, and keep people informed

• You’re curious, resourceful, and willing to dig into unfamiliar problems

• You enjoy scaling operations and improving the way work gets done

Responsibilities:

• Own day-to-day operations across our LA building portfolio, serving as the primary point of contact for employees, building management, and landlords

• Manage workplace services end to end, including snack and beverage programs, office supplies, lunch services, mail and deliveries, and other on-site amenities

• Source, onboard, and manage workplace vendors, including contracts, pricing, service levels, invoicing, and performance reviews

• Plan and run events and experiences in LA, from team gatherings and all-hands to leadership visits and seasonal programming

• Manage the LA workplace budget, tracking spend, forecasting needs, and finding savings without sacrificing quality

• Partner with Facilities on maintenance, repairs, space moves, and building issues, ensuring requests are resolved quickly

• Support office expansions, renovations, and relocations in LA, owning defined portions from planning through occupancy

• Coordinate closely with IT, Security, Finance, People, Legal, and business leaders

• Maintain accurate records for leases, floor plans, workplace standards, vendors, and operational documentation

• Develop standardized documentation, workflows, and repeatable processes for workplace operations

• Gather employee feedback and use it to improve services, spaces, and programs

• Help create scalable workplace practices that can support a growing, global organization

• Work full-time onsite at our office in Los Angeles (El Segundo), California

Minimum Requirements:

• 5–7 years of experience in workplace, office management, facilities, operations, or a related field

• Experience managing vendors and service contracts, and owning a budget

• Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail

• Strong project management instincts with the ability to juggle multiple priorities simultaneously

• A hands-on, no-task-too-small attitude, with the strategic judgment to know which problems deserve a system and which just need doing

• Ability to work independently, identify what needs to be done, and move work forward without extensive direction

• A service-oriented, hospitality mindset and a genuine interest in the employee experience

• Comfortable building structure in ambiguous, fast-paced environments

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills across technical and non-technical teams

• Comfort learning and administering new operational tools and systems

• Curious, resourceful, and proactive; you enjoy figuring things out and improving the way things are done

Why CHAOS?

• Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company

• Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more

• Our Perks: Free daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code

• Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses

• Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices

Salary Range: $100,000 - $130,000

The stated compensation range reflects only the targeted base compensation range and excludes additional earnings such as bonus, equity, and benefits. If your compensation requirements fall outside of the range, we still encourage you to apply. The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. jobs.description:
We are looking for a Recruiter to join our Rexel USA team in Dallas, TX!

Summary:

The Recruiter will play a vital role in shaping the talent landscape of our organization. This role will be responsible for sourcing, researching, and implementing effective recruiting strategies to attract qualified candidates across various disciplines and locations. Collaborating closely with hiring managers and organizational leaders, the Recruiter will ensure that Rexel fills open positions in a timely manner with candidates who align with our values and contribute to our success.

What You'll Do:

• Specialty, Corporate, and College Recruiting: Lead full-cycle recruitment for Rexel’s specialty businesses and corporate functional roles, including Human Resources, Finance, Operations, Legal, and Information Technology. Develop and execute strategic recruiting plans in partnership with hiring managers, using data-driven sourcing strategies and recruitment KPIs to measure pipeline strength, candidate quality, timeliness, and overall effectiveness. Lead college recruiting efforts to identify interns and candidates for the early-career rotational program, ACE, by building and maintaining strong relationships with universities and candidates; effectively utilizing Handshake; attending college career fairs and other campus events; and developing sustainable talent pipelines. Continuously evaluate and improve university recruiting strategies while providing hiring managers with qualified candidates and actionable market insights.
• Recruitment Lifecycle Management: Manage the recruitment process from start to finish, including conducting hiring manager intake calls, sourcing candidates, reviewing applications, conducting phone screens, providing feedback to candidates, and extending offers for various positions across multiple disciplines and locations. Execute all recruiting activities with a strong sense of urgency to meet business and hiring needs. Develop and implement a clear hiring strategy for each assigned requisition in partnership with the hiring manager.
• Workforce Planning and Analysis: Collaborate with business leaders to understand staffing needs and projections. Utilize effective workforce planning strategies, including operational analysis and research, to provide insights and recommendations that enhance the candidate pipeline and align with organizational goals.
• Networking and Candidate Sourcing: Build and maintain a strong network of contacts to identify and source qualified candidates. Leverage industry connections, job boards, and social media. Participate in career fairs, conferences, and community job fairs to engage with potential candidates and evaluate the effectiveness of these events. Use proactive and innovative sourcing techniques to identify passive candidates, expand diverse talent pools, and consistently present highly qualified candidates to hiring managers.
• Efficiency and Process Improvement: Identify and implement process improvements that support the achievement of recruiting goals and key performance indicators (KPIs) around time, cost, and complexity for hiring managers and the Talent Acquisition Team. Manage requisitions and candidate activity with a sense of urgency, promptly addressing barriers and ensuring timely movement through each stage of the recruitment lifecycle. • Performance Tracking and Reporting: Adhere to established recruitment KPIs. Track recruitment metrics to assess the effectiveness of sourcing strategies and make timely data-driven recommendations for continuous improvement. Provide regular updates to leadership on recruitment progress, challenges, and successes.

jobs.title: Lead Technical Program Manager, Robotaxi
jobs.description:
Waabi, founded by AI visionary Raquel Urtasun, is the leader in Physical AI. With a world-class team, we're unlocking the next era of autonomous transportation with technology that's powering commercial autonomous trucks and robotaxis. Waabi is backed by and partners with world leaders in AI, automotive, logistics, and deep tech.
 
With offices in Toronto, San Francisco, Dallas, and Pittsburgh, Waabi is growing quickly and looking for diverse, innovative and collaborative candidates who want to impact the world in a positive way. To learn more visit: www.waabi.ai


Waabi is bringing its proven autonomous driving technology from trucking to the robotaxi space, and we need a program management leader to drive the execution. You will own the roadmap for integrating the Waabi Driver into our commercial fleet, acting as the connective tissue between engineering, operations, and external partners. You will partake in shaping our go-to-market approach, drive partner strategy, and ensure we deliver a safe, scalable rider experience. If you thrive on turning complex technical milestones into seamless commercial launches, this is your chance to be an integral part of Waabi’s next chapter.
 
You will...
Define and maintain the integrated robotaxi program plan — key milestones, cross-team dependencies, and critical path — spanning autonomy, vehicle hardware, safety/V&V, fleet operations, and commercial launch readiness.
Own program-level risk management. Surface issues early, bring data-backed options rather than just status updates, and ensure every dependency has a clear owner and ETA.
Drive launch and market-readiness planning across vehicle readiness, ODD (operational design domain) coverage, safety validation sign-off, site and facility readiness, and regulatory or permitting requirements for new markets and service areas.
Partner with Autonomy, Safety, Commercial, and Operations to translate top-down strategy into executable roadmaps, and hold teams accountable to the plan.
Build and run executive reporting — concise, credible updates on program status, risk, and path-to-green for leadership.
Define and track the KPIs that measure readiness for driverless operation, such as ODD coverage, disengagement rates, system readiness, and rider experience metrics.
Establish scalable processes and tooling for robotaxi program tracking, ensuring a single source of truth as the program and fleet scale.
Represent the robotaxi program in cross-company planning, ensuring it's properly sequenced against Waabi's trucking roadmap and shared platform investments.
Qualifications:
10+ years of technical program management experience, with a track record leading complex, cross-functional technical programs from ambiguity to delivery.
Direct experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics, or another safety-critical, deeply cross-functional environment spanning hardware, software, and safety.
Demonstrated ability to build program structure from scratch — dependency maps, risk registers, executive reporting, milestone tracking — in a fast-moving, early-stage environment.
Strong technical fluency across hardware, software, and autonomy/ML domains — able to ask the right questions and spot a false dependency without being a domain expert in any one area.
Excellent written and verbal communication; comfortable writing a crisp one-pager for an executive audience and facilitating a working-level technical review in the same week.
Proven cross-functional leadership without formal authority — you drive alignment and hold teams accountable through influence, not org-chart position.
Hands-on experience with program tracking tools such as Jira, Asana, or other Project Management.
BS or MS in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.
 
Bonus/Nice to Have:
Proven history executing driverless commercial rollouts, operational domain expansions, or initial market deployments for robotic transport platforms.
Working knowledge of system safety assurance, ODD boundaries, and integrating safety sign-off gates into target deployment schedules.
Track record establishing or scaling continuous fleet management, remote command facilities, or real-time operations centers.
Prior collaboration with policy, legal, and public affairs stakeholders to secure local operating authorizations and permits.
Hands-on application of modern AI solutions to streamline operational tracking, eliminate manual administrative friction, and speed up critical decisions.

The Manufacturing Associate will produce various DNA and plasmid products, focusing on molecular and cellular biology, as well as running analytic techniques in the high-throughput/highly-automated lab according to established SOPs, along with working with sensitive equipment and following good manufacturing practices. Candidates must also be a team player, neat and highly organized, able to work in a cleanroom environment and foster safe work practices.

The ideal candidate will be driven and will do what it takes to keep manufacturing on track in a fast paced start-up environment.  The Manufacturing Associate will be responsible for the production of custom gene based products and/or various intermediates according to established SOPs and complete manufacturing batch records to contribute to the daily production schedule.

Roles and Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

• Manufacture high quality custom products in a high throughput MFG lab according to established SOPs.

• Operate laboratory equipment and liquid handling robots such as Hamilton Stars, bioanalyzers, centrifuges, sealers, thermocyclers, spectrometers, Illumina Next-Gen sequencers etc.)

• Effectively use molecular and cell biology processes and techniques, especially PCR, DNA quantitation, purification and cloning.

• Maintain thorough, accurate and detailed documentation of all work performed using existing document templates and software applications.

• Update and write work instructions and documentation.

• Work independently and in a safe manner.

• Pay great attention to details and perform consistent work without excessive supervision.

• Help Leads and Supervisors with troubleshooting and the handling of process deviations.

• Package and/or organize products for shipping.

• Work according to Good Manufacturing and ISO practices. Learn, adopt and promote lean manufacturing concepts.

• Complete all the daily assigned tasks to keep the manufacturing schedule on track and report back to Lead and Supervisor.

What You’ll Bring to the Team

• Relevant experience that can indicate success in a high throughput, fast pace laboratory manufacturing environment.

• Associates or Bachelors degree in Biology, chemistry or related field is desirable.

• Familiarity or prior experience in a manufacturing and/or a laboratory environment is highly desirable.

• Good written and verbal skills are critical.

• Good computer skills (Excel, Word, Atlassian etc) and the ability to quickly learn new software applications.

• Ability to pay great attention to details.

Working Conditions

• The work will be performed in a very dynamic laboratory team environment.

• It is a controlled laboratory environment.

• Must be able to stand for long periods of time while performing duties.

• Must be able to work safely with chemicals and hazardous materials.

• Must be able to lift up to 20 lbs.

• Must be able to work outside of regular work hours/ work a flexible shift as needed

About Twist Bioscience

Twist Bioscience synthesizes genes from scratch, known as “writing” DNA. Just as children learn to both read and write, the next phase of development for the genomics revolution is the ability to write DNA.

At Twist Bioscience, we work in service of people who are changing the world for the better. In fields such as health care, agriculture, industrial chemicals and data storage, our unique silicon-based DNA Synthesis Platform provides precision at a scale that is otherwise unavailable to our customers.
