jobs.title: CX Systems Strategy and Solutions Lead
jobs.description:
Job Posting End Date

10-23-2026

Please note the job posting will close on the day before the posting end date.

Job Summary

Working within Waterfall or Agile frameworks, a Business Analyst will work with a variety of disciplined focused team members all working toward a common goal of delivering value with quality and scale. Responsible for collaborating with other Job Families such within Technology and across our business partners to deliver consistent, reliable technology solutions that leverage AEP's technology standards, architectures and best practices.  Independently performs advanced business and project analysis for any sized project.

Job Description

The IT Consultant Senior - Customer Experience Systems Strategy and Solutions is responsible for business relationship, portfolio strategy, product direction, customer and employee experience, opportunity analysis, prioritization, adoption, and value realization across the Customer Experience Systems portfolio. The role jointly manages the portfolio with the Customer Experience Systems Engineering Lead and represents Customer Operations throughout planning, design, implementation, measurement, and continuous improvement.

The position partners with Contact Center and Customer Operations leaders, Technology teams, and Gigawatt partners to identify and shape AI-enabled and other advantageous technical enhancements. The role protects the intended customer and employee experience, defines business outcomes and controls, and ensures solutions are adopted and deliver measurable value.

What you’ll do:

Essential Job Functions & Tasks

Strategic Leadership

• Develop and maintain the multi-year Customer Experience Systems strategy and product portfolio roadmap.
• Align investments with Customer Operations priorities, customer experience objectives, enterprise strategies, regulatory needs, and measurable outcomes.
• Anticipate customer, workforce, channel, operational, and technology trends and recommend strategic responses.
• Drive simplification, reuse, application rationalization, and coordinated planning across the portfolio.

Business and Operational Partnership

• Serve as a primary Technology relationship partner for Customer Operations and Contact Center leadership.
• Develop deep understanding of customer journeys, operating processes, employee workflows, performance measures, pain points, and emerging needs.
• Facilitate portfolio planning, demand intake, prioritization, funding, governance, and executive decision discussions.
• Translate business and operational challenges into clear opportunities, product strategies, requirements, and outcome measures.

Product, Experience, and Analysis Leadership

• Lead product discovery, customer journey analysis, employee workflow analysis, process design, experience requirements, use-case definition, and value hypotheses.
• Serve as a primary business and operations partner for the move from Genesys Engage to Genesys Cloud CX, keeping the migration tied to Customer Operations priorities and the intended customer and employee experience.
• Shape the order in which each line of business moves to Genesys Cloud CX, balancing operational readiness, call volume, regulatory commitments, and cutover risk.
• Lead the review of current routing, IVR, self-service, and agent workflows, and decide what to redesign, simplify, or retire rather than move as-is.
• Make sure business requirements, acceptance criteria, and success measures are defined for each migration wave, and lead business acceptance alongside Contact Center leadership.
• Establish product vision, scope, business requirements, acceptance criteria, business ownership, roadmaps, and success measures.
• Use customer feedback, employee insights, operational data, analytics, and research to guide product decisions.
• Balance customer value, employee experience, operational need, risk, regulatory commitments, technical debt, cost, and delivery capacity.

AI Solution Partnership and Lifecycle

• Shape customer and employee AI use cases and partner with Gigawatt teams that lead development of underlying AI solutions.
• Lead business participation in experimentation, proofs of concept, prompt and conversation-design requirements, user evaluation, and business acceptance.
• Partner in data and knowledge readiness, human review and escalation design, responsible-use assessments, output-quality monitoring, solution-performance monitoring, and ongoing tuning.
• Define adoption, process integration, business controls, expected outcomes, and criteria for expansion, redesign, replacement, or retirement.

Technology and Engineering Partnership

• Work with the Engineering Lead from discovery forward to incorporate technical feasibility, architecture, dependencies, risk, capacity, and lifecycle implications.
• Translate portfolio priorities into clear business objectives, product requirements, experience requirements, and measurable outcomes.
• Participate in solution options and design reviews to preserve business intent and customer and employee experience.
• Jointly manage dependencies and tradeoffs across Genesys, digital channels, customer platforms, data, integrations, infrastructure, and Gigawatt-enabled capabilities.

Adoption, Change, and Value Realization

• Assess impacts to customers, employees, processes, policies, controls, training, communications, and performance measures.
• Lead operational readiness, stakeholder engagement, pilot feedback, adoption planning, and business acceptance.
• Establish baselines and monitor customer satisfaction, effort, self-service, first-contact resolution, employee productivity, quality, adoption, efficiency, and financial value.
• Use outcomes and feedback to recommend tuning, expansion, redesign, replacement, consolidation, or retirement.

jobs.title: CX Systems Engineering Lead
jobs.description:
Job Posting End Date

10-23-2026

Please note the job posting will close on the day before the posting end date.

Job Summary

Responsible for the technical architecture and engineering integrity of the Customer Experience Systems portfolio. Leads solution design, software and platform engineering, infrastructure, system integration, and technical resource planning. Ensures solutions are secure, scalable, reliable, supportable, and sustainable. Promotes architecture principles, engineering standards, and enterprise technology solutions that meet business needs and align with Customer Operations and enterprise strategies. Provides technical leadership across solution delivery, production readiness, reliability, and lifecycle management. Decisions are guided by policies, procedures, enterprise standards, business plans, and portfolio objectives.

Job Description

The IT Consultant Senior - Customer Experience Systems Engineering is responsible for technical strategy, architecture, system design, engineering direction, infrastructure, integration, technical-resource planning, technical execution, reliability, and lifecycle health across the Customer Experience Systems portfolio. The role jointly manages the portfolio with the Strategy and Solutions Lead and translates desired customer and operational outcomes into secure, scalable, resilient, observable, supportable, and maintainable solutions.

The role must have sufficient Contact Center and CCaaS expertise to learn quickly, evaluate designs and configurations, guide technical teams, diagnose complex issues, and roll up sleeves when appropriate. The position is not primarily a project manager, Scrum Master, platform administrator, or production-support coordinator.

What you’ll do:

Essential Job Functions & Tasks

Technical Strategy and Solution Architecture

• Define current-state, transition-state, and future-state architecture and the engineering roadmap for Customer Experience Systems.
• Translate product roadmaps into technical strategies, solution options, architecture decisions, integration approaches, infrastructure needs, and engineering plans.
• Lead technical discovery and assess feasibility, complexity, dependencies, constraints, risk, effort, capacity, and sequencing.
• Establish reusable patterns, engineering standards, nonfunctional requirements, and design-review practices.
• Evaluate tradeoffs among buy, build, configure, integrate, and reuse options.

Contact Center and Customer Platform Engineering

• Provide technical leadership for the move from Genesys Engage to Genesys Cloud CX, from current-state assessment through each migration wave, cutover, and stabilization.
• Define the target architecture for Genesys Cloud CX, including telephony and carrier connectivity, routing and IVR design, identity and access, security controls, and integrations with AEP customer and enterprise systems.
• Work with Genesys delivery teams and systems integrators to review designs, configurations, and test evidence, and protect AEP’s architecture standards and long-term supportability.
• Lead technical planning for migrating integrations, data flows, and contact center reporting, and look for ways to reduce custom code and point-to-point integrations along the way.
• Own technical readiness for each cutover, including performance, resilience, failover, rollback, and production support handoffs, so service to customers isn’t disrupted.
• Build internal Genesys Cloud CX skills across the team, cutting long-term reliance on vendors and preparing AEP to administer and improve the platform after migration.
• Provide technical leadership for Genesys CCaaS, IVR, conversational self-service, voice, digital channels, routing, workforce engagement, recording, quality, analytics, and agent experience.
• Guide technical optimization of mobile, web, customer information, CRM, case management, knowledge, identity, communications, payment, outage, analytics, and data capabilities.
• Evaluate native product features, enterprise platforms, and custom-development options before recommending solutions.
• Monitor platform roadmaps, releases, deprecations, capacity, availability, performance, resilience, and technical opportunities.

Application, Data, Integration, and Infrastructure Engineering

• Lead solution design across applications, services, APIs, events, integrations, data flows, cloud, networks, environments, identity, and infrastructure.
• Ensure clear interface contracts, error handling, security, observability, resilience, performance, recovery, and support ownership.
• Promote DevSecOps, automated testing, configuration and infrastructure automation, repeatable deployment, and technical documentation.
• Reduce brittle point-to-point integrations, duplicated services, unsupported components, and unnecessary customization.

AI Solution Engineering Partnership

• Work with Gigawatt partners that lead development of underlying AI solutions while representing Customer Experience Systems architecture, integration, infrastructure, security, performance, reliability, and lifecycle needs.
• Partner in experimentation, proofs of concept, prompt and conversation design, AI evaluation and testing, and data and knowledge readiness.
• Define APIs, events, data flows, identity, access, monitoring, traceability, human oversight, fallback, and operational handoffs.
• Monitor technical and output quality, solution performance, security, reliability, and scalability and support ongoing tuning, expansion, redesign, replacement, or retirement decisions.

Hands-On Technical Leadership and Resource Strategy

• Provide technical direction to developers, engineers, architects, infrastructure teams, data teams, vendors, and systems integrators.
• Determine the skills, capacity, environments, tooling, and sourcing needed and recommend how to bring in or staff the right technical resources.
• Review code, configurations, designs, test evidence, and technical documentation when appropriate.
• Build or guide prototypes, validate critical assumptions, and diagnose complex technical issues when hands-on involvement is needed.
• Challenge vendor recommendations and protect AEP architecture, engineering quality, supportability, and long-term value.

Engineering Execution and Readiness

• Convert portfolio priorities into architecture deliverables, engineering tasks, estimates, dependencies, milestones, and technical work plans.
• Lead design reviews, technical risk management, cross-team dependency resolution, and engineering-quality reviews.
• Ensure functional and nonfunctional requirements are addressed through appropriate testing and evidence.
• Lead technical-readiness recommendations covering security, performance, resilience, observability, deployment, rollback, recovery, supportability, and production readiness.

Reliability, Security, and Lifecycle Engineering

• Establish service objectives and measures for availability, performance, capacity, resilience, recoverability, observability, supportability, and maintainability.
• Lead engineering analysis of significant or recurring incidents and ensure root causes are addressed.
• Guide vulnerability remediation, problem management, obsolescence planning, technical debt reduction, platform lifecycle, and modernization.
• Ensure production teams have adequate telemetry, documentation, runbooks, escalation paths, and technical knowledge.
• Incorporate cybersecurity, privacy, data governance, accessibility, records, and regulatory requirements from the beginning.

Decision Support and Cross-Functional Technical Leadership

• Jointly prepare decision-quality recommendations on solution approach, architecture, buy-build-configure-reuse choices, exceptions, AI risk, sourcing, funding, resources, and production readiness.
• Explain technical options, tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, staffing, cost, sequencing, and lifecycle implications to senior technical and operational leaders.
• Identify and engage appropriate architecture, cybersecurity, infrastructure, data, legal, privacy, finance, procurement, governance, platform, and vendor stakeholders.
• Mentor technical resources and promote shared standards, internal knowledge, automation, and reduced vendor dependency.

Qualifications

Required

• Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, or a related technical field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
• Eight or more years of progressive experience in software development, application engineering, solution architecture, platform engineering, infrastructure, system integration, or a related discipline.
• Experience providing technical leadership for complex enterprise applications, platforms, integrations, infrastructure, or software-delivery initiatives.
• Strong understanding of architecture, software engineering, APIs, integration, data flows, cloud, infrastructure, security, testing, deployment, observability, reliability, and supportability.
• Experience translating product needs into technical options, architecture, plans, estimates, resource needs, and executable work.
• Demonstrated ability to review technical designs or configurations, guide prototypes, lead problem diagnosis, and roll up sleeves when appropriate.
• Experience leading through influence across internal teams, vendors, and systems integrators.

Preferred

• Experience with Genesys Cloud or another enterprise CCaaS platform.
• Experience supporting broad Customer Experience Systems or large-scale Contact Center and Customer Operations environments.
• Experience integrating customer-facing or employee-facing AI, automation, conversational, analytics, or digital capabilities.
• Experience with AWS, API management, identity, data platforms, observability, DevSecOps, resilience engineering, and cybersecurity controls.
• Experience in a regulated industry, preferably electric utility or energy.

Leadership Competencies

Success Measures

A senior technical leader with broad engineering depth and sufficient Contact Center and CCaaS expertise to operate credibly from architecture through detailed technical decisions. jobs.title: Global Process Engineering Authority – Stator Wind Manufacturing
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

The Global Process Engineering Authority (GPEA) will work closely with the Global Process Engineering Leader (GPEL) for the Generator Value Stream, the primary focus area will be developing and deploying global standards that improve the reliability, availability, and performance of GE Vernova’s manufacturing equipment and maintenance processes. They will analyze data, and work cross-functionally to implement proactive measures that improve generator processes.

In this role, you will also be responsible for cost reduction through standardization of equipment and processes, establishing standards, and ensuring adherence to these standards. You will also be a focal point for new technology introductions, asset transfers, new process introductions; inclusive of lead time, technology selection and recommendations for fixturing, process, control plans, and qualifications of manufacturing assets. The GPEA will coach and influence a dotted-line organization, comprised of factory technical leads across the supply chain. Critical to the role is leveraging analytical skills, the lean methodology and the guiding principle of creating process standards for equipment (“One Product One Process”) to drive SQDC in line with business and functional objectives.

The candidate chosen for this position will acquire strong technical knowledge and extensive exposure to manufacturing, engineering, quality, and safe process development. The selected candidate plays a key role in the value stream, and in building a culture of inclusion and respect for people as well as continuous improvement.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

• Define, control, communicate global processes for manufacturing assets, including facility integration, acceptance testing, machine health checks & calibrations, preventative maintenance plans, spare parts strategy, technical & technology training.

• Validate design specifications and shop floor application of new processes. Including EHS, Manufacturing Engineers, Engineering, Quality, Materials, Industrialization, Materials, and Sourcing.

• Develop and implement reliability improvement strategies using industry best practices such as FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis), and Root Cause Analysis (RCA).

• Collaborate with maintenance, operations, engineering, and safety teams to design and implement preventive and predictive programs.

• Establish key performance indicators (KPIs) for equipment reliability, and track progress against targets.

• Drive continuous improvement initiatives aimed at reducing equipment downtime and improve quality processes.

• Lead investigations into failures and chronic issues, identifying root causes and implementing long-term solutions.

• Provide technical support for asset management, including equipment life cycle analysis and spare parts optimization.

• Participating in the design and installation of new equipment and implementation of processes, ensuring reliability is considered from the outset (Design for Reliability).

• Requires specialized knowledge within the function. Influence the development of strategy for the area of responsibility, including control of resources and influences policy formulation.

• Interprets internal and external business challenges and recommends best practices to improve products, processes or services. Stays informed of industry trends that may inform work.

• Uses high level of judgment to make decisions and handle complex tasks or problems in areas of operational, product management, manufacturing, technology or engineering. Has ability to assess quality of information given and ask pertinent questions to stakeholders. Able to offer new solutions to problems outside of set parameters and can construct and provide recommendations. Uses multiple internal and some external sources outside of own function to help arrive at a decision.

• Will lead functional teams or projects with minimal resource requirements, risk, and/or complexity. Communicates difficult concepts and may influence others' options on particular topics. May guide others to consider a different point of view.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited university or college with a minimum of 10 years of industrial experience in manufacturing or quality OR a High School Diploma / GED with at least 15 years of industrial experience in manufacturing or quality
• 5 years of generator manufacturing experience

• Strong knowledge of engineering concepts and quality processes

• Ability to interpret blueprints, specifications, drawings, and schematics

• Project Management skills and experience
• Willing and able to travel approximately 25% globally

Technical Requirements

• Experience working cross functionally and Co-leading the implementation of manufacturing systems that support Next Generation Supply Chain migration globally across the Generator Value Stream

• Experience utilizing design for Six Sigma methodology (DFSS), including, measuring existing machine capability, analyzing process requirements, and developing a strategy to maintain / improve process yield

• Ability to deploy lean principles, including, Transformation Planning, 3P (Production Preparation Process), Total Productive Maintenance, Standard Work, Kaizen, Problem Solving, and Poka Yoke.

Desired Characteristics

• Managed a cost center or P&L with a solid understanding of operational metrics

• Direct leadership experience of both professional and production employees.

• Ability to coach and influence others and lead small teams

• Strong oral and written communication skills

• Strong interpersonal and leadership skills

• Lead initiatives of moderate scope and impact

• Ability to coordinate and manage several projects simultaneously

• Effective problem identification and solution skills

• Proven analytical and organizational ability

• Deep manufacturing technical expertise

• Has comprehensive knowledge of underlying principles, approaches, and methodology

Benefits Available to You

GE Vernova employees rise to the challenge of building a world that works. In order to meet this mission, we provide varied, competitive benefits to help support our workforce: Our Culture | GE Vernova (gecareers.com)

• Our compensation & benefits are designed to reward high performers and help you manage your personal and family needs. We offer a robust benefits package depending on your employment status and your national requirements.
• A healthy, balanced lifestyle can mean different things to different people. We've created programs that support the way you live and work today.
• GE Vernova invests to provide opportunities to grow your career by providing a path for continued on-the-job learning and development.

Inclusion & Diversity

At GE Vernova, we believe in the value of your unique identity, background and experiences. We are committed to fostering an inclusive culture, where everyone feels empowered to do their best work because they feel accepted, respected and that they belong.  Click here to learn more: https://jobs.gecareers.com/vernova/global/en/i-d-e

GE Vernova’s Gas Power business engineers advanced, efficient natural gas-powered technologies and services, along with decarbonization solutions that aim to help electrify a lower carbon future. It is a global leader in gas turbines and power plant technologies and services with the industry’s largest installed base.

jobs.title: Sr FA Engineer
jobs.description:
At Jabil (NYSE: JBL), we are proud to be a trusted partner for the world's top brands, offering comprehensive engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. With 60 years of experience across industries and a vast network of over 100 sites worldwide, Jabil combines global reach with local expertise to deliver both scalable and customized solutions. Our commitment extends beyond business success as we strive to build sustainable processes that minimize environmental impact and foster vibrant and diverse communities around the globe.

JOB SUMMARY

Direct Failure Analysis Engineers in operating within area of assigned responsibilities with a high level of efficiency, integrity and enthusiasm, striving to achieve excellence in all endeavors.  Responsible for investigating and reducing component failures at electrical test through prompt, aggressive root cause analysis and effective corrective actions.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

TECHNICAL MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES
·         Improve component quality of non-conforming products by establishing failure analysis and obtaining corrective action from suppliers.
·         Interact with various departments (Quality, Purchasing, Manufacturing) to resolve/improve component issues.
·         Monitor components reject levels and respond to issues accordingly.
·         Report technical information concerning component failures to various team members and customer.
·         Reclaim revenue of rejected components via return of defective product.
·         Implement proactive measures that will foster productivity and higher product yields while reducing economic loss.
·         Respond to production line part problems immediately and address boards on component hold.
·         Monitor the storage of moisture sensitive components in dry pack and nitrogen cases; shock sensitive devices.
·         Follow ESD procedures at all times.
·         Speak with customer engineering personnel in a professional and effective manner.
·         Adhere to all safety and health rules and regulations associated with this position and as directed by supervisor.
·         Comply and follow all procedures within the company security policy.

LEADERSHIP AND MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES (if applicable)
Recruitment and Retention:
·         Recruit and interview Failure Analysis Engineers and Technicians.
·         Communicate criteria to recruiters for Failure Analysis Engineer and Technician position candidates.
·         Coach Failure Analysis Engineers in the interviewing/hiring process.
·         Monitor team member turnover; identify key factors that can be improved; make improvements.

Employee and Team Development:
·         Identify individual and team strengths and development needs on an ongoing basis.
·         Create and/or validate training curriculum in area of responsibility.
·         Coach and mentor Failure Analysis Engineering staff to deliver excellence to every internal and external customer.

Performance Management:
·         Establish clear measurable goals and objectives by which to determine individual and team results (i.e. operational metrics, results against project timelines, training documentation, attendance records, knowledge of operational roles and responsibilities, personal development goals).
·         Solicit ongoing feedback from Test Engineering Manager, Workcell Manager (WCM), Business Unit Manager (BUM), peers and team member on team member’s contribution to the Workcell team.  Provide ongoing coaching and counseling to team member based on feedback.
·         Express pride in staff and encourage them to feel good about their accomplishments.
·         Perform team member evaluations professionally and on time.

Your Impact at Lowe's

As a Customer Service Associate, you combine top-notch customer service skills with genuine care for people to help customers feel comfortable while shopping at Lowe's. This is an excellent role for those who want to engage with customers and help them solve their home improvement challenges.

How We Support You

Whether you need a part-time position or a place to plant yourself and grow, Lowe's is ready to support your goals. As a Lowe's associate, you'll gain access to many benefits beyond competitive pay and flexible schedules.

• Make your well-being a priority with multiple top-tier health insurance options.
• Explore educational opportunities with Lowe's tuition assistance program.
• Take charge of your financial future with a company-matching 401(k) and optional Employee Stock Purchase Program.
• Gain extra savings with a 10% Associate Discount.
• Learn new trade skills with our Track to the Trades program.

For information about our benefit programs and eligibility, please visit https://talent.lowes.com/us/en/benefits.

Your Day at Lowe's

As a Customer Service Associate, you will welcome customers to Lowe's and help them find the right products and services for their home improvement needs. You will interact with customers throughout the day, help them find and select products, occasionally load merchandise, and ensure all customer needs are met.

While you will spend most of your time listening to customers, answering questions, and organizing merchandise, your daily responsibilities may vary by department.

Customer Service Associates work in one of the following departments, based on hiring needs and skillsets: Appliances, Cabinets, Flooring, Live Nursery, Inside Garden, Hardware, Tools, Millwork, Building Materials, Plumbing, Electrical, Paint, Home Décor, Tool Rental, or Pro Services.

Key Responsibilities

• Welcome customers to Lowe's, answer questions, and deliver friendly and professional customer service.
• Assist customers with locating and handling merchandise
• Down stock merchandise by looking for empty areas on shelves and replenishing supplies
• Process orders and deliveries accurately so customers receive merchandise as expected and on time
• Cross-functionally train in other areas of the store to help deliver the best customer service
• Prepare merchandise in your department based on customer needs (e.g., tint and mix paint, cut and thread pipe, cut and bundle wood, cut drywall, cut blinds)
• Guide customers through shopping or checkout
• Complete other duties as assigned

Minimum Qualifications

• 6 Months Experience using a computer, including inputting, accessing, modifying, or outputting information
• 6 Months Experience using common retail technology, such as smart phones and tablets
• Reading, writing, and performing basic arithmetic (addition and subtraction)
• Able to perform duties that may require prolonged standing, sitting, and other activities necessary to perform job duties
• Minimally lift 25lbs unassisted or over 25lbs with or without an accommodation

Preferred Qualifications

• 6 months of Retail and/or customer service experience
• Bi-lingual skills
• Certification in trade related to department (e.g., hardware, kitchen, plumbing, electrical, lawn and garden, and lumber/building materials)

Lowe's commitment to growth and teamwork extends to the community as well. To better equip our stores and serve our communities, we strongly encourage bilingual, military, and veteran talent to apply and join our team.

Travel Requirements

This role does not require regular travel; however, this role may need to travel occasionally to meetings, training, or to support neighboring stores.

Working Conditions

Environmental factors vary by location. You may be working in both inside and outside weather conditions. Exposure to varying climates, including extreme heat or cold, wet, damp, humid, windy, or drafty conditions, is possible. You may be exposed to constant or intermittent noises in addition to moving or shaking objects and equipment.

Lifting methods vary based on role, weight, and volume. Associates must follow guidelines, limiting single lifts to 75 pounds. Team lifts are used minimally starting at 75 pounds or when needed. Powered equipment should be used as required, with proper training or assistance from a trained coworker.

As a Receiver/Stocker, you help keep the store clean, safe, and ready for customers by accurately receiving freight, stocking shelves, and organizing merchandise and top stock. You’ll unload deliveries, handle equipment and hazardous materials safely, and make sure your area is prepped for daily success.

This role is physical and fast-paced, requiring safe lifting practices and attention to detail. You’ll spend most of your shift on your feet, working mornings, afternoons, evenings, or overnight depending on store needs. And when a customer or teammate needs help, you’ll be there with a friendly, professional attitude.

Key Responsibilities

• Provides SMART customer service at all times through the daily execution of Lowe's customer service policies, procedures and programs

• Seeks out customers to understand his/her needs and assists in locating, demonstrating, selecting, carrying, and/or loading merchandise

• Listens to and responds knowledgeably and promptly to customer and employee questions by taking them to areas of the store and walking them through projects when necessary

• Communicates information to customers regarding all stock, special order merchandise, feature benefits, application, and warranty information related to Lowe’s programs

• Coaches, develops, provides feedback, and trains associates in the various departmental duties or sales opportunities (CSA Front End Team)

• Uses a cash register to process sales transactions, returns, and refunds according to company guidelines

• Provides proper monetary change to CSA Front End associates for register activities

• Removes security tags, verifies product information, and bags merchandise for customers

• Assists in line vesting to help turn around time for checkout, opening additional registers when necessary to ensure enough coverage

• Prepares register area at the beginning and end of shift by confirming functionality of registers and scanners and stocking register supplies

• Inspects returned merchandise for damages

• Enters and submits customer orders, prints order tickets, verifies receipts, and signs off on loading tickets

• Looks up product information and competitor prices for products to verify price match

• Records all items that are used in the store on the store use lists

• Completes cash counting and daily reconciliation duties as assigned

• Monitors cash in drawer and cash recycler levels to ensure they do not exceed limit requirements

• Monitors merchandise entering and leaving the store entrances and exits and assists customers or associates who trigger the alarm

• Detects common signs of shoplifting, theft, and other security risks, and promptly communicates them to management and/or Asset Protection

• Ensures compliance with housekeeping standards and programs (e.g., Zone Recovery) to maintain cleanliness and organization of store and working areas

• Maintains a safe and secure work environment, which may include conducting daily safety reviews, noting hazards, keeping aisles clear, and securing doors and gates

• Adheres to all safety requirements relevant to one’s regular job duties: top stock safety, reinstalling safety cables, use of aisle blockers, a tether line on power equipment, spotters, and safety devices

• Operates store equipment as needed depending on one specific role and department (e.g., Zebra phone, telephone, paging system, cash recycler, copiers, fax machines, computers, CCTV surveillance system, key cutter, panel saw, paint mixer, flooring cutters, compacter baler)

• In addition to the above responsibilities, this individual is held accountable for other duties as assigned

Required Qualifications

• High school diploma or GED or equivalent years of experience in lieu of education requirement, if applicable
• Less than 1 Year Experience using a computer, including inputting, accessing, modifying, or outputting information

• Less than 1 Year Experience using common retail technology, such as smart phones and tablets

• 1 Year Retail experience as a cashier
• Ability to obtain sales related licensure or registration as may be required by law

Preferred Qualifications

• 1 Year Experience identifying and selling products based on customer needs, including credit cards, installations, add-on sales, protection plans, and explaining warranties, product features, and benefits

• 1 Year Experience as a head cashier

• Less than 1 Year Experience working in any department at a Lowe's retail store

• 1 Year Supervisory experience in any field, including directing, delegating, evaluating, training, and coaching employees

• Less than 1 Year Retail experience detecting common signs of shoplifting (e.g., merchandise hidden inside of containers, merchandise under carts, price labels switched)

Job title: Graduate Procurement Specialist

Location: Burgess Hill, Sussex, UK

Length of programme: 2 years (September 2027 - August 2029)

Finance & Operations Early Careers: Graduate Procurement Specialist opportunity

Our Early in Career Development Programme accelerates your growth to directly impact patients' lives. Start your career with a UK market leader in biotechnology, recognised as the #1 Best Big Company to Work For (2021) and dedicated to equity, diversity, and inclusion.

Job Purpose

At Roche Diagnostics, our mission is to improve patients’ lives through innovative diagnostic solutions. Procurement supports this mission by securing the suppliers, products and services needed by our business, colleagues and customers.

A rare opportunity has been made available in the procurement function in the UK &  Ireland team. The role is based in the Finance & Operations Directorate. The function ensures organisational efficiency and excellence through robust supply frameworks, optimised sourcing, and aligned strategic planning, foresight and execution.

As a Graduate Procurement Specialist, you will join a collaborative team and gain practical experience across strategic sourcing, supply chain resilience,  supplier management, commercial analysis, compliance and continuous improvement. Working with experienced professionals and stakeholders across Roche you will apply your commercially savvy mindset with academic knowledge while developing a career in procurement and supply chain management.

We are looking for someone commercially inclined with a keen eye for detail, curious, motivated and eager to learn who wants to develop as a procurement professional.

The role is a paid, full-time graduate role of two years’ duration, based in Burgess Hill, West Sussex with hybrid working with 3 days in office.

The Opportunity

You will gain exposure to the full procurement lifecycle, including:

• Support tenders, quotation analysis and commercial evaluations to secure value while maintaining quality, service and compliance.
• Monitor performance, maintain relationships and identify opportunities to improve service, resilience and value.
• Analyse procurement and supplier data to identify trends, risks, savings opportunities and actionable insights.
• Work with Finance, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain and other teams to understand requirements and support effective decisions.
• Assist with contract administration, purchasing compliance and adherence to Roche policies and relevant regulations.
• Help simplify processes, improve ways of working and use digital tools and data more effectively.
• Contribute to responsible sourcing, supplier sustainability and Roche’s environmental and social ambitions.
• Support procurement projects from requirements gathering through implementation, tracking progress and benefits.
• Support exploration of AI and automation opportunities within Procurement processes, including assessing the overall AI/automation landscape as well as the feasibility of AI/automation solutions.

As you develop, you will take greater ownership, contribute ideas and build confidence in making evidence-based commercial recommendations.

Why a Procurement programme at Roche?

Join a world-leading  innovative organisation. Experience a science-led international environment that values collaboration, learning and new ideas.

Grow your career. Grow in Global or affiliate procurement roles. Contribute to meaningful business challenges and build skills for a long-term career in procurement, supply chain or commercial management.

Build a strong commercial foundation. Develop experience across sourcing, supplier management, commercial analysis, contracts and procurement operations.

Turn data into value. Learn how procurement insights can improve decisions, manage risk, enhance performance and deliver sustainable value.

Who You Are

Essential Skills & Experience

We are seeking a graduate with initiative and an interest in how procurement creates value for businesses and customers.

Essential requirements

• A degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business, Finance, Economics, STEM or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant academic experience.
• Strong analytical and numerical skills, with the ability to interpret information and draw logical conclusions.
• Effective communication and interpersonal skills, including confidence engaging with colleagues and suppliers.
• Strong organisation, attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities.
• A proactive, problem-solving approach and willingness to ask questions, challenge constructively and suggest improvements.
• A collaborative, accountable and ethical approach to working with others and following policies.
• Confidence using Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint, or willingness to develop these skills.
• Genuine interest in procurement, commercial management, negotiations, sourcing, supplier relationships and healthcare or diagnostics.

What will help you succeed?

Extensive procurement experience is not required. We value enthusiasm, curiosity and willingness to learn alongside technical knowledge.

• Strong interest in commercial processes, compliance, problem-solving, or data governance within a regulated environment
• Experience or knowledge within automation / AI, metrics, dashboards, and performance frameworks (e.g., OKRs, KPIs)
• Comfortable with a continuous improvement mindset and challenging the “why” with a willingness to take ownership of tasks
• Comfortable working with ambiguity and eager to learn in a fast-paced environment
• Strong written and verbal communication skills

• Experience creating presentations or working with data in PowerBI, Appsheets, Tableau or similar tools

You will thrive if you enjoy working with data, solving problems, understanding business operations and turning ideas into practical initiatives. Above all, you should be motivated to develop, take ownership and contribute to a shared purpose.

Application process:

Stage 1: Submit your CV and cover letter

• Our focus is to understand why you have applied for this role and what you will bring to the role to ensure team and personal success.
• Applications close on Friday, 16 October 2026. The application process may be extended beyond this date but could close at any point after this time.

Stage 2: Recorded video interview

• You will take part in a recorded video interview, where you wil be presented with questions and record your answer to support your application
• Estimated date: November 2026

Stage 3: In person assessment centre

• You will take part in our full day in person assessment centre at our Roche offices in Burgess Hill, Sussex. Further details will be provided if successful.
• Expected date: w/c 07 December 2026. The exact date will be provided if successful.

Please note: Unfortunately, visa sponsorship is not available for this role. Candidates must already hold a valid authorisation to work in the UK.

Ready to apply? Go ahead and join us, we are waiting for you!

Who we are

A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.

Let’s build a healthier future, together.

jobs.title: Director, Pharmacokinetics
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Pharmacokinetics, Dynamics, Metabolism and Bioanalytics (PDMB) function of our Research & Development Division, is seeking a dynamic and collaborative individual to lead a team of scientists in the Drug Metabolism and Pharmacokinetics (DMPK) group in West Point, Pennsylvania.  The team primarily supports discovery programs across modalities (small molecules and conjugates) and therapeutic areas, enabling strategic decisions from lead selection through FIH.  As Director in the West Point DMPK group, your main responsibility is leading a motivated team of experienced Scientists representing the department in cross-functional teams as well as a group of bench scientists, charged with conducting mechanistic ADME studies. The position requires a focus on talent development as well as scientific creativity.

The DMPK director must be able to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment, drive innovation, and have excellent scientific, interpersonal and communication skills in order to guide the team on the design, implementation and interpretation of in silico, in vitro and in vivo studies necessary to influence decisions in drug discovery and development.

The ideal candidate will have an in-depth understanding of ADME, as well as pharmacokinetic and PK/PD principles that impact the discovery and development of new chemical entities. Experience with small molecules drug discovery is expected and additional experience with various drug modalities across therapeutic areas is desired. The candidate should be familiar with PK, PK/PD and PBPK modeling as tools to drive decision making.

We are highly engaged in influencing the success of a large and exciting portfolio and continue to evolve the influence of new computational and laboratory techniques towards the selection of differentiated products.  This role provides a unique opportunity to influence our evolving pipeline while enabling the growth of the next generation of leaders.

Education Minimum Requirement:

• PhD. in chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Pharmacology, Biomedical Engineering, Biochemistry, or related field with 8+ years of experience supporting drug discovery in the Pharmaceutical Industry.
• Applicants with MSci. degree with 12+ years relevant industry experience will be considered.

Required Experience and Skills:

• Experienced in providing DMPK support in drug discovery programs, including assessment of tractability, dose and PK predictions, drug metabolism, assessment of drug interaction risk and communicating analyses and recommendations to interdisciplinary teams and management.
• Experienced in integrating preclinical ADME, PK, and pharmacology data to enable translational PK/PD modeling and simulation to support dose selection, design of PK/PD and safety assessment studies, and dose justifications for preclinical and clinical studies
• Knowledge of cutting-edge in silico approaches to inform decision making related to the characterization of metabolism, drug interactions, exposure-response relationships and variability.
• Knowledge of modern instrumentation in support of DMPK workflows.
• Strong leadership, interpersonal, communication, problem solving, and collaboration skills along with strength in delivering results on firm deadlines.
• At least 3 years’ experience with management or supervision of staff.
• A strong aptitude for and previous experience in managing scientific teams and attracting, developing, and retaining talent.
• Excellent verbal and written communications skills and an ability to excel in a team-based environment.

Preferred Experience and Skills:

• Experience with authoring documents in support of regulatory filings, including IBs, INDs and CTDs as well as responses to regulatory questions.
• Experience with evaluation of third-party assets.
• Strong publication track record in ADME science and/or the Drug Discovery and Development field.

Primary Responsibilities:

• Providing strategic, scientific, and operational leadership for a group of scientists responsible for support, through experimentation and project representation on discovery teams.
• Actively working with staff to encourage and facilitate their career development.
• Collaborating with internal stakeholders to ensure the timely delivery of quality data and documentation.
• Collaborating with members of the DMPK organization and PDMB at large to support the advancement of scientific and strategic initiatives.
• Setting future strategy and facilitating/implementing new technologies in the organization
• Providing scientific oversight of programs supported by staff in the group and thorough and timely review of internal and external documents prepared by team members.

Required Skills:

ADME, ADME, Bioanalysis, Bioanalytical Assays, Clinical Pharmacology, Cross-Cultural Awareness, Dosing, Drug Development, Drug Discovery Research, Drug Metabolism, Drug Research, Immunoassays, Innovation, Investigational New Drug, In Vitro Research, In Vivo Studies, Mentoring Staff, Modeling Simulations, Pharmaceutical Analysis, Pharmaceutical Industry, Pharmaceutical Research, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Pharmacodynamics, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacology {+ 8 more}

jobs.description:
Blackstone is the world’s largest alternative asset manager. Blackstone seeks to deliver compelling returns for institutional and individual investors by strengthening the companies in which the firm invests. Blackstone’s over $1.3 trillion in assets under management include global investment strategies focused on real estate, private equity, credit, infrastructure, life sciences, growth equity, secondaries and hedge funds. Further information is available at www.blackstone.com. Follow @blackstone on LinkedIn, X (Twitter), and Instagram.

Business Unit Overview:

Blackstone is a global leader in real estate investing. Blackstone’s real estate business was founded in 1991 and has US $314 billion of investor capital under management. Blackstone is the largest owner of commercial real estate globally, owning and operating assets across every major geography and sector, including logistics, data centers, residential, office and hospitality. Our opportunistic funds seek to acquire undermanaged, well-located assets across the world. Blackstone’s Core+ business invests in substantially stabilized real estate assets globally, through both institutional strategies and strategies tailored for income-focused individual investors including Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust, Inc. (BREIT). Blackstone Real Estate also operates one of the leading global real estate debt businesses, providing comprehensive financing solutions across the capital structure and risk spectrum, including management of Blackstone Mortgage Trust (NYSE: BXMT).

Job Title: Associate

Job Description:

This professional will be responsible for strategic support of the valuations effort and its related functions globally across Blackstone’s opportunistic and core+ strategies. The Associate will play a key role in Blackstone Real Estate’s valuations effort. This will involve a) coordination of the execution and outcomes of U.S. valuations, b) consolidation and analysis of global valuations outcomes, and c) execution of summary valuation-related materials and analysis. The role will involve partnership in coordinating key internal and external processes, consolidating and analyzing outcomes and metrics as well as delivering supporting documentation and materials to internal and external stakeholders. This professional will work closely with members asset management, finance, fund-specific and portfolio company teams to execute and enhance the overall valuation process and deliverables globally.

Responsibilities:

• Product and Investment Knowledge: Become proficient in Blackstone Real Estate’s global funds and investments, with particular focus on valuation practices.

• Valuation Outcomes and Assumptions: Work collaboratively across teams and vehicles to analyze and present valuation outcomes produced from a discounted cash flow approach by property, investment, market and/or sector, globally, to drive thematic monthly or quarterly valuation results.

• Valuations Process: Partner with asset management, finance and portfolio companies to coordinate and deliver monthly and / or quarterly internal valuations. Assist with the proper closure of key third-party processes, including appraisal, independent valuation advisor and audit.

• Internal Reporting: Oversee and execute quarterly valuation materials and supporting analysis to present results, requiring the aggregation and synthesis of large sets of data both internally and externally.
• Special Projects: Support global special projects relating to valuation strategies and process, new products, appraisals and third-party service providers.

Qualifications:

• 2+ years; Strong technical background in valuations-related role (preferably in execution of DCF valuations)
• Experience executing files and presentations in fast moving and dynamic environment

• Inquisitive /critical thinker

• Collaborative approach, with confidence engaging directly with Asset Management and other stakeholders on behalf of the Valuations team to drive outcomes
• Strong organizational skills, with sound judgment in managing competing priorities
• Can take notes and distill to senior leaders in crisp and clear format
• Team player, excellent interpersonal skill

jobs.title: Director, Business Strategy - Electrical Design & Execution
jobs.description:
Position Summary...

What you'll do...

The Director, Electrical Engineering and Design is responsible for providing strategic leadership and technical oversight for electrical engineering and lighting design across Walmart, Sam’s Club, and Supply Chain facilities. This role leads the development and implementation of enterprise engineering standards, design strategies, and technical requirements supporting new construction, remodels, renovations, and existing facility infrastructure.

The Director leads a team of engineering professionals and provides strategic oversight of an external engineering collective responsible for supporting electrical engineering and design activities across the enterprise. This position ensures that engineering solutions are safe, reliable, cost-effective, constructible, maintainable, and aligned with operational and long-term business objectives.

This role requires a strong combination of technical expertise, organizational leadership, strategic planning, engineering design oversight, external partner management, and cross-functional collaboration.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Electrical Engineering and Design Leadership

• Establish and lead the enterprise strategy for electrical engineering and design across Walmart, Sam’s Club, and Supply Chain facilities.
• Provide technical leadership and oversight for electrical infrastructure and system design, including utility services, electrical distribution, emergency and standby power, lighting, lighting controls, and related facility electrical systems.
• Develop and maintain engineering design requirements that balance safety, reliability, constructability, operational performance, maintainability, and total cost of ownership.
• Ensure electrical engineering and design solutions support business objectives, operational requirements, and long-term facility infrastructure strategies.
• Provide strategic direction and technical guidance for complex engineering challenges impacting new construction, remodels, renovations, and existing facilities.
• Identify opportunities to improve engineering efficiency, design consistency, system performance, and overall project execution.

Electrical and Lighting Design Standards

• Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of enterprise electrical engineering and lighting design standards, specifications, and technical requirements.
• Establish consistent design approaches that support construction efficiency, operational reliability, energy performance, and lifecycle cost optimization.
• Provide technical oversight for interior and exterior lighting design, ensuring alignment with safety, customer and associate experience, operational needs, and energy efficiency objectives.
• Evaluate emerging electrical and lighting technologies, equipment, and design practices for potential enterprise implementation.
• Establish processes for reviewing and approving engineering design deviations, alternative solutions, and significant technical decisions.
• Ensure engineering standards and design practices align with applicable codes, regulations, industry standards, and company requirements.
• Incorporate field performance, lessons learned, and stakeholder feedback into ongoing improvements to engineering standards and design practices.

Engineering Team Leadership and Development

• Lead, develop, and mentor a team of electrical engineering professionals responsible for enterprise engineering standards, technical oversight, and design support.
• Establish clear team priorities, performance expectations, and accountability aligned with organizational objectives.
• Develop engineering talent and technical capabilities through coaching, mentoring, professional development, and knowledge sharing.
• Foster a culture of technical excellence, innovation, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
• Ensure effective allocation of internal engineering resources to support strategic initiatives, technical reviews, and project requirements.
• Build organizational capabilities that support evolving business needs, emerging technologies, and long-term engineering strategies.

External Engineering Collective Oversight

• Provide strategic leadership and oversight of the external engineering collective supporting electrical engineering and design activities across the enterprise.
• Establish clear technical expectations, design deliverables, roles, responsibilities, and performance requirements for external engineering partners.
• Develop and maintain an effective operating model between internal engineering teams and the external engineering collective to support consistent, scalable, and efficient design execution.
• Establish engineering review, quality assurance, and technical governance processes to ensure designs meet enterprise standards and project requirements.
• Monitor engineering collective performance against established expectations for design quality, schedule, responsiveness, cost, and technical accuracy.
• Lead collaboration and issue resolution between external engineering partners and internal stakeholders to address design challenges and improve execution.
• Partner with sourcing, procurement, and other business teams to support engineering services strategy, resource planning, and partner performance management.
• Drive continuous improvement in engineering processes, design coordination, and overall collective performance.

Engineering Design and Project Oversight

• Provide technical and strategic oversight for electrical engineering and lighting design supporting enterprise capital projects and facility initiatives.
• Partner with Architecture, Construction, Project Management, Facilities, and Operations teams to ensure electrical and lighting designs are coordinated with broader project requirements.
• Establish design review processes appropriate to project complexity, technical risk, and business impact.
• Support resolution of complex engineering issues, design conflicts, and field conditions requiring enterprise-level technical guidance.
• Identify recurring design and construction challenges and implement systemic improvements to engineering standards, processes, and execution.
• Ensure engineering decisions consider project cost, schedule, constructability, operational impact, and long-term maintenance requirements.
• Drive accountability for engineering quality and consistency across internal teams and external design partners.

Strategic Planning, Innovation, and Continuous Improvement

• Develop long-term engineering strategies that support evolving facility needs, business priorities, and infrastructure requirements.
• Identify and evaluate opportunities to improve electrical system reliability, energy efficiency, operational performance, and lifecycle cost.
• Lead the evaluation of new electrical and lighting technologies and develop recommendations for enterprise adoption.
• Leverage project performance, operational feedback, and engineering data to identify trends and opportunities for improvement.
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support strategic initiatives involving electrical infrastructure, energy management, resiliency, and facility modernization.

jobs.description:
Position Summary...

What you'll do...

Fulfillment Experience builds the capabilities and operating mechanisms that make Walmart a reliable, convenient on-demand partner. Our teams determine what customers can buy, the promise and fulfillment choices they see, how orders are managed and recovered, and how the network performs at scale. We partner across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Finance, Merchandising, Store Operations, Fulfillment Centers, Last Mile, Transportation, and Strategy to improve customer outcomes while balancing speed, assortment, cost, and operational feasibility.

Role summary

The (USA) Manager, Technology Operations identifies and solves complex, high-impact fulfillment problems across a defined product, operational, or customer-experience area. This role turns ambiguous customer, operational, and financial signals into a clear diagnosis, an aligned plan, and measurable results. Working across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Finance, and operations partners, the Manager leads initiatives from discovery and analysis through decision, delivery, readiness, and impact measurement. Success requires structured problem solving, clear communication, sound business judgment, and the ability to influence without direct authority.

What you'll do

• Own a complex problem space or initiative that improves customer experience, fulfillment performance, or financial outcomes.

• Use customer, operational, and financial data to identify opportunities, quantify impact, isolate root causes, and define success measures.

• Translate ambiguous problems into clear problem statements, hypotheses, options, and data-driven recommendations.

• Lead cross-functional solution design and execution with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Finance, Store Operations, Fulfillment Centers, Last Mile, Transportation, and other partners.

• Build and manage end-to-end plans that make ownership, milestones, dependencies, risks, decision points, pilots, launch readiness, and success measures clear.

• Drive alignment and resolve trade-offs without direct authority; escalate issues with a clear recommendation when timely leadership decisions are needed.

• Create concise, executive-ready updates and decision materials that clarify what changed, why it matters, and the action required.

• Measure results after launch, identify gaps or unintended outcomes, and drive refinements, scaling, or corrective action.

• Improve the team's planning, visibility, and execution through better processes, tools, automation, and operating routines.

• Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives in eCommerce, supply chain, operations, product, strategy, analytics, or another fast-paced, data-rich environment.

• Strong structured problem-solving skills, including the ability to turn ambiguous issues into clear questions, synthesize disparate inputs, identify root causes, and recommend a practical path forward.

• Strong analytical fluency and comfort using data to form hypotheses, assess trade-offs, define metrics, and measure impact.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to make complex work understandable and action-oriented for audiences at every level.

• Proven ability to influence without authority, build trust across functions, navigate competing priorities, and drive commitments to closure.

• Disciplined program-management skills, including planning, milestone management, dependency and risk management, and launch or change readiness.

• Sound customer, operational, and financial judgment; able to balance the ideal solution with what is practical to execute at scale.

• Experience in omnichannel retail, eCommerce, fulfillment, supply chain, marketplaces, or a similarly complex operating environment.

• Working knowledge of SQL, BI and visualization tools, Jira, Airtable, or process-automation tools.

jobs.title: (USA) Operations Manager, Fleet Safety
jobs.description:
Position Summary...

What you'll do...

Are you ready to use your innovative mindset to help create a world-class experience for customers for the World’s Largest Retailer? The Operations Manager, Fleet Safety, is a crucial role that thinks strategically while leading, motivating, and developing a team aimed at delivering world-class safety and operations.

About Walmart Transportation:

Our team is crucial in ensuring the safe and efficient movement of goods across the country. In this role, you will play an integral part in our company’s success by ensuring the safe operations of our private fleet, allowing them to deliver essential goods to our customers in a safe and timely manner.

What You’ll Do:

• You will be responsible for identifying potential risks and conducting training sessions to educate drivers on safe operation practices.

• You will supervise the team, ensuring that each member follows safety protocols and holds themselves accountable.

• In the event of an accident or injury, you will handle the reporting and investigative processes, ensuring thorough analysis and prompt action.

• You must be familiar and stay up to date with OSHA regulations and reporting criteria, always maintaining compliance to create a safe and healthy work environment for everyone.

What You’ll Bring:

• You possess knowledge of laws, regulations, and safety rules regarding materials transportation, including DOT, FMCSA, PHMSA, CVSA, and state regulations.

• You have a solid working knowledge of vehicle maintenance, HazMat bill of ladings, safety, and transportation paperwork.

• You’re a team player who can effectively communicate with customers, suppliers, and associates regarding safe operations of Walmart Tractors/Trailers.

• You can drive and implement business plans to achieve production, quality, and safety goals.

• You can forecast staffing, workload, and safety performance results to meet business demands.

• You can monitor and manage productivity by preparing, reviewing, and analyzing business reports.

• You ensure compliance with Logistics and company quality and safety standards, policies, procedures, and directives by developing, distributing, and maintaining procedures and supporting documentation.

• You can identify and ensure associate, customer, and supplier concerns are resolved using your judgment or consulting others when needed.

• You can supervise and manage associates and leaders in your area by giving direction, monitoring safety performance, providing feedback, and identifying training and development needs.

The above information has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed in the role. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job. The full Job Description can be made available as part of the hiring process.

Benefits & Perks:

2 years’ experience in continuous improvement methodologies (for example, Total Productive Maintenance (TPM)) within supply chain or transportation maintenance environments.

jobs.title: 12hr Night Shift Packaging Machine Operator
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Job Description

Job Description

Job Title: Machine Operator - Night Shift

Location: Topeka, KS (Mars Petcare)

Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent

---

Mars is looking to hire a highly motivated Machine Operator for our state-of-the-art manufacturing plant in Topeka, Kansas.

Whether you are an experienced manufacturing professional, someone looking to transition into a technical field, or a military Veteran transitioning to the civilian workforce, Mars offers the structured training, tools, and supportive team environment you need to build a long-term, rewarding career.

As a day shift Machine Operator, you will become a system expert in your assigned production area. You will be responsible for the safe, efficient operation of advanced equipment, ensuring our products meet the high standards our consumers and pets deserve.

---

What We Offer (Benefits & Perks)

· Health & Wellness: Comprehensive Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance starting on day one.

· Financial Security: Competitive base pay, annual performance-based bonus potential, and a highly competitive 401(k) company match.

· Work-Life Balance: Immediately eligible (based on hire date) for up to three weeks of paid vacation, 12 Paid Holidays per year, and Sick Pay.

· Family Support: Paid Maternity & Parental Leave, Short-Term & Long-Term Disability.

· Career Growth: Access to world-class technical training, clear pathways for promotion, and educational assistance.

---

Key Responsibilities

· Equipment Operation: Safely and efficiently operate food-safe machinery and production lines to meet daily operational targets.

· Problem Solving & Troubleshooting: Assess equipment operating reliability and perform routine technical repairs, adjustments, and root-cause troubleshooting.

· Preventative Maintenance: Perform routine maintenance tasks and partner with the specialized Maintenance team on complex equipment upkeep.

· Quality Assurance: Execute critical food safety and quality checks (e.g., metal detection, inspecting date codes, monitoring dump logs) and maintain a high level of product ownership.

· Detailed Record Keeping: Keep highly accurate logs and digital shift support documentation using basic desktop and production tracking computer systems.

· Material Handling: Safely operate a forklift to manage material flow and inventory control principles in your production area.

---

What You’ll Bring (Qualifications)

Minimum Qualifications:

· Education: High School diploma, GED, or equivalent civilian/military education.

· Physical Capability: Ability to stand on concrete floors for extended periods, bend, stoop, twist, turn, reach, climb stairs, and lift up to 50 lbs.

· Safety Mindset: Willingness to wear proper Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) including hair net, bump cap, ear plugs, safety shoes, and uniform.

· Certifications: Ability to obtain and maintain OSHA forklift certification (Mars will provide full on-site training and licensing).

Preferred Qualifications:

· Experience: 1+ years of manufacturing experience operating industrial machinery OR equivalent technical military experience (such as equipment maintenance, operations, or mechanical repairs).

· Technical Skills: Basic understanding of inventory control systems or experience utilizing enterprise asset management systems (e.g., SAP, GCSS, or equivalent databases).

---

Military & Veteran Technical Equivalency Guide

At Mars, we highly value your military service. If you served in any of the following fields (or a related occupational specialty), your military training maps directly to the technical, safety, and leadership demands of this role:

· U.S. Army: Allied Trade Specialist (91E), Wheeled Vehicle Repairer (91B), Motor Transport Operator (88M), Unit Supply Specialist (92Y), Horizontal Construction Engineer (12N).

· U.S. Navy: Machinist's Mate (MM), Machinery Repairman (MR), Engineman (EN), Equipment Operator (EO), Logistics Specialist (LS).

· U.S. Air Force: Aerospace Propulsion Specialist (2A6X1), Aircraft Metals Technology (2A7X1), Materiel Management (2S0X1), Pavements & Construction Equipment (3E2X1).

· U.S. Marine Corps: Machinist (2161), Metal Worker (1316), Engineer Equipment Operator (1345), Supply Chain/Logistics Specialist (3043), Motor Vehicle Operator (3531).

· U.S. Coast Guard: Machinery Technician (MK), Damage Controlman (DC), Storekeeper (SK).

About Mars, Incorporated

Mars is a family-owned business with more than a century of history making diverse products and offering services for people and the pets people love. With almost $35 billion in sales, the company is a global business that produces some of the world’s best-loved brands: M&M’s®, SNICKERS®, TWIX®, MILKY WAY®, DOVE®, PEDIGREE®, ROYAL CANIN®, WHISKAS®, EXTRA®, ORBIT®, 5™, SKITTLES®, UNCLE BEN’S®, and COCOAVIA®. Mars also provides veterinary health services that include BANFIELD® Pet Hospitals, Blue Pearl®, VCA® and Pet Partners™.

The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency, and Freedom – inspire our more than 100,000 Associates to create value for all its partners and deliver growth they are proud of every day.

jobs.title: Sr. Accountant
jobs.description:
The Senior Accountant is responsible for supporting and overseeing key accounting operations, including Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, customer billing, cash application, vendor and customer setup, and related accounting activities. This position works closely with internal accounting teams, business operations, customers, and other Eurofins entities to ensure transactions are processed accurately, timely, and in accordance with company policies.

The Senior Accountant also provides day-to-day supervision and guidance to two Staff Accountants supporting AR billing and collections and plays an important role in maintaining accurate customer balances, resolving payment issues, and improving the overall efficiency of accounting processes.

Sr. Accountant Duties Include but are not Limited to the Following:

Accounts Payable & Vendor Management

• Manage and review AP invoices through the Coupa Accounts Payable system, ensuring invoices are processed accurately and timely.
• Create purchase requisitions and obtain appropriate Purchase Order (PO) numbers prior to invoice processing.
• Review invoices for proper supporting documentation, approvals, GL account coding, department/cost center coding, and PO information.
• Work closely with the NSC Accounts Payable team to ensure invoices are submitted, approved, and processed within required payment timelines.
• Research and resolve invoice discrepancies, coding issues, PO mismatches, and other AP-related exceptions.
• Coordinate the creation and maintenance of new vendors in Coupa, ensuring required vendor information and documentation are complete.

Customer Billing & Accounts Receivable

• Review customer billing requirements and prepare customer invoices as needed.
• Perform billing calculations and ensure invoices contain accurate pricing, customer information, accounting codes, and other required billing details.
• Review supporting documentation to ensure invoices are complete and accurate before submission to customers.
• Create and maintain new customer accounts and coordinate required customer onboarding documentation.
• Provide customers with company W-9 forms and approved banking/remittance information when required for customer vendor setup and payment processing.
• Work closely with the AR Billing Specialist to resolve billing issues and ensure invoices are issued accurately and timely.

Cash Application & AR Management

• Apply daily customer payments to open accounts receivable invoices and ensure payments are posted accurately.
• Review AR aging and unapplied cash reports regularly and investigate outstanding or unidentified balances.
• Research unapplied and misapplied payments and coordinate corrections to ensure customer accounts are properly stated.
• Work proactively to reduce aged receivable balances and unapplied cash.
• Assist the AR Collection Specialist with customer invoice questions, collection activities, payment research, and account reconciliation.
• Investigate payments that may have been sent to another Eurofins laboratory or bank account and coordinate intercompany transfers or other corrective actions to ensure funds are applied to the appropriate customer account.
• Assist in resolving customer disputes and discrepancies that may delay collection of outstanding balances.

Basic Minimum Education Requirements:

• Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

Basic Minimum Qualifications:

• Minimum of 3–5 years of progressive accounting experience, preferably including Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, billing, and general accounting.
• Experience with Coupa or similar procurement/AP systems preferred.
• Strong Microsoft Excel skills and ability to analyze accounting data and reconcile.
• Excellent attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, particularly in researching billing, payment, and account discrepancies.
• Ability to work effectively with customers, internal departments, centralized accounting teams, and other Eurofins entities.
• Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship.

Position is full-time working Monday - Friday 09:00am - 5:00 pm, and additional hours as needed. Candidates currently living within a commutable distance to Norwood, MA are encouraged to apply.

Excellent full-time benefits including:

• Comprehensive medical coverage, dental, and vision options
• Life and disability insurance
• 401(k) with company match
• Paid vacation and holidays
