jobs.title: Technical Deployment Specialist
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Industrial labor powers our world, and protecting the people who do that work is both a moral imperative and a business advantage. At Voxel, we're transforming workplace safety and operational efficiency with AI-driven computer vision that turns existing security cameras into a system for spotting hazards and high-risk activity before incidents happen.

Our site intelligence platform helps safety and operations leaders at Fortune 500 grocers, retailers, manufacturers, and logistics providers uncover root causes, reduce risk proactively, and make smarter, data-driven decisions. Based in San Francisco with team members around the globe, Voxel is backed by leading venture investors.

The Role

As a Technical Implementation Specialist, you'll be the hands-on owner of getting Voxel live at customer sites. Once a deal is signed, you take the deployment plan and make it real: connecting cameras, configuring our edge devices, working through network and security requirements with customer IT teams, and validating that everything performs as expected.

You'll partner closely with Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, and Engineering to deliver smooth, repeatable rollouts across single and multi-site environments. This role is critical to fast time-to-value for our customers and to scaling our deployment process as we grow.

What You'll Do

 - Execute end-to-end technical implementations, from kickoff and site readiness through go-live and handoff to Customer Success.

 - Configure and deploy Voxel's edge AI platform, including camera integration, device setup, and connectivity validation.

 - Work directly with customer IT, network, and security teams to complete network readiness checks, firewall and proxy configuration, and access requirements.

 - Produce technical documentation that helps customers secure internal IT and security approvals.

 - Troubleshoot deployment issues across networking, camera systems, and edge hardware, escalating toEngineering when needed.

 - Manage implementation timelines, track progress, and communicate status, risks, and next steps clearly to internal and customer stakeholders.

 - Coordinate onsite installations, including travel to customer sites for more complex deployments.

 - Contribute to and continuously improve implementation playbooks, checklists, and best practices so deployments get faster and more consistent.

 - Capture customer feedback and deployment friction and share it with Product and Engineering to improve the platform.

What We're Looking For

jobs.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

The Mechanical Engineering team at Form is focused on designing the battery cell, module, and full pack system that forms the foundation of our innovative utility-scale multi-day energy storage system.  We strive to deliver designs that are optimized for performance, quality, reliability, and cost for high-volume manufacturing at Form Factory.

 

We are seeking a  Staff Technical Program Manager to serve as a cornerstone of our mechanical design integration efforts. In this high-impact role, you will orchestrate the end-to-end execution of complex mechanical programs, bridging the gap between product architecture, detailed design, and high-volume manufacturing. You will be responsible for defining program strategy, proactively identifying and mitigating technical roadblocks, and fostering cross-functional alignment between engineering, operations, and supply chain teams. As a technical leader, you will champion the successful integration of first-of-a-kind systems, ensuring we meet our aggressive timelines while maintaining the highest standards of system reliability and design-for-cost optimization.  

 

Relocation assistance is available. 

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Lead cross-functional mechanical design projects from concept through high-volume manufacturing, ensuring alignment with product architecture and performance requirements.

 - Drive project schedules, identifying critical path risks and implementing mitigation strategies to keep programs on track.

 - Facilitate effective communication between engineering, operations, and supply chain teams to ensure design for cost and manufacturability (DFM) objectives are met.

 - Lead the coordination of first-of-a-kind build activities and system integration efforts, serving as the central point of contact for mechanical system implementation.

 - Manage prototyping efforts and support engineering teams in building and verifying analytical models to validate system designs.

 


WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - 6+ years of experience in technical program management, with a strong background in mechanical engineering or complex system development.

 - Proven track record of managing high-complexity engineering projects, particularly in hardware development or high-volume manufacturing environments.

 - Demonstrated experience navigating ambiguity and leading cross-functional teams to deliver integrated solutions on aggressive timelines.

 - Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret engineering data and guide decision-making on design trade-offs.

 - Excellent organizational and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders at all levels.

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field (Master’s or MBA preferred).

The Staff Product Manager, Fleet Management owns the product strategy and execution for the systems that keep Crusoe's GPU and CPU fleet running reliably and efficiently at scale. You'll define how Crusoe provisions, monitors, maintains, and optimizes its server fleet supporting AI training and inference workloads, translating operational requirements into scalable product capabilities. This covers the full lifecycle of compute: initial provisioning, firmware and configuration management, burn-in, multi-node testing, health monitoring, maintenance orchestration, repair, and decommissioning.



The role sits at the intersection of infrastructure operations, engineering, and customer experience. Fleet-level systems determine how much of our capacity is sellable, how fast we can bring new clusters online, and how quickly a customer's workload recovers when hardware fails. You'll be defining the problem space as much as solving it, and you should be comfortable operating in ambiguity, with support from senior leadership as the initiative takes shape.



You'll collaborate closely with hardware partners, engineering, infrastructure operations, networking, supply chain, finance, and customer success to ensure cohesive lifecycle management across Crusoe Cloud. As a Staff PM, you'll lead significant cross-functional initiatives, influence technical and product strategy across multiple teams, and be accountable for outcomes that directly impact company goals.



What You'll Be Working On:

 - Own the vision and product strategy for fleet management, including provisioning, burn-in, lifecycle management, health monitoring, maintenance orchestration, and performance optimization

 - Drive outcomes across the entire product lifecycle, from discovery through launch and iteration, for fleet management capabilities

 - Define product direction for systems managing large-scale GPU and CPU infrastructure, ensuring reliability, utilization, and operational efficiency

 - Lead cross-functional initiatives spanning engineering, infrastructure operations, networking, and customer success to deliver integrated fleet management solutions

 - Build consensus with tech leads and engineering managers on architecture decisions, tooling investments, and operational process improvements

 - Identify opportunities to improve fleet utilization, reduce operational overhead, and enhance observability through product innovation

 - Translate customer-facing reliability and performance impact, gathered through customer success, into product requirements

 - Mentor other product managers and engineers, sharing expertise in infrastructure operations and complex systems thinking



What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - 6+ years of product management experience delivering infrastructure or platform products, with demonstrated ownership of complex, cross-functional initiatives

 - Deep expertise in fleet management concepts including provisioning, lifecycle management, monitoring, and operations at scale

 - Strong understanding of distributed systems, server hardware, and infrastructure automation

 - Proven ability to solve ambiguous, novel problems requiring research, invention, and creative analysis

 - Experience driving product vision for complex systems with long-term strategic impact, balancing technical tradeoffs and operational requirements

 - Track record of building consensus across engineering, operations, and infrastructure teams on technical direction and investment priorities

 - Strong analytical skills interpreting operational metrics, performance data, and utilization patterns to guide product decisions

 - Excellent communication skills articulating technical concepts and connecting them to business outcomes

 - Experience mentoring colleagues in product management or technical roles

Bonus Points

 - Experience with large-scale GPU infrastructure or AI/ML platform operations

 - Familiarity with infrastructure automation tools, orchestration systems (Kubernetes, Slurm), or configuration management platforms

 - Experience with observability platforms, monitoring systems, or incident management workflows

Benefits:

jobs.title: Engineering Lead, Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)
jobs.description:
Who We Are & Why Join Us

Avathon is the leading Industrial AI autonomy platform, helping customers across heavy industries -- energy, mining, manufacturing, aerospace, defense, and logistics -- accelerate the journey toward autonomous operations. Our platform is built on a Computational Knowledge Graph foundation that contextualizes and connects operational data across siloed systems, bringing together time series, structured, unstructured, and machine vision data to power AI-driven applications in asset performance management, supply chain intelligence, visual AI, and global trade management. With capabilities spanning digital twins, normal behavior modeling, natural language processing, and computer vision, Avathon delivers real-time predictive intelligence and agentic decision-making at industrial scale.

Cutting-Edge AI Innovation -- Join a team at the forefront of AI, developing groundbreaking solutions that shape the future. High-Growth Environment -- Thrive in a fast-scaling startup where agility, collaboration, and rapid professional growth are the norm. Meaningful Impact -- Work on AI-driven projects that drive real change across industries and improve lives.

Learn more at: avathon.com

We are hiring an Engineering Lead for Product Lifecycle Management to own the technical delivery of Avathon's PLM integrations and the AI capabilities built on top of them. You will work alongside our Forward Deployed Design Leads and customer engineering teams to connect PLM, CAD/PDM, ERP and MES systems to the Avathon platform, model product structures and engineering change flows in our Computational Knowledge Graph, and ship the BOM comparison, change impact and digital thread features customers use every day. This is a hands-on lead role. You will write code, own the integration architecture, and lead a small team of engineers through implementation, go-live and hypercare.

Responsibilities:

PLM Integration Architecture
- Own the technical design for integrating customer PLM systems (Teamcenter, Windchill, 3DEXPERIENCE, SAP PLM, Oracle Agile) with the Avathon platform
- Build and maintain connectors and data pipelines from PLM, CAD/PDM, ERP and MES sources into our Bronze/Silver/Gold data lake
- Define canonical data models for parts, EBOM and MBOM structures, variants, effectivity and engineering changes
- Set standards for data quality, sync latency and reconciliation between source systems and the platform

Knowledge Graph and AI Features- Model product structures and change relationships (ECR, ECO, MCA, MBOM, BOP) in the Computational Knowledge Graph so any change can be traced to its downstream impact
- Build the backend services behind BOM comparison, engineering change impact and clear-to-build views
- Work with our ML, data science and agent teams to apply Normal Behavior Models and AI agents to PLM data, such as flagging unusual ECR patterns or change-driven supply risk
- Turn one-off customer work into reusable platform components

Delivery and Technical Leadership
- Hands on lead to through discovery, build, go-live and hypercare on customer deployments
- Run technical working sessions with customer PLM, IT and engineering teams and act as the senior technical contact on the account
- Own go-live readiness: integration testing, data validation, performance and security review
- Review designs and code, set engineering practices, and mentor engineers on the PLM domain
- Partner with design, product and customer success to scope work, call out risk early and keep delivery on plan

Key Qualifications:

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field
- 8+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years leading engineers or technical delivery
- Hands-on integration experience with at least one enterprise PLM platform (Teamcenter, Windchill, 3DEXPERIENCE, SAP PLM or Oracle Agile), including its APIs and data model
- Strong working knowledge of BOM management, engineering change management, variants and effectivity
- Experience integrating PLM with ERP, CAD/PDM, MES and quality systems
- Strong backend skills in Python with experience building data pipelines and REST APIs
- Experience with graph data models or graph databases is a strong plus
- Familiarity with digital thread concepts; MBSE exposure (SysML, Cameo, Rhapsody) is a plus
- Experience in manufacturing, automotive, aerospace or defense environments
- Comfortable working directly with customers and traveling to customer sites
- Clear technical writing and communication

Salary Range: $160,000-$220,000

jobs.title: Solutions Architect, Enterprise IT
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

Industrial labor powers our world and protecting the people who do that work is both a moral imperative and a business advantage. At Voxel, we're transforming workplace safety and operational efficiency through AI-driven computer vision technology that helps organizations see unseen risks before incidents occur.

Voxel's platform enables Fortune 500 safety and operations leaders to uncover root causes, drive proactive risk reduction, and make smarter, data-driven decisions. Our Solutions Engineering team ensures customers successfully adopt, deploy, and scale Voxel across complex enterprise environments.

 
 


THE ROLE

As a Solutions Architect, Enterprise IT at Voxel, you'll be the technical expert on our largest enterprise deals. Partnering with our sales and account teams, you'll work directly with customers' corporate IT, security, and infrastructure teams to design how Voxel's edge AI platform fits into their environments, from network access and device management to security and compliance requirements.

You'll lead technical discussions with prospective and existing customers, turn complex requirements into clear, workable solutions, and act as the bridge between customers and Voxel's Product and Engineering teams to ensure our platform integrates seamlessly at scale.

This role is built for a seasoned enterprise IT expert who is just as comfortable whiteboarding a solution with a customer's IT team as they are aligning internal stakeholders around it.

 
 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead technical discovery with enterprise IT, security, and infrastructure teams to understand their environments, requirements, and constraints.

 - Design tailored solutions that meet each customer's technical requirements, including network access and bandwidth, device management, and security.

 - Partner with Sales and Customer Success teams on large enterprise deals to resolve technical blockers.

 - Own Voxel's compliance with customer security requirements, leading security reviews, IT questionnaires, and architecture approvals as the technical point of contact.

 - Create clear, customer-facing solution documents and architecture diagrams that translate complex technical requirements into decisions customers can act on.

 - Work closely with our Deployment team to ensure agreed-upon solutions are implemented successfully.

 - Serve as the senior escalation point for complex enterprise IT, network, and security challenges throughout the sales process and deployment.

 - Act as the voice of enterprise customers to Product and Engineering, translating customer needs into technical requirements that shape the product roadmap.

 - Build reusable reference architectures and solution patterns that make it faster to say yes to future enterprise requirements.

 
 


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required Qualifications

 - 6–8 years of experience in solutions architecture, sales engineering, or enterprise IT/network engineering roles.

 - Deep expertise in corporate IT networking and systems (TCP/IP, routing, firewalls, VPNs, Linux internals, edge/IoT architectures)

 - Experience leading technical discussions with senior technical stakeholders across enterprise IT, security, and infrastructure teams.

 - Proven ability to gather requirements from enterprise customers and translate them into clear technical requirements for Engineering.

 - Strong track record of creating customer-facing technical documentation, solution designs, and architecture diagrams.

 - Familiarity with enterprise security requirements and processes, such as security reviews, IT questionnaires, and compliance frameworks like SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

Nice to Have

 - Hands-on experience with 802.1X, certificate management/PKI, or enterprise device management.

 - Background working with large multi-site environments such as warehouses, distribution centers, or retail.

 - Relevant certifications such as CCNP, CISSP, or equivalent.

jobs.title: Training Specialist
jobs.description:
The future of aerospace and defense starts here.

Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch. We design and deliver propulsion and defense systems that solve the most urgent and critical national security demands.

Training Specialist

The future of aerospace and defense starts here.

Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from space and hypersonics to solid rocket motors. Our products and technologies require an extraordinary team—a team that will mold tomorrow’s technologies while deploying today’s best. We are a motivated team with a passion for solving problems and empowering each other every day to develop our skills, knowing there is always room for growth.

Role Summary

Ursa Major is seeking a Training Specialist to support the development, coordination, delivery, and continuous improvement of learning programs across the organization. This role will partner closely with People Operations, leaders, managers, and subject matter experts to deliver effective learning experiences that support employee onboarding, development, compliance, and organizational capability.

A significant component of this role will be ownership of the operational execution of Ursa Major’s new hire onboarding program. The Training Specialist will proactively manage onboarding activities from pre-boarding through the employee’s first day, coordinating across hiring managers, People Operations, IT, Security, Facilities, and other internal partners to ensure new employees have a consistent, welcoming, and well-prepared experience.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, proactive, comfortable facilitating across a variety of audiences, and able to manage both detailed program execution and broader learning initiatives in a fast-paced environment.

Responsibilities

Training & Development

• Support the design, development, coordination, and delivery of employee learning and development programs across the organization.

• Develop, update, and maintain training materials, including presentations, facilitator guides, participant materials, job aids, e-learning content, and other learning resources.

• Partner with leaders, managers, People Operations, and subject matter experts to understand training needs and translate those needs into effective learning solutions.

• Support training needs assessments through employee and manager feedback, organizational priorities, performance trends, and other available data.

• Coordinate leadership and manager development programs, including scheduling, communications, materials, participant management, and facilitation support.

• Coordinate required compliance and recurring employee training programs, including communication, scheduling, completion tracking, and documentation.

• Coordinate additional learning opportunities, including systems training, technical or functional introductory training, and other available in-person or virtual development opportunities.

• Maintain training calendars, learning records, attendance, completion data, and related documentation.

• Gather participant feedback and evaluate training effectiveness using surveys, assessments, completion data, performance indicators, and other available metrics.

• Identify opportunities to improve training content, delivery methods, processes, and the overall employee learning experience.

New Hire Onboarding

• Own the operational execution and coordination of Ursa Major’s new hire onboarding program, proactively monitoring upcoming hires and independently managing required activities and deadlines leading up to each employee’s start date.

• Serve as the primary coordinator for new hire readiness, partnering with hiring managers, People Operations, IT, Security, Facilities, and other internal teams to ensure onboarding requirements are completed accurately and on time.

• Manage pre-boarding communications with new hires and hiring managers, including manager readiness checklists, first-day communications, schedules, expectations, and other required information.

• Confirm hiring managers have appropriate first-day plans in place, including team integration, work location, lunch arrangements, and plans following formal onboarding activities.

• Track new hire setup and readiness across applicable systems and resources.

• Proactively follow up with responsible teams on outstanding onboarding items and communicate or escalate readiness concerns as appropriate.

• Coordinate onboarding presenters and schedules. Manage onboarding logistics, including room reservations, calendar invitations, training materials, new hire binders, swag, desk readiness, and other onsite preparation.

• Support HRIS onboarding activities, including monitoring completion of new hire information and required onboarding steps and completing assigned People Operations actions necessary to move employees through the hiring and onboarding process.

• Coordinate additional new hire learning experiences, including introductory systems training, available in-person training, facility or operational experiences, and other role-relevant learning opportunities.

• Provide day-of onboarding support, including preparing training spaces, welcoming new hires, helping employees get settled, facilitating applicable portions of onboarding, and responding to or appropriately directing questions.

• Partner with presenters and People Operations to continuously improve onboarding schedules, content, materials, and learning experiences.

• Identify recurring onboarding gaps or readiness issues and recommend process improvements that create a more consistent and effective new hire experience.

• Support contractor onboarding activities and related processes as assigned.

• Bachelor's or Associates degree in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Education, Business, Communications, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

• 2+ years of experience in corporate training, learning and development, employee onboarding, organizational development, or a related field.

• Experience facilitating training or presentations for employee, manager, or other professional audiences.

• Experience developing, coordinating, or maintaining training programs and learning materials.

• Working knowledge of adult learning principles and instructional design concepts.

• Strong written and verbal communication and presentation skills.

• Strong organizational and project management skills with demonstrated ability to independently manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholders.

• High attention to detail and demonstrated ability to proactively identify and follow through on outstanding actions.

• Ability to build collaborative relationships and work effectively with employees, managers, leaders, and subject matter experts across functions.

• Ability to analyze feedback and training data to identify trends and opportunities for improvement.

• Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment where priorities and business needs may change quickly.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office or similar productivity tools.

Preferred Experience:

• Experience owning or coordinating a new hire onboarding or orientation program.

• Experience with a Learning Management System (LMS), HRIS, or other learning technology.

• Experience developing e-learning or digital learning content.

• Experience supporting leadership or manager development programs.

• Experience supporting compliance or required employee training programs.

• Experience working within a manufacturing, engineering, aerospace, defense, or other technical environment.

jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Managing Directory, Private Equity (PE) is a senior commercial leadership role within RRD’s RevTeam. This individual is responsible for establishing relationships with the Private Equity ecosystem to build strategic, long-term sales momentum. Unlike traditional high-volume

sales roles, this position requires a nuanced, high-trust, low-volume "Account-Based Selling" approach.

The incentive program range is 20% - 30% of base salary payable based on achieved performance metrics.

The primary mission is to identify, secure, and expand relationships directly with PE Operating Partners, Portfolio Operations leads, and Value Creation directors who are under immense pressure to drive EBITDA growth. By deeply understanding the financial objectives of PE firms, this leader will position RRD’s specialized portfolio of services and our unique consultative assessment process as the go-to solution for driving enterprise value across portfolio companies.

Key Responsibilities

• Target Identification & Strategic Relationship Building

• Identify & Engage Key Stakeholders: Target and build deep, recurring relationships with Portfolio Operations leads, Operating Partners, and Value Creation directors within targeted funds, segmented by sector and strategy.
• Network Utilization: Leverage an existing professional network to gain access to highly gatekept PE environments and create meaningful business conversations.
• Peer-to-Peer Engagement: Speak the distinct financial and operational vocabulary of the PE universe to establish immediate credibility with operational leadership.

• Master Service Agreement (MSA) Navigation

• Navigate complex PE procurement processes to secure Master Service Agreements (MSAs) within their portfolio of operating companies.
• Short-List Positioning: Ensure that when an Operating Partner identifies an operational inefficiencies or cost takeout initiative within a portfolio company (PortCo), RRD is automatically positioned on the short-list to call.

• Portfolio Company (PortCo) Expansion

• Expand Success: Actively expand RRD’s footprint across multiple targeted portfolio companies by leveraging and proving early success in initial PortCo engagements.
• Account Growth: Network across the firm’s broader ecosystem to cross-sell and scale RRD’s services into additional portfolio assets.

• Leverage Value Creation Tactics

• Pro-Bono/Low-Cost Assessments: Introduce specialized operational assessments during the PE firm's pre-acquisition due diligence and long-term holding phases.
• Pipeline Building: Utilize these early assessments to build immense goodwill, positioning RRD to win the full execution contract the day the acquisition deal officially closes.

Education and Experience

• Degree: Bachelor’s degree in business, Finance, or a related discipline required; Master’s degree or MBA preferred.
• Target Professional Profile: Must possess a background matching one or more of the following archetypes:The Ex-Management Consultant (MBB / Big 4): Alumni of McKinsey, Bain, BCG, or a tier-1 operations consulting firm, specifically from their Private Equity or Post-Merger Integration practices. Understands how PE firms think and possesses a strong peer network. The Former PortCo Executive: A former COO, VP of Sales, or VP of Operations who has successfully scaled and exited a PE-backed portfolio company, bringing immediate empathy and peer-to-peer credibility.The Boutique PE-Origination Specialist: A proven track record of successfully selling professional services (e.g., IT, HR infrastructure, supply chain consulting) directly to PE funds.
• Geographic Location: Must be physically based in one of the primary, highly regional PE hubs to facilitate face-to-face, "handshake" relationship building:East Coast: New York City / Greenwich, CT / BostonMidwest: ChicagoWest Coast: San Francisco / Silicon Valley / Los AngelesSecondary consideration: Austin / Miami / Atlanta

Core Competencies and Skills

• PE Financial Literacy: Deep understanding of the core financial metrics driving the PE universe, including EBITDA, IRR (Internal Rate of Return), Multiple Expansion, and the execution of the 100-Day Plan.
• Solution Mapping: Ability to quickly master RRD’s diverse portfolio of services and translate them directly into levers for a PE firm’s financial and operational objectives.
• ABM Commercial Expertise: Highly skilled in running low-volume, high-trust Account-Based Selling strategies tailored for long, complex institutional sales cycles.
• Collaborative Leadership: Ability to work cross-functionally within RRD to deploy specialized delivery teams once a fund-level relationship or MSA is secured.

Performance Evaluation (KPIs)

Rather than relying solely on traditional short-term invoiced revenue, success in this role will be measured by:

• Signed MSA Agreements: Number of Master Service Agreements executed at the portfolio company level.
• Executed Assessment Engagements: Volume of pre- or post-acquisition operational assessments signed and delivered.
• Sales Revenue: Recognized revenue attributed to PE relationships and engagements.

This role is salary plus incentive program eligible and the current RRD salary range is $175,000 to $245,000 per year. The salary range may be adjusted based on the applicable geographic location of the hired employee, and the range may change in the future. At RRD, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions may vary based upon, but not limited to education, skills, experience, proficiency, performance, shift and location. RRD’s benefit offerings include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, life insurance and other voluntary supplemental insurance coverages, plus parental leave, adoption assistance, tuition assistance and employer/partner discounts.

About Equip 

Equip is the leading virtual, evidence-based eating disorder treatment program on a mission to ensure that everyone with an eating disorder can access treatment that works. Created by clinical experts in the field and people with lived experience, Equip builds upon evidence-based treatments to empower individuals to reach lasting recovery. About the Role

The Director of Business Operations will be responsible for leading the strategic execution, operational cadence, and infrastructure across Equip’s Care Operations function. This role serves as a critical operational backbone, translating high-level organizational strategy into scalable systems that elevate both Care Delivery and Care Experience. By establishing robust operational accountability and guiding a team of analysts and project managers, the Director ensures cross-functional alignment and peak departmental performance. Ultimately, this role powers Equip’s growth by building sustainable systems that enable our care teams to deliver high-quality treatment at scale.

Responsibilities

 - Own the strategic planning, goal setting, and operational cadence for the Care Operations department to drive organizational alignment and business outcomes.

 - Lead a team of analysts and project managers, providing direct management, performance oversight, and professional development.

 - Design and execute high-impact initiatives that improve operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and overall patient and provider experience across Care Operations.

 - Direct data analysis and operational reporting to uncover trends, diagnose root causes, and translate insights into scalable action plans.

 - Partner with cross-functional leadership to build, pilot, and implement standardized processes, project plans, and change management strategies across Care Delivery and Care Experience.

 - Establish comprehensive tracking frameworks, operational metrics, and performance dashboards to ensure departmental accountability and quality control.

 - Develop scalable operational infrastructure, best practice documentation, and continuous improvement mechanisms that support long-term organizational growth.

 - Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

 - 5+ years of professional experience in business operations, management consulting, program management, or a related field within a healthcare or high-growth environment.

 - Bachelor’s degree in business, operations, healthcare administration, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

 - Demonstrated experience managing direct reports, including analysts or project managers, and driving team performance.

 - Demonstrated experience leading end-to-end strategic project management, process improvement, and change management initiatives.

 - Demonstrated experience writing and utilizing SQL to query complex datasets and translate operational data into actionable insights.

 - Demonstrated ability to design, pilot, and implement scalable operational processes across cross-functional teams.

 - Demonstrated proficiency using data analysis and spreadsheet tools (e.g., Excel, Google Sheets) to build operational models and reporting frameworks.

 - Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities, resolve complex operational challenges, and communicate effectively with senior stakeholders.

Compensation & Benefits Package

Compensation: 

 - Earning Potential Range: $140,000 to $175,000 + 20% Annual Performance-Based Bonus Potential

Time Off:

 - Flex PTO policy (3-5 wks/year recommended) + 11 paid company holidays.

 - Generous Parental Leave. 

Core Benefits: 

 - Competitive Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, and AD&D insurance.
   
   - Equip pays for a significant percentage of benefits premiums for individuals and families.

 - Spring Health, a 100% employer-paid mental health benefit through Guardian.
   
   - You can receive 5 free therapy sessions and 5 free coaching sessions per year for you and each of your dependents.

 - Employee Assistance Program (EAP), a company-paid resource for mental health, legal services, financial support, and more!

 - HealthJoy, a 100% employer-paid platform connecting you to a healthcare concierge who can help you navigate your benefits.

 - 401K Option! 

Work From Home Additional Perks: 

 - $50/month stipend added directly to an employee’s paycheck to cover home internet expenses. 

 - Initial work-from-home stipend of up to $500.

Physical Demands

Work is performed 100% from home with no requirement to travel. Must be able to remain in a stationary period for prolonged periods at a desk or workstation, with the option to alternate between sitting and standing as needed. Must be able to operate standard office equipment such as a computer screen and keyboards as well as to exchange accurate information, actively listen, and communicate clearly with colleagues, clients or stakeholders over the phone, via video conferencing, and/or in person.

We use an online assessment tool called Maki for skills-based selection of applicants for sales advisor positions within some of our stores. Maki is not an automated decision-making tool. jobs.title: Senior Staff Program Lead, Cloud Engineering Operations
jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About This Role

Crusoe's Cloud Engineering organization is 380 people today and hiring toward 550. When we sell capacity, we make customers two promises: it will be ready on the date we said, and it will work while they use it. At this scale, keeping those promises doesn't happen by accident anymore. This role exists to make sure it happens on purpose.

You'll lead Engineering Operations: the operating system that lets Cloud Engineering leadership agree on outcomes, execute, and keep its promises to customers. You'll own the standing programs that make operations better every week (SLOs, incident follow-up, change safety, capacity delivery tracking, and operational data) and build the systems that feed the weekly executive Engineering Operations review. You don't just report when a metric slips; you find the owner, hold them to the commitment, and make sure a decision happens fast.

You'll start as the first hire in this function, working solo while you prove out the model above. As the mandate holds up, you'll shape how the function grows: what to build, who to bring in, and what to keep lean.

This isn't a role scoped to a single program or a single dashboard. You will be a strategic advisor to leadership on whether teams are actually executing operationally, and the person who makes clear owners, shared metrics, and a steady cadence stick across the org.

The ideal candidate has a technical background (software engineering, SRE, Technical Program Management, or product in an infrastructure context) and is close enough to production systems to hold senior engineering leaders to what they committed.



What You'll Be Working On

Engineering Operations programs

 - Own the standing Engineering Operations programs: SLO/SLI definition and attainment, incident management and follow-up, change safety (change policy, maintenance readiness, and pre-production checks), capacity delivery tracking, and operational data. Partner with the engineering leaders who own each program and hold the line on outcomes.

 - Define and track the metrics that show how the org runs, grows, builds, and enables itself: usable capacity, SLO attainment, MTTD and MTTR, customer-found incidents, on-time capacity delivery, milestone slip, change failure rate, follow-up closure rate, and change policy compliance. Data should tell the story before anyone has to ask.

 - Partner with engineering, SRE, data engineering, and product to keep operational data accurate, with one source of truth for each metric.

 - Partner with engineering, TPM, product, SRE, data scientists, customer success, and data center operations to ensure operations run smoothly across all functional areas.

 - Work toward a single pane of glass that makes the operational health of the organization easy to understand at a glance.



Accountability and operating cadence

 - Own the weekly executive Engineering Operations review: build the systems, data, and pre-reads that feed it, and make sure every risk on the page has an owner, a date, and a next step.

 - Run the weekly operations planning forum, and partner with Product on a monthly business review that ties operational health to customer outcomes.

 - Make ownership explicit: clear accountable owners, swimlanes, and articulated outcomes for every program and metric.

 - Hold teams to what they committed. Drive incident follow-ups, overdue actions, and slipping milestones to closure, and escalate fast when an owner can't fix the problem alone.

Growing the function

 - Operate as an individual contributor first: prove out the programs, metrics, and cadence before asking for headcount.

 - Make the case for more capacity as scope outgrows one person, then help hire and onboard the people who join the function.

 - Own the evolution of the operating system itself, not just the programs inside it: retire process that no longer earns its cost, and keep the overhead on engineering teams as low as possible.

What You'll Bring to the Team

 - 10+ years in software engineering, SRE, technical program management, or a technical product role, close enough to production systems to know what an SLO breach actually means.

 - A track record of leading org-wide programs at the staff level or above, and of driving accountability across senior engineering leaders without formal authority.

 - Comfortable starting as a team of one: you don't need a team in place to start driving impact, and you know when the case for headcount is real versus premature.

 - You've operated in high-growth infrastructure environments where processes are still being built; ambiguity doesn't paralyze you.

 - You're a natural coordinator who works across teams without formal authority. Engineering, SRE, and product leads trust you because you follow through.

 - You can turn messy, multi-source data into a clear picture of organizational health, and you know how to pick the few metrics that drive decisions over the many that fill dashboards.

 - You've designed operating rhythms (weekly reviews, business reviews, incident reviews) that leaders actually use, and you keep them light for the teams that feed them.

 - Scrappy, low-ego, high-drive. You build the program and tooling yourself when it doesn't exist yet, and you care more about the outcome than the credit.



Bonus Points

 - Time inside AWS, GCP, Azure, CoreWeave, Lambda Labs, or a similar cloud provider.

 - Experience running an SLO, incident review, or change management program at a cloud or infrastructure company.

 - Familiarity with incident.io http://incident.io, Opsgenie, PagerDuty, or similar incident management platforms at scale.

 - Background in AI/ML infrastructure.



Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $230,000 - $280,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

jobs.description:

Kikoff: The Fintech Powering Financial Security at Scale
Kikoff is a profitable, pre-IPO fintech company on a mission to empower everyone to achieve financial security. With record revenue growth in 2025 and a unicorn valuation, we've built a suite of products that help millions of people build credit, access liquidity, and save money.
We're scaling fast. Join us if you want to build something meaningful and help millions of people move forward financially.

We value extreme ownership, clear communication, a strong sense of craftsmanship, and the desire to create lasting work and work relationships. Yes, you can build an exciting business AND have real-life real-customer impact.

About the Role

Kikoff's growth depends on marketing that moves fast and connects with our customers. At the same time, our marketing must be accurate, substantiated, properly disclosed, and approved. Reporting to the Head of Compliance, you will be the person who makes both happen in English and in Spanish.

This is not just a reviewer seat. We are hiring a builder and owner of marketing compliance and a shared system of record with AI-assisted review that will keep pace with the speedy marketing team. You will lead that build.

What You'll Do

• Own marketing compliance end to end by enforcing the standards, review, claims substantiation, records, monitoring, and tooling and set the roadmap for it with the Head of Compliance.

• Review consumer-facing material in English and Spanish across channels, including paid social and search, email and SMS, landing pages and web, in-app and onboarding flows, app store listings, direct mail, affiliate and influencer content, customer support guidance, and partner collateral.

• Review Spanish creative on its own terms, ensuring disclosures are equivalent in meaning and prominence to their English counterparts and that legal terminology is rendered correctly rather than literally.

• Take the lead on developing Kikoff's AI-assisted marketing review capability and partner with Legal, Marketing, and Engineering to build it, including the ground truth it depends on and how it is evaluated before it is trusted.

• Maintain the policies, procedures, risk tiering, disclosure standards, and channel playbooks, and keep review records to satisfy examiners, auditors, and bank partners.

What We're Looking For

• Full professional fluency in Spanish and English, with the ability to review, edit, and give written compliance guidance on financial marketing copy in both. This is a working requirement of the role, assessed in an interview.

• 6+ years in compliance, legal, or regulatory review in consumer financial services, including 4+ years directly reviewing and approving consumer marketing and advertising at a bank, fintech, lender, or similarly regulated consumer brand.

• Experience owning a marketing review function or program, not just a queue. Demonstrated high-volume review at speed, and the ability to speak to how you kept quality from slipping as throughput went up.

• Experience driving automation of a review process and the appetite to specify AI tooling; having built or configured AI-assisted review, claims checking, or marketing monitoring yourself is a significant plus.

• A strong sense of urgency. You treat the launch date as a real constraint, and you would rather give a clear answer today with the caveat attached than a perfect one after the campaign has shipped.

• Excellent written communication in both languages, and the ability to influence without authority.

We're Also Looking For

• Credit-building, credit reporting, or subscription financial product experience; managing a bank partner's marketing approval process; fair lending exposure in advertising and audience targeting; or hands-on use of marketing compliance monitoring platforms such as PerformLine, any of these is a plus.

• CRCM, CIPP/US, or a JD is a plus and not required.

If you meet most of this, we'd like to hear from you.

$115,000—$170,000 USD

jobs.title: Director, Research & Data
jobs.description:
About Ceribell

Ceribell is a medical technology company focused on transforming the diagnosis and management of patients with serious neurological conditions. The Ceribell System is a novel, point-of-care electroencephalography (“EEG”) platform specifically designed to address the unmet needs of patients in the acute care setting, and is being used in hundreds of community hospitals, large academic facilities and major IDN's across the country. Our entire team is driven by a shared commitment to transforming the landscape of critical care through our rapid seizure detection technology, come join the movement!

Position Overview:

As Director/Manager of Research and Data at Ceribell, you will lead the effort to find, acquire, and secure the clinical and EEG datasets that power the development of new indications for the Ceribell EEG platform. This role is part of Ceribell's Data Science team, with a dotted line to the Clinical team, and sits at the intersection of R&D, Clinical, and our academic and hospital partners. You will build relationships with researchers and academic centers, evaluate research proposals and support research collaborations, and drive EMR integrations with partner hospitals so that Data Science has the high-quality, clinically well-characterized data it needs to build and validate new algorithms. The Ceribell EEG platform opens the door to additional clinical indications where faster access to EEG-based insight could improve patient care, and this is an opportunity to help shape that expansion.

What you'll do:

• Work with Data Science team to translate the needs of new indications into specific data requirements and a prioritized data acquisition plan.

• Identify, evaluate, and build relationships with researchers, physician advisors, and academic centers who hold or can collect the data we need. Negotiate data access, licensing, and purchase arrangements.

• Evaluate research proposals from external investigators for scientific merit, clinical relevance, and alignment with our indication priorities. Serve as the scientific point of contact for research collaborations from proposal through data return, and help shape study designs so the resulting data is usable for algorithm development.

• Lead EMR integration efforts with partner hospitals to obtain linked clinical context and outcomes data. Work with hospital IT, clinical informatics, and clinical champions to scope data feeds, mappings, and workflows.

• Assess the quality and fit of incoming datasets (label quality, cohort definition, population diversity, annotation methodology) in partnership with data scientists before and after acquisition.

• Partner with Legal, Regulatory, and Privacy on data use agreements, IRB requirements, de-identification, and HIPAA compliance.

• Work closely with the Clinical team to support early-stage clinical studies and ensure data collection aligns with study protocols.

• Maintain a data asset inventory and pipeline tracker: what we have, what we need, and what is in negotiation.

• Manage multiple simultaneous data partnerships and projects across indications.

• Represent Ceribell at scientific conferences and in academic networks.

What We're Looking For:

• Advanced degree (MD, PhD, PharmD, DNP, or equivalent) in a clinical or research-oriented field, such as neurology, neuroscience, critical care, neurophysiology, or biomedical science.

• At least 5 years of experience in clinical research, healthcare, or medical technology, with a track record of building and managing research collaborations with academic institutions and investigators.

• Strong clinical and research judgment, including the ability to evaluate study design, research proposals, and clinical data quality.

• Working knowledge of data science and machine learning fundamentals sufficient to judge dataset suitability.

• Working knowledge of basic statistics, including sample size and power, confidence intervals, sensitivity and specificity, and common sources of bias and confounding, sufficient to evaluate study designs and dataset adequacy.

• Experience with EMR data and integrations, or clinical informatics projects.

• Familiarity with clinical research regulations and data governance (IRB, HIPAA, de-identification, data use agreements).

• Experience with EEG or other biosignal data is preferred.

• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain technical data needs to clinicians and clinical context to data scientists.

• Entrepreneurial mindset, adaptability, and a passion for improving patient outcomes through data.

Compensation Range

$222,000—$242,000 USD

A candidate’s final salary offer will be based on their skills, education, work location and experience, and thus it may differ from the posted range. Compensation may also include bonuses consistent with Ceribell’s corporate compensation plan. Note, the above description is not all-encompassing and Ceribell reserves the right to change or modify job duties and assignments at any time.

In addition to your base compensation, Ceribell offers eligible employees the following:

• 13 Paid Holidays + 3 Company Wellness Days

• Fantastic culture with tremendous career advancement opportunities

• Joining a mission-minded organization!

Ceribell reports transfers of value to health care providers (HCPs) as required by federal and state transparency laws. These laws and implementing regulations require Ceribell to provide government agencies with HCPs’ names, addresses and the type of payments or other value received, generally for public disclosure. jobs.title: Program Manager, Massed Modular Aircraft
jobs.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

Role Overview:

We are seeking an experienced Program Manager with a strong technical background to lead the planning, execution, and delivery of autonomous Massed Modular Aircraft program contracted through Defense Innovation Unit (DIU). The successful candidate will own program cost, schedule, and technical performance (CSP) baselines from proposal through development, test, production, and sustainment, serving as the primary interface with customers (DoW, government agencies, international customers), internal engineering teams, operations teams, and supply chain partners. This role requires a rare blend of program management discipline and hands-on technical fluency in military aircraft domain.

Responsibilities:

• Own full program P&L, including cost performance, schedule adherence (IMS/IMP), risk/opportunity management, and technical baseline control (EVMS-lite) across the program lifecycle.

• Serve as primary point of contact for customer program offices (e.g., PEO, PM offices), leading program reviews (PMR, technical interchange meetings, milestone reviews).

• Coordinate cross-functional Integrated Product Teams (IPTs) spanning systems engineering, airframe, aerodynamics, guidance, propulsion, warhead/payload integration, avionics, software, manufacturing, quality, test, and logistics.

• Develop and maintain Integrated Master Schedules (IMS); manage critical path and resolve schedule conflicts.

• Manage program risk and opportunity registers; drive mitigation plans for technical, schedule, cost, and supply chain risks.

• Support proposal development, including Basis of Estimate (BOE) generation, technical volume input, pricing strategy, and capture activities for new business and follow-on contracts.

• Provide informed oversight across the full system lifecycle: requirements decomposition, System Requirements Review (SRR), Preliminary/Critical Design Review (PDR/CDR), integration, flight/static test, Test Readiness Review (TRR), and Production Readiness Review (PRR).

• Partner with Chief Engineer and systems engineering lead to assess technical trade studies, verify requirements traceability, and ensure design maturity gates are met.

• Oversee airworthiness, flight safety, and range safety processes, and ensure compliance with applicable safety standards.

• Coordinate developmental and operational test campaigns (DT&E/OT&E), including flight test, captive carry, HIL/SIL integration labs, and environmental/qualification testing.

• Ensure configuration management (CM) rigor and technical data package integrity across engineering releases.

• Manage contract performance against FAR/DFARS requirements, CDRLs, and contract line items (CLINs); support contract modifications and Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs).

• Ensure compliance with ITAR/EAR export control regulations, DoW security requirements (NISPOM), and applicable airspace/range approvals (e.g., FAA COA, military range safety).

• Manage supply chain and subcontractor performance for long-lead and critical components (seekers, guidance electronics, propulsion, warheads, airframes, avionics).

• Report program status, financial performance, and risk posture to executive leadership and customer stakeholders.

Minimum Requirements:

• Minimum 15 years of program/project management experience within the defense or aerospace industry, with direct experience managing an aircraft program

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical field

• Strong working knowledge of Earned Value Management Systems (EVMS), Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) development, and risk management processes.

• Experience managing programs under FAR/DFARS contract types (CPFF, CPIF, FFP) and supporting government customer program offices.

• Excellent leadership, negotiation, and executive-level communication skills; demonstrated ability to manage cross-functional IPTs and lead through influence.

• Willingness to travel (typically 20–30%) to customer sites, test ranges, and manufacturing/integration facilities.

Preferred Requirements:

• Master’s degree or MBA preferred.

• PMP certification preferred

• Experience supporting Foreign Military Sales (FMS) or international program execution.

• Experience with digital engineering environments and model-based acquisition approaches.

• Prior experience as a Chief Engineer, Deputy Program Manager, or Integration Lead prior to moving into Program Manager roles.

• Ability to obtain/maintain Secret/Top Secret/SCI clearance

Why CHAOS?

• Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company

• Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more

• Our Perks: Free daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code

• Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses

• Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices

Salary Range: $230,000 - $330,000

The stated compensation range reflects only the targeted base compensation range and excludes additional earnings such as bonus, equity, and benefits. If your compensation requirements fall outside of the range, we still encourage you to apply. The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant & Office Coordinator
jobs.description:
ABOUT RADIANT

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based startup building the world’s first mass-produced, portable nuclear microreactors. The company’s first reactor, Kaleidos, is a 1-megawatt, fail-safe microreactor that can be transported anywhere power is needed and run for up to 5 years without refueling. Portable nuclear power with rapid-deploy capability can replace similar-sized diesel generators and provide critical asset support for hospitals, data centers, remote sites, and military bases. Radiant’s unique, practical approach to nuclear development leverages modern software engineering to rapidly deliver safe, factory-built microreactors that use existing, well-qualified materials. Founded in 2020, Radiant is on track to test its first reactor at the Idaho National Laboratory this summer, with initial customer deliveries beginning in 2028.

Executive Assistant to the Chief Nuclear Officer & DC Office Coordinator 


Radiant’s goals are ambitious – we will be the first company to mass-produce portable nuclear reactors. We have world-class engineers designing our Kaleidos 1MW microreactor, and we need a world-class team to build our business. Radiant is looking for a bright and eager executive assistant and office coordinator to join our Government Affairs team in DC and be a welcoming, friendly host to all visitors entering our office. 
 
Responsibilities & Duties:

Executive Assistant to the Chief Nuclear Officer (CNO)

 - Manage CNO’s dynamic schedule, including frequent domestic and international travel, external meetings with high-profile officials, interviews with the press, and worldwide speaking engagements

 - Become familiar with Radiant’s wide-spanning public and private sector network and balance the CNO’s priorities across external stakeholder engagements and internal projects

 - Attend calls with event organizers on behalf of the CNO

 - You will often represent the CNO and the wider company – handle all communications and engagements (internal & external, virtual & in-person) with respectful professionalism



Office/Administrative

jobs.title: Thermo-Mechanical Design Engineer - Reactor Cavity Cooling Systems
jobs.description:
About Us

At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space.



The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy.

About the Team

As a Thermo-Mechanical Design Engineer, you will be the Responsible Engineer (RE) for the Reactor Cavity Cooling System (RCCS), leading the design and analysis of a critical deployment system. You will be responsible for the thermal, mechanical, and piping design of the RCCS, ensuring the reactor cavity and surrounding structures remain within design temperature limits, while minimizing wasted thermal power. This role involves thermal-fluid analysis, piping and structural sizing, filtration system design, and integration of piping, supports, stacks, and cavity components. The ideal candidate has expertise in thermal-fluid systems, HVAC, piping, and structural design, and enjoys solving multidisciplinary engineering challenges in a highly constrained design environment.



Roles and Responsibilities:

 - Perform thermal-fluid, mechanical, and structural analyses to support the sizing, layout, and optimization of cooling system components, including piping, ducts, stacks, supports, filtration equipment, and reactor cavity structures.

 - Define system architecture, operating limits, design margins, and control strategies to ensure reliable performance across all operating conditions.

 - Develop design documentation, including engineering calculations, system specifications, interface definitions, design reports, and technical justifications to support licensing and design reviews.

 - Support the design, fabrication, and execution of component and system-level testing by developing test articles, test stands, instrumentation plans, and validation procedures to demonstrate system performance and life-cycle reliability.

 - Coordinate cross-functionally with reactor systems, structures, licensing, manufacturing, procurement, and operations teams to ensure successful integration of the RCCS into the overall plant design.

 - Support supplier selection, technical evaluations, design reviews, and resolution of manufacturing and installation issues.

 - Present technical work at internal and external design reviews and provide engineering leadership throughout the design, analysis, testing, and deployment lifecycle.

Basic Qualifications:

 - Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a related engineering discipline with an emphasis on thermal-fluid sciences, heat transfer

 - 5+ years of professional engineering experience in the design, analysis, or development of thermal-fluid, HVAC, heat transfer, or cooling systems.

 - Experience performing engineering analyses including thermal, fluid flow, and structural calculations to support component and system design.

 - Demonstrated ability to work effectively on multidisciplinary engineering teams and communicate technical concepts to a variety of stakeholders.

Preferred Skills & Experience:

 - Master's degree or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, Thermal Sciences, or a related discipline.

 - Experience designing or analyzing natural circulation, buoyancy-driven, or convective heat transfer systems using CFD or multiphysics simulation tools.

 - Demonstrated expertise in HVAC or industrial ventilation system design, including equipment selection, ducting, filtration, airflow management, and system performance testing.

 - Proficiency with engineering analysis and simulation tools such as ANSYS, COMSOL Multiphysics, or equivalent finite element (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) software.

 - Knowledge of materials and structural design considerations, including material selection for heat transfer applications, thermal stresses, creep, corrosion, and environmental degradation.

 - Experience designing systems in accordance with ASME Boiler & Pressure Vessel Code, ASME B31 piping codes, or other applicable mechanical and structural design standards.

 - Experience serving as a technical lead or Responsible Engineer, coordinating multidisciplinary engineering activities from concept development through testing and deployment.

Additional Requirements:

 - Ability to work long hours and weekends as necessary to support critical milestones.

Location:

 - We are located in Torrance, CA in a 322,000 square foot, brand new facility featuring large open spaces for team collaboration, R&D, and production, as well as easy access to the 405, 105, and 110 freeways. Our facility is in the heart of Los Angeles' vibrant emerging tech ecosystem alongside many other high growth startups and enterprises.





Culture

At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful:

 - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system

 - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle

 - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done”

 - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together

 - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption
   
   

Equal Opportunity

Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.




ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987.

jobs.title: Second Line Testing Sr. Analyst
jobs.location: Phoenix, Arizona, United States, San Francisco, California, United States
jobs.description:
Kikoff: The Fintech Powering Financial Security at Scale
Kikoff is a profitable, pre-IPO fintech company on a mission to empower everyone to achieve financial security. With record revenue growth in 2025 and a unicorn valuation, we've built a suite of products that help millions of people build credit, access liquidity, and save money.
We're scaling fast. Join us if you want to build something meaningful and help millions of people move forward financially.

Why Kikoff:

This is a consumer fintech startup, and you will be working with serial entrepreneurs who have built strong consumer brands and innovative products. We value extreme ownership, clear communication, a strong sense of craftsmanship, and the desire to create lasting work and work relationships. Yes, you can build an exciting business AND have real-life real-customer impact.

About the Role

Compliance at Kikoff has one job above all others: make sure we do what we say. Reporting to the Head of Compliance, you are how we know. This is a hands-on testing role supporting new products and growing volumes. You independently test whether the controls behind our consumer financial services and our BSA/AML program work in practice, and whether customers get the outcomes our obligations require.

Automation is how we keep pace: you will help build and run the AI tooling that handles routine testing, with human oversight built in, so your judgment goes where it matters most. Findings are the product of this role. We expect them to hold up, and we back them when they do.

What You'll Do

• Execute risk-based testing and monitoring reviews from scoping through remediation validation, including population definition, sampling, evidence, analysis, findings, and reporting.

• Perform second-line BSA/AML and sanctions monitoring, investigate what comes through, and support required regulatory reporting.

• Help build and run AI tooling with Legal, Compliance, and Engineering that sorts monitoring exceptions and handles routine tests, with human oversight built into the process: test it before relying on it, learn what it misses, and document how it is used so we can show an examiner or our bank partner how it is controlled.

• Translate regulatory obligations and customer-outcome risks into precise control questions, test procedures, and failure criteria, testing both whether a control is designed correctly and whether it operates that way in production.

• Test the controls across fair lending, FCRA and credit furnishing, UDAAP, Reg E, Reg Z, ECOA/Reg B, servicing and collections, privacy, and marketing review.

• Produce testing and monitoring reporting for Compliance leadership, our bank partner, and governance committees, and support regulatory examinations, bank partner reviews, and internal audit.

• Contribute to our testing methodology, templates, and quality standards as coverage expands with the business.

What We're Looking For

• 4+ years in compliance testing, monitoring, internal audit, or regulatory assurance in consumer financial services, at a bank, fintech, lender, servicer, or consultancy.

• You can turn a broad risk into a bounded, defensible review: a clear objective, population, evidence plan, test procedures, and a conclusion whose limits you state. You pull and reconcile your own populations, using SQL or a BI tool.

• Working knowledge of consumer protection regulation, with real depth in a few: UDAAP, FCRA, fair lending, Reg E, and Reg Z.

• BSA/AML and sanctions experience, including escalation review and investigation. You can write a narrative that a reviewer can follow without asking questions.

• You use AI in your own work and can say where you would trust it and where you would not.

Nice to Have

• Experience applying AI to real testing work, such as triaging exceptions, classifying populations, or automating a recurring test.

• Regulatory examination, bank partner review, or internal audit experience.

• Credit-building, credit reporting, lending, or earned wage access product experience.

• CRCM, CAMS, CIA, CISA, CPA, or a comparable qualification, and hands-on use of tools such as Amplitude, Jira, Notion, or a GRC platform.

If you meet most of this, we'd like to hear from you.

Compensation

Base salary is location-based and will be determined by factors including market location, experience, skills, and qualifications. In addition to competitive cash compensation, this role is eligible for equity and a comprehensive benefits package.

$100,000—$150,000 USD
