Quality Engineer – Connected Ecosystem

POSITION OVERVIEW

Quality Engineers on the Connected Ecosystem team are responsible for validating the integration of a wide variety of smart home devices within Alarm.com’s ecosystem. This role has a strong focus on functional testing of end‑to‑end systems and provides hands‑on exposure to the full product stack, including software, firmware, hardware, and networked systems.

This position is well‑suited for new graduates or early‑career Quality Engineers who are self‑starters, demonstrate a strong sense of ownership, and are eager to grow their technical skills. Successful candidates are strong problem solvers who are comfortable working with incomplete information, learning complex systems, and proactively identifying risk. You will be expected not only to execute tests, but to think critically about system behavior and drive quality improvements.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN THIS ROLE

• You take ownership of assigned features or systems and proactively identify quality risks

• You independently investigate issues, gather data, and propose next steps before escalating

• You produce clear, actionable test documentation and bug reports

• You continuously expand your technical understanding of the system under test

• You collaborate effectively with engineering, product, and other QA teams to drive quality forward

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Develop a strong understanding of product functionality, system architecture, and data flow

• Write, execute, and maintain test plans, test cases, and supporting documentation

• Perform manual end‑to‑end testing across hardware, firmware, software, and network components

• Identify, log, track, and follow defects through resolution

• Write high‑quality, detailed, and reproducible bug reports

• Analyze logs, metrics, and system data to troubleshoot and identify root causes

• Set up, configure, and maintain test environments, devices, and equipment

• Triage urgent or high‑impact issues, prioritize appropriately, and propose solutions

• Configure, maintain, and monitor test automation setups where applicable

• Assess risk and determine appropriate test strategy based on system complexity and impact

• Collaborate closely with developers, product managers, and other engineering teams

• Continuously look for opportunities to improve test coverage, tooling, and processes

• Other duties as assigned

REQUIREMENTS

Required

• 0–3 years of Quality Assurance or related technical experience

• B.A. or B.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Computer Science, or relevant discipline

• Strong problem‑solving and analytical skills with a methodical approach to troubleshooting

• Demonstrated technical aptitude and ability to learn new systems quickly

• Ability to work across hardware, software, and networked systems

• Comfort working with incomplete information and ambiguous problems

• Strong attention to detail and a process‑oriented mindset

• Self‑motivated with a demonstrated sense of ownership and accountability

• Strong written and verbal communication skills

• Team‑oriented mindset with the ability to collaborate effectively

Nice to Have

• Exposure to test automation frameworks or tools

• Familiarity with at least one programming or scripting language (e.g., Python, Java, JavaScript, C#, etc.)

• Experience analyzing logs, system data, or network traffic

• Exposure to IoT, embedded, or distributed systems

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer
jobs.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



The Role

Hadrian is building an AI-powered operating system for the factory: one integrated platform for how we engineer and build critical parts for aerospace and defense. As one of Hadrian's first product designers, you will work with key internal customers across engineering and factory operations. You will design the tools and automations that make our product lifecycle faster, and shape experiences that connect work across teams from end to end.

You will report to the Product Design Lead and work from Los Angeles.



What You'll Do

 - Partner with key internal customers across engineering and factory operations, and learn their workflows firsthand.

 - Design the tools and automations at the core of Hadrian's AI-powered factory operating system.

 - See how work moves across teams and functions, and design experiences that carry it from end to end.

 - Define the problem, design in Figma, and ship the first working version in code with coding agents such as Claude Code.

 - Work with engineers to take your work to production, and measure how it changes the way the factory runs.

What We're Looking For

 - A record of solving complex customer problems: you can show the customer, the problem, and the measured result.

 - Shipped features and products that customers adopted and that moved the business.

 - Experience shipping high-stakes features at scale.

 - Systems thinking: you design for the whole workflow, across teams and functions.

 - Senior or staff-level product design experience, equivalent to Meta IC5 to IC6, with high taste and a high degree of craft in Figma and in code.

What Will Set You Apart

 - You have designed software for industrial, operational, or high-precision work, where the product runs something physical.

 - You have designed AI-powered products or agent-driven workflows that people rely on every day.

 - You prototype in production code and ship it.

 - You are passionate about the mission to reindustrialize American manufacturing, and want your work to shape how the country builds rockets, satellites, jets, and ships.

A manufacturing background is not required.

jobs.title: Model Risk Manager
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
About the role:

Mercury is looking for a Model Risk Manager to help build and operate a practical, risk-based Model Risk Management program as we continue to scale and prepare for life as a regulated bank.

Models support an increasingly broad range of decisions across Mercury, including credit underwriting, portfolio management, fraud prevention, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational processes. This role will provide independent review and effective challenge throughout the model lifecycle while helping Mercury apply governance proportionate to the actual risk of each model.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can move comfortably between technical analysis, regulatory expectations, and business context. You will conduct model validations, challenge assumptions and limitations, improve our model inventory and monitoring practices, and work closely with teams across Risk Ops, Data, Engineering, Product, Finance, Compliance, and Internal Audit.

Showing up as a true collaborator, advisor and partner to the business will be key as we continue to build out this function and work towards our collective goals at Mercury. You should be comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where the objective is not governance for its own sake, but helping Mercury use models safely, responsibly, and effectively.

What you’ll do:

• Perform independent validations and reviews of internally developed and third-party models across areas such as credit, fraud, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational risk.

• Evaluate each model’s methodology, assumptions, data quality and lineage, implementation, and performance through reviews and testings such as outcomes analysis, benchmarking, back-testing, and sensitivity testing scaled to its risk and materiality.

• Provide credible and constructive challenges to model developers, owners, and users while maintaining effective working relationships with 1LOD.

• Assess model risk and materiality based on a model’s inherent risk, purpose, exposure, use, and potential impact.

• Help maintain a complete and accurate model inventory, including model ownership, risk rating, dependencies, limitations, validation status, monitoring requirements, and open issues.

• Review ongoing monitoring plans and results, including performance thresholds, overrides, data drift, model changes, and conditions that could make a model no longer fit for purpose.

• Evaluate vendor models and other third-party analytical products, including available documentation, transparency, performance, limitations, customization, and Mercury’s ability to monitor and control their use.

• Document validation conclusions clearly, identify issues, recommend proportionate remediation, and track findings through resolution.

• Support controlled model use when validation cannot be completed before implementation by helping establish appropriate limitations, compensating controls, monitoring, and approvals.

• Develop clear reporting on model risk, validation coverage, performance concerns, concentrations, dependencies, exceptions, and overdue remediation for management and governance committees.

• Help improve Mercury’s Model Risk Management Policy, standards, procedures, and templates.

• Use automation and analytical tools to make model inventory management, testing, monitoring, and reporting more efficient.

• Partner with Mercury’s Data and AI Governance teams to establish clear boundaries and handoffs between traditional model risk management and the governance of generative AI, agentic AI, and other analytical systems outside the formal model definition.

• Support regulatory examinations, Internal Audit reviews, and other assurance activities involving model risk.

What we’re looking for:

• 5+ years of relevant experience in model validation, model development, quantitative risk analytics, or a related discipline within banking, fintech, financial services, or consulting.

• Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Engineering, Financial Engineering or a related field. Master’s degree or PhD is preferred.

• Strong knowledge of model risk management principles and current regulatory expectations, including the revised interagency guidance reflected in SR 26-2.

• Intensive experience validating or developing models in one or more areas such as BSA/AML, fraud, financial forecasting, CECL, capital, liquidity, and credit underwriting, using one or more methodologies such as machine learning (e.g., XGBoost, random forests), scorecards, complex vendor models (e.g., Alloy, Firco), and complex spreadsheet-based models.

• Proficiency with SQL and Python (from a data analytics lens); comfortable building understanding of models independently of their developers through collecting evidence and data analytics.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can explain model risk to a data scientist and to a regulator, or translate your findings and recommendations to guidance for the 1LOD product/business teams, and use different language for each.

• Exceptional attention to detail across documentation, code base, testing artifacts and quantitative analysis provided by 1LOD.

• Sound judgment and a practical, risk-based mindset: you can distinguish significant model risk from lower-risk matters and have the confidence to challenge model owners constructively, including senior stakeholders.

• High ownership, intellectual curiosity, and comfort building processes in a fast evolving environment, where priorities evolve quickly, new ad hoc requests emerge regularly, and role boundaries are intentionally broad. You can operate effectively without tightly-defined scope, find the highest-leverage work, and get it done.

Preferred qualifications:

• Experience helping build or materially enhance a model risk management program.

• Familiarity with bank regulatory examinations, charter readiness, or the implementation of risk programs within a growing financial institution.

• Knowledge of Haskell

What success looks like:

• Mercury maintains a complete and reliable view of its material models and aggregate model risk.

• Critical models receive timely, technically credible, and risk-based independent review.

• Model limitations, performance concerns, and remediation needs are clearly understood and acted upon.

• Model owners view Model Risk as a rigorous and constructive partner that improves decisions without creating unnecessary friction.

• Mercury’s Model Risk Management program is scalable, practical, and ready to withstand regulatory and independent assurance review.

*Mercury is a financial technology company, not a bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group, Column N.A., and Evolve Bank & Trust, Members FDIC.

Mercury values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All individuals seeking employment at Mercury are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities or special needs. jobs.title: Cleared IT Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:
Quindar builds modern, cloud-native satellite mission operations software with a simple mission: to operate satellites like servers. Our platform replaces fragmented, legacy ground systems with an integrated, automation-driven approach that brings modern software velocity to space operations.  

We're a small, fast-moving team with deep aerospace and software roots, energized by big challenges and motivated by the impact we have on real missions in this next chapter of the Space Age. If you want to work with sharp, ambitious people who push boundaries, move quickly, and are excited to take space operations to the next level, Quindar is the place to do it.

What You'll Be Doing

Quindar is building and operating classified environments to support mission partners across the U.S. government. We are seeking an IT Infrastructure Engineer to own the systems that keep those environments secure, reliable, and ready for mission operations.

This is a broad, hands-on infrastructure role. You will administer Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) and Windows Server systems, Kubernetes environments, virtualized infrastructure, storage, backups, and core network services. Working closely with our ISSM, Facility Security Officer, and engineering teams, you will implement security controls, support accreditation activities, and maintain compliant operations in classified spaces.

You Will:

 •  Deploy, configure, patch, harden, and troubleshoot RHEL and Windows Server systems.

 •  Build and maintain virtualization, Kubernetes, storage, backup, and recovery systems            for mission-critical workloads.

 •  Manage access controls, monitor system health, review logs, and remediate                             vulnerabilities.

 •  Support security assessments, accreditation documentation, remediation plans, and             continuous monitoring.

 •  Automate repeatable administration tasks and improve alerting and operational                    procedures.

 •  Diagnose issues across servers, storage, networking, and applications, including                     occasional scheduled maintenance or after-hours support.

Qualifications

Required

•  5+ years of experience administering IT infrastructure in an enterprise or government           environment.

•  Current, active U.S. Government Secret clearance or higher, with the ability to maintain it.

•  Strong hands-on experience with RHEL, including installation, configuration, patching,          troubleshooting, and security hardening.

•  Experience administering Windows Server and Kubernetes environments.

•  Experience operating virtualized infrastructure, enterprise storage, and backup and               recovery systems.

•  Experience applying security and compliance requirements in a classified environment.

•  Familiarity with applicable Risk Management Framework processes, NIST security                  controls, and DISA STIGs.

•  Working knowledge of networking, identity and access management, monitoring, and          incident response.

•  Ability to document systems clearly, resolve problems independently, and own                       infrastructure from deployment through ongoing operations.

Preferred

 •  Eligibility for SCI access or experience supporting systems in a SCIF.

 •  Experience designing infrastructure for high availability and tested recovery.

 •  Experience automating infrastructure administration and configuration.

 •  Familiarity with classified network connectivity and the operational requirements of              SIPRNet or JWICS.

 • Experience preparing accreditation evidence, remediating findings, and supporting                audits or inspections.

What Success Looks Like

 - Classified infrastructure is secure, reliable, documented, and ready to support mission operations.

 - Servers and Kubernetes environments are consistently configured, patched, monitored, and maintained.

 - Virtualization, storage, and backup systems meet workload needs, with recovery procedures that have been tested.

 - Security findings are addressed promptly, and compliance evidence is easy to produce.

 - Engineers and mission operators can depend on the infrastructure and get fast help when issues arise.

ITAR Requirements

 - To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.



Why You'll Love Working at Quindar

 - We work in a cutting-edge industry, and you'll be part of a small team with a direct impact on our customers' space missions.

 - We take work-life balance seriously. We require employees to take 15 days off, provide unlimited PTO, and observe most U.S. federal holidays.

 - We provide quarterly health and wellness benefits, comprehensive health insurance with 100% coverage for employees and a 4% 401(k) match.

 - Each year, we gather for a four-day company offsite. Previous locations include San Francisco, Nashville, Denver, Santa Fe, New Orleans, San Diego, Bozeman, and New York City.

 - Our culture and company are evolving. You'll help shape what comes next.

jobs.title: Aircraft Maintenance Expeditor
jobs.description:
Stratolaunch is a technology accelerator that engineers operationally realistic testing at Mach 5+. Our air-launched, Talon testbeds are reusable, cost-effective platforms that enable routine access to the hypersonic environment. We deliver flight data critical to validating system performance and achieving rapid technology deployment. Together with our customers, we drive innovations that are imperative to advancing national security.

Stratolaunch is seeking a hands-on a Maintenance Expeditor to help the aircraft maintenance team in the efficient execution of the work scope performed to the aircraft; maintenance, preventive maintenance, inspections, and alterations. This role demands a highly organized and proactive contributor with attention to detail, a commitment to support the maintenance team, and support  our growing aerospace maintenance and flight-test operations. This role will support maintenance personnel in the achievement of shared team and company goals, with demonstrated professionalism, integrity, and credibility.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

• The Expeditor is responsible for coordinating the parts, materials, tooling, equipment, maintenance kits, and work instructions required to support aircraft maintenance operations

• Work with Maintenance Planning, Maintenance Control, Materials, Procurement, Quality, Crew and Mechanics to ensure maintenance teams have the required, documentation and kitted parts available when needed.

• Coordinate with Maintenance control on availability of current and applicable maintenance work instructions, task cards, engineering instructions, drawings, and technical documentation.

• Support preparation and organization of maintenance work packages.

• Review upcoming maintenance requirements and identify required parts, materials, consumables, and supplies.

• Track parts from request through procurement, receiving, inspection, availability, and delivery to the maintenance team.

• Monitor shortages, backorders, delayed shipments, and other material constraints.

• Coordinate with Materials, Procurement, suppliers, and internal stakeholders to expedite critical requirements.

• Support the preparation and staging of maintenance kits.

• Verify kits contain the required parts, quantities, consumables, tooling requirements, and applicable documentation.

• Track kit status and communicate incomplete or delayed kits.

• Coordinate delivery of completed kits to the appropriate aircraft or maintenance work area.

• Maintain visibility of priority and long-lead material requirements.

• Escalate material issues that could affect maintenance or flight-test schedules.

• Support urgent/AOG material requirements when necessary.

• Verify parts and materials are available prior to scheduled maintenance activities.

• Coordinate with Tool Control, Maintenance, Quality, and other support organizations to resolve tooling issues.

• 2+ years of experience in aviation, aerospace, aircraft maintenance, materials, logistics, supply chain, manufacturing, or a related technical environment.

• Strong organizational and follow-up skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.

• Ability to read and understand technical documentation, work instructions, drawings, and parts information.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Outlook.

• Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities.

• Ability to identify problems, establish priorities, and drive issues toward resolution.

• Ability to work effectively with mechanics, engineers, supervisors, suppliers, and leadership.

• The ideal candidate is a strong communicator and problem solver who can manage multiple priorities, identify potential delays early, and aggressively follow issues through to resolution.

• Proficient knowledge of MS Office (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint)

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

• Aircraft maintenance, flight-test, or production experience.

• Familiarity with aircraft parts, tooling, consumables, and maintenance processes.

• Experience with maintenance kitting, inventory systems and work-package preparation.

• Familiarity with aircraft configuration control and controlled technical documentation.

• Aviation or aerospace maintenance experience preferred.

Special remarks regarding work environment, if applicable

Benefits and our location(s):

jobs.title: Enterprise Sales Lead - Healthcare
jobs.description:
ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

As Enterprise Sales Lead - Healthcare, you’ll own our North America enterprise motion across providers, payers, and life sciences, helping health organizations put agents in front of patients, members, and clinicians that are safe, fast, and fit the systems they already run.

In regulated industries, relationships are the currency, so we’re looking for a leader who already knows the buyers and the rulebook. You’ll have the mandate to win net-new logos, drive agent sales, and build the playbook and the team.

In this role, you will:

 - Win net-new logos and drive adoption of ElevenLabs, including closing deals yourself and also building and scaling the team

 - Own the enterprise healthcare function across health systems, payers, and pharma/medtech: strategy, pipeline, forecast, process, execution

 - Define the enterprise ICP, sales methodology, and a repeatable motion for each segment

 - Land and expand with large health systems, health plans, and life sciences companies

 - Open doors through your own network of senior buyers, and turn early wins into the references the rest of the vertical will call

 - Work through BAAs, security review, and AI governance boards (and MLR review for pharma), starting compliance conversations in week one

 - Partner with our Forward Deployed Engineers to scope integrations with the EHR, claims, and telephony systems customers already run

 - Help customers pick one high-volume starting point (scheduling, reminders, after-hours coverage, benefits and claims status, HCP support) and prove it before scaling

 - Build a reference network of healthcare peers that buyers can call

 - Lead executive briefings, events, and high-stakes negotiations

 - Bring a sharp view of the competitive landscape, including build-vs-buy, platform bundlers, and vertical point solutions, to positioning and strategy

 - Set the bar for sales culture, integrity, and customer-first execution

Requirements:

 - 10+ years of enterprise sales experience, including at least 2 years leading a team.

 - Track record selling into health systems, payers, or life sciences, with deep fluency in HIPAA, BAAs, AI governance, and long, multi-stakeholder cycles

 - An established network of senior decision-makers in one or more of health systems, payers, or life sciences, so you can name the buyers you’d call in your first 30 days

 - Experience building a new sales motion or playbook from scratch, whether as a founding leader or inside a larger company

 - Passion for experimenting to find the positioning and messaging that wins in market, and turn what works into the playbook

 - Seven-figure enterprise deals and complex sales cycles

 - Ability to be strategic and hands-on at once

 - Executive presence at C-suite and board levels

 - Low ego and hands-on: equally at home in a C-suite briefing and in the weeds of a prospecting list or Proof of Value. Motivated by impact and growth more than title

 - Passion for the transformative potential of voice and conversational AI
   
   

Location
 This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in the United States, however the ability to operate in EST, CST, or PST timezones is required. There is a preference for candidates to be based in New York or San Francisco, with the option to work out of our office.

jobs.title: Program Scheduler
jobs.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

Role Overview:

We are seeking an experienced Program Scheduler will develop, maintain, and analyze Integrated Master Schedules (IMS) supporting Massed Modular Aircraft program across all lifecycle phases — from concept/development and design through qualification, production, fielding, and in-service/sustainment support. This role will support both U.S. government/defense contracts and commercial customer agreements, requiring familiarity with the differing scheduling rigor, reporting requirements, and contractual drivers of each. The ideal candidate partners closely with Program Management, Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Finance to build realistic, resource-loaded, risk-informed schedules and to proactively identify and communicate schedule risk before it impacts program execution.

Responsibilities:

• Develop and maintain Integrated Master Schedules (IMS) and Integrated Master Plans (IMP) across all program phases: development/design, test and qualification, production, delivery, and in-service/sustainment support.

• Build resource-loaded, logic-driven schedules with clearly defined critical path(s), key milestones, and deliverable dependencies.

• Integrate engineering, manufacturing, test, supply chain, and quality inputs into a single, coherent program schedule baseline.

• Maintain schedule baselines and manage baseline change control in accordance with program and corporate schedule management procedures.

• Perform critical path analysis, schedule margin/float analysis, and schedule risk assessment (e.g., Monte Carlo/schedule risk analysis) to identify and quantify risk to key milestones.

• Conduct schedule health checks (e.g., DCMA 14-point assessment) to ensure schedule quality, logic integrity, and compliance with contractual and corporate standards.

• Identify schedule variances, root causes, and recovery/workaround options; communicate impacts clearly to program leadership.

• Support Integrated Baseline Reviews (IBRs), Program Management Reviews (PMRs), and Milestone/Gate reviews with schedule status, analysis, and risk input.

• Tailor scheduling approach and reporting cadence/format to the requirements of the applicable contract framework — including EVM-compliant scheduling for cost-type/FAR-based government contracts and more streamlined milestone-based scheduling for commercial or fixed-price agreements.

• Support development of contractually required schedule deliverables (e.g., IMS/IMP submittals, Contract Data Requirements List/CDRL schedule products) for government programs.

• Support customer schedule reviews and data calls, including potential international/Foreign Military Sales (FMS) or Direct Commercial Sales (DCS) customer engagements.

• Partner with Financial Analysts to integrate schedule and cost performance data for EAC development and variance analysis.

• Work with Supply Chain to incorporate supplier and long-lead procurement schedules into the program-level IMS.

• Coordinate with Engineering and Manufacturing on technical baseline changes and their schedule impacts.

• Support proposal scheduling, including development of Basis of Estimate (BOE) schedules and schedule risk inputs for new business pursuits.

• Maintain and administer scheduling software/tools (e.g., Microsoft Project, Oracle Primavera P6, or equivalent) and integration with cost/EVM tools.

• Prepare schedule status reports, dashboards, and metrics (e.g., schedule performance index/SPI, milestone trend charts) for internal and customer reporting.

• Maintain schedule documentation and audit trail supporting government and internal reviews.

Minimum Requirements:

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, Project Management or a related technical field

• Minimum 5 years of program scheduling experience, with direct exposure to defense/aerospace industry

• Proficiency with scheduling tools such as Oracle Primavera P6 and/or Microsoft Project.

• Working knowledge of Earned Value Management (EVM) principles and EIA-748 EVMS guidelines.

• Experience developing and maintaining Integrated Master Schedules (IMS) across full program lifecycle — development through production and in-service/sustainment support.

• Exposure to both defense (EVM/FAR-based) and commercial customer scheduling frameworks.

• Familiarity with DCMA 14-point schedule assessment and schedule risk analysis (SRA)/Monte Carlo tools (e.g., Acumen Fuse, Safran Risk).

• Experience supporting Integrated Baseline Reviews (IBRs) and formal government program reviews.

Preferred Requirements:

• PMI Scheduling Professional (PMI-SP) or similar certification

• Ability to obtain/maintain Secret/Top Secret/SCI clearance

Why CHAOS?

• Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company

• Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more

• Our Perks: Free daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code

• Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses

• Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices

Salary Range: $165,000 - $275,000

The stated compensation range reflects only the targeted base compensation range and excludes additional earnings such as bonus, equity, and benefits. If your compensation requirements fall outside of the range, we still encourage you to apply. The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations.

Recruiting Agencies: CHAOS Industries does not accept unsolicited resumes or outreach. Unsolicited submissions will not be reviewed or compensated.

jobs.title: Director, Customer Operations-Walmart
jobs.description:
BUILT ON FLAVOR.  FUELED BY PEOPLE.

What’s it like to work at Kinder’s? Well, there’s a lot of snacking and geeking out over what we all cooked over the weekend. Beyond that, there’s also plenty of hard work. Because we don’t just like flavor, we’re obsessed with it.

With over 100 products sold nationwide, we’re now a top-five brand in multiple flavor categories at Costco, Walmart, Whole Foods, and more. We’re not your typical CPG company. Privately held and founder-led, we like to think of ourselves as a pirate ship in a sea of cruise ships. Our crew is adventurous and fearless. We chart our own course and chase big ideas to make food unforgettable.

As we expand globally and approach $1 billion in revenue, we need more smart-and-scrappy, flavor-obsessed people to come aboard. If you’re looking for a place where you can see the real impact of your work... this is it! Every day, you’ll be part of a journey to add flavor to millions of meals and lives.

About The Role

Kinder's is seeking an experienced Director, Customer Operations who is passionate about building world-class customer operations while leading high-performing teams that deliver exceptional service to our retail partners. This leader will oversee Customer Operations across our largest strategic accounts while driving operational excellence across logistics, warehousing, customer service, and order fulfillment.

We are a fast-growing company working hard to bring amazing flavor solutions that are as exciting and delicious as they are simple to use to our consumers whether they are experienced cooks or first-timers in the kitchen. We are obsessed with quality and are 100% committed to being the most innovative company in any market we serve. Our mission is to bring awesome flavor to consumers whenever and wherever they are looking for it and whatever they are looking for it in (seasonings, sauces, gravy, marinades, or anything else we can come up with). We have experienced tremendous growth over the last 5 years, but we think we are just getting started. We love our consumers and are fired up to be part of their flavor journey. And we need more great folks to help us continue to raise the bar for what they think is even possible in their own kitchens.

Today, we have over 100 products sold nationwide at retailers including Costco, Walmart, Sam's Club, Whole Foods, Sprouts, Kroger, Safeway and many more. While we have been around for over 75 years, we have experienced explosive growth in the last 5 years and are now a top 5 brand in the U.S. in multiple flavor categories including seasoning blends, BBQ sauce, and wing sauce. To keep our momentum rolling, we need more passionate flavor advocates and builders to come join our team and help us reach every kitchen across the U.S. and beyond.

How You'll Have an Impact at Kinder's

As the Director, Customer Operations, you will lead the Customer Operations organization responsible for Walmart, Sam’s Club, and future strategic retail customers while overseeing the operational partnership with Logistics and Warehousing. Reporting directly to the SR. Director, Customer Operations & Logistics/Warehousing, this role is responsible for creating scalable processes, driving service excellence, improving supply chain performance, and leading a team focused on delivering best-in-class customer execution.

You will serve as the operational leader connecting Sales, Supply Chain, Planning, Logistics, Finance, Customer Service, Warehousing, and external partners to ensure flawless execution from order placement through customer delivery. This leader will own strategic customer operations initiatives, identify opportunities to improve efficiency and profitability, and build organizational capabilities that support Kinder’s continued growth.

Key Responsibilities

Customer Operations Leadership

• Lead and develop the Customer Operations organization supporting Walmart, Sam's Club, and future strategic retail customers.

• Directly manage Customer Operations Managers for Wal-Mart Corp and support clear goals, performance expectations, and development plans.

• Build scalable customer service and order management processes that support continued business growth.

• Partner as executive escalation point for complex customer service and operational issues.

• Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Logistics & Warehousing Partnership

• Partner closely with the VP Customer Operations & Logistics/Warehousing to optimize transportation, warehousing, inventory flow, and customer fulfillment.

• Drive strategic improvements with 3PL providers and warehouse partners to improve service levels and reduce costs.

• Monitor operational KPIs including OTIF, fill rate, inventory health, warehouse productivity, and customer scorecards.

• Develop contingency plans to minimize customer disruption during supply chain challenges.

Customer Strategy & Operational Excellence

• Develop operational strategies that support customer growth while improving execution efficiency.

• Partner with Sales Leadership on customer business planning, promotional execution, modular transitions, and new item launches.

• Ensure forecasting, replenishment, inventory management, and order fulfillment processes are aligned across functions.

• Lead cross-functional initiatives to improve customer service metrics, inventory optimization, and order accuracy.

• Standardize SOPs, reporting, scorecards, and best practices across Customer Operations.

Business Performance & Analytics

• Establish operational dashboards that provide visibility into customer performance and supply chain execution.

• Analyze trends, identify operational risks, and develop action plans to improve service performance.

• Present operational performance, business insights, and strategic recommendations to Executive Leadership.

• Drive continuous improvement initiatives utilizing data, analytics, and KPI performance.

Cross Functional Leadership

• Partner closely with Sales, Demand Planning, Supply Planning, Finance, Procurement, Customer Care, IT, and Commercial teams.

• Lead weekly cross-functional operational reviews.

• Champion operational readiness for customer initiatives including seasonal programs, product launches, promotions, and supply transitions.

• Ensure alignment between commercial objectives and operational execution.

Process Improvement & Organizational Development

• Identify opportunities to automate manual processes and improve operational efficiency.

• Develop organizational capabilities that support future growth.

• Mentor and develop emerging leaders within Customer Operations.

• Lead change management initiatives across Operations and Customer Service functions.

• Build a high-performance culture focused on collaboration, accountability, and continuous learning.

What You Bring to the Table

• 10+ years of progressive experience in Customer Operations, Supply Chain, Customer Service, Logistics, or Operations leadership within Consumer Packaged Goods preferably with Walmart Corp background.

• Minimum 5 years leading managers and cross-functional teams.

• Strong experience supporting large national retailers including Walmart and Sam's Club.

• Deep understanding of retail replenishment, customer operations, order management, logistics, warehousing, and inventory management.

• Proven ability to lead organizational change and process improvement initiatives.

• Experience working with 3PL providers, transportation partners, and warehouse operations.

• Demonstrated success leading cross-functional initiatives across Sales, Operations, Finance, and Supply Chain.

• Strong analytical and financial acumen with experience utilizing operational KPIs to drive business decisions.

• Exceptional executive communication and presentation skills.

• Proven ability to influence without direct authority across multiple functional teams.

• Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills; SAP experience preferred.

• Experience with Walmart Luminate, Retail Link, NOVA, or similar retailer systems preferred.

• Bachelor's degree required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

Leadership Competencies

• Strategic Thinking

• Customer Obsession

• Operational Excellence

• Talent Development

• Executive Presence

• Change Leadership

• Continuous Improvement Mindset

• Collaboration & Influence

• Data-Driven Decision Making

• Results Orientation

Location and Travel

The position will be based out of our Bentonville, AR office with monthly travel to our Walnut Creek, CA headquarters and periodic travel to distribution centers, 3PL partners, customer headquarters, and other Kinder's locations. We strongly believe in the power of culture and community and have a hybrid work structure with three days in the office each week to encourage collaboration, innovation, and stronger partnerships across the organization.

Pay Transparency

The expected starting salary range for this role is $215,000- $240,000 per year. The salary range posted for this role reflects the good-faith base pay range Kinder’s reasonably expects to offer at the time of posting and may vary based on the location of the role. Individual compensation within the posted range will be determined based on factors such as relevant education, experience, qualifications, skills, and business needs.

SEASONED FOR SUCCESS:

• No two days here are the same.

• We try to be good team members and good communicators, but we don’t live by hierarchy and structure – everyone is a difference maker here.

• We make a lot of decisions in the face of incomplete information – our team embraces ambiguity and tries to make good decisions fast rather than great decisions slow.

• We believe our job is to take smart risk, not to eliminate risk.

• We believe in growing our skills and becoming a better company with more managerial expertise, but we are an entrepreneurial company at heart.

• We aren’t trying to be average – we want to do exceptional things, and we are willing to work hard to achieve them.

BENEFITS THAT BRING MORE TO THE TABLE:

We offer a range of total rewards that may include paid time off, 401k, bonus / incentive eligibility, equity grants, competitive health benefits, and other family-friendly benefits, including parental leave. Kinder’s benefits vary based on eligibility and can be reviewed in more detail during the interview process.

OUR RECIPE FOR BALANCE:

We believe great culture starts with people. We’re a people-first company built on connection, collaboration, and balance. Most of our work happens in the office to spark creativity and community, but we also offer flexibility so team members have the autonomy to work outside the office when needed to support their work-life balance and personal commitments.

WHERE EVERY INGREDIENT MATTERS:

Kinder's is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, gender, citizenship, marital status, religion, age, disability, gender identity, results of genetic testing, veteran status, as well as any other legally-protected characteristic. If you have a disability under the Americans with Disabilities Act or similar law, and you need any accommodation during the application process or to perform these job requirements, please reach out to us at careers@kinders.com

jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

insitro is a physical AI company dedicated to unlocking causal human biology and accelerating the delivery of better medicines to patients. Our unique Virtual Human™ platform identifies novel, high-impact genetic intervention points, which our TherML™ platform translates into therapeutics—whether small molecules, biologics, or oligos. With multiple programs in metabolic disease and neuroscience advancing toward the clinic, and our first IND submission slated for the second half of this year, we are at a pivotal inflection point.

insitro's success depends on attracting and developing exceptional talent across a wide range of high-demand disciplines. We're looking for a highly organized Recruiting Coordinator to join us on a 3-month contract, with the option to extend, and coordinate a high volume of recruiting activity as we build world-class teams. This is a highly visible role with frequent interaction with senior leadership across the company.

Based in South San Francisco, this position reports directly to the Director of Talent Acquisition & Workforce Strategy, with day-to-day management by the Recruiting Operations Specialist. It offers an in-person hybrid schedule of two to three days per week on average, flexing up to five days based on onsite interview volume and business need.




RESPONSIBILITIES

Candidate Experience & Coordination

 - Interview Scheduling: Own end-to-end interview scheduling and related meetings, including debriefs, for a high volume of candidates across teams and levels.

 - Onsite Logistics: Manage candidate meetings from start to finish, whether they happen at headquarters or offsite.

 - Travel & Reimbursements: Coordinate candidate travel and process expense reimbursements quickly and accurately.

 - Seamless Experience: Ensure every candidate feels supported and informed at every step of the process.



Recruiting Operations & Partnership

 - ATS Ownership: Track candidate progress in Ashby from first contact through offer, maintaining the team's data integrity.

 - Tools Expert: Become a subject matter expert on Recruiting Operations tools, processes, and tech stack.

 - Process Documentation: Document standard operating procedures so the team runs consistently and efficiently.

 - Go-To Partner: Build strong relationships with hiring managers and selection teams, helping them solve day-to-day needs.




ABOUT YOU

Experience & Qualifications

 - Proven Tenure: 2+ years of experience as a Recruiting Coordinator.

 - High-Volume Scheduling: Experience managing multiple interview events on a calendar at the same time.

 - Executive Coordination: Experience scheduling executive-level interviews in partnership with Executive Assistants.

 - Recruiting Tech: Hands-on experience with an ATS such as Ashby, Greenhouse, or Lever, plus tools like scheduling assistants, JD builders, or data visualization platforms.

 - Spreadsheet Skills: Working knowledge of Excel or Google Sheets.

 - AI Fluency: Comfortable using AI tools such as Claude in your daily work.



Core Competencies

 - Highly Organized: You keep many moving pieces on track without letting details slip.

 - Solution-Oriented: You bring a "can-do," "let's find a solution" mindset to every request.

 - Poised with Leadership: You're comfortable in a visible role that works closely with senior leaders across the company.

 - Discreet & Trustworthy: You handle sensitive and confidential information with professionalism and sound judgment.



Compensation & Benefits at insitro

Our target starting salary for successful US-based applicants for this role is $46 - $50/hr. To determine starting pay, we consider multiple job-related factors including a candidate's skills, education and experience, market demand, business needs, and internal parity. We may also adjust this range in the future based on market data.



In addition, insitro also provides our contract employees:

 - Excellent medical, dental, and vision coverage as well as mental health and well-being support

 - Access to free onsite baristas and cafe with daily lunch and breakfast for employees who are either onsite or hybrid



insitro is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

We believe diversity, equity, and inclusion need to be at the foundation of our culture. We work hard to bring together diverse teams–grounded in a wide range of expertise and life experiences–and work even harder to ensure those teams thrive in inclusive, growth-oriented environments supported by equitable company and team practices. All candidates can expect equitable treatment, respect, and fairness throughout the interview process.

 

About insitro

insitro is a drug discovery and development company using machine learning (ML) and data at scale to decode biology for transformative medicines. At the core of insitro’s approach is the convergence of in-house generated multi-modal cellular data and high-content phenotypic human cohort data. We rely on these data to develop ML-driven, predictive disease models that uncover underlying biologic state and elucidate critical drivers of disease. These powerful models rely on extensive biological and computational infrastructure and allow insitro to advance novel targets and patient biomarkers, design therapeutics and inform clinical strategy. insitro is advancing a wholly owned and partnered pipeline of insights and therapeutics in neuroscience and metabolism. Since launching in 2018, insitro has raised over $700 million from top tech, biotech and crossover investors, and from collaborations with pharmaceutical partners. For more information on insitro, please visit www.insitro.com http://www.insitro.com.

jobs.title: Master Stratolaunch Job Template - Non-Engineering (Full Time)
jobs.description:
Stratolaunch is a technology accelerator that engineers operationally realistic testing at Mach 5+. Our air-launched, Talon testbeds are reusable, cost-effective platforms that enable routine access to the hypersonic environment. We deliver flight data critical to validating system performance and achieving rapid technology deployment. Together with our customers, we drive innovations that are imperative to advancing national security.

Stratolaunch is seeking a GSE Mechanic to maintain all operational ground support equipment supporting our carrier aircraft and hypersonic vehicles. This hands-on role performs scheduled and unscheduled maintenance and provides dependable equipment support during flight and ground-test operations. The mechanic coordinates equipment readiness and placement with Aircraft Maintenance, Flight Operations, Flight Test, Engineering, and program teams. Occasional mission travel is required.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

• Inspect, troubleshoot, repair, and test powered and non-powered GSE; perform scheduled and unscheduled maintenance.

• Maintain engines, electrical and charging systems, generators, hydraulics, pneumatics, brakes, drivetrains, steering, and cooling systems.

• Service ground power units, compressors, hydraulic carts, tow tractors, trailers, and other GSE using technical manuals and approved procedures.

• Stage, transport, connect, operate, monitor, disconnect, recover, and store GSE during flight and ground-test operations; verify compatibility and operating limits.

• Coordinate on-site equipment placement with Aircraft Maintenance, Flight Operations, Flight Test, Engineering, and program teams; report readiness and limitations.

• Perform pre-use, periodic, and post-use inspections; identify leaks, wear, damage, and hazards. Tag and remove unserviceable equipment from use.

• Use diagnostic tools, wiring diagrams, and schematics to isolate faults; verify repairs and document serviceability before release under company procedures.

• Operate company vehicles; tow and secure equipment using rated connections and spotters. Observe flight-line routes, clearances, speed limits, and exclusion areas.

• Maintain inspection and maintenance records, work orders, usage, parts, and discrepancy status; track service intervals and repeat defects.

• Apply flight-line safety, foreign object debris (FOD) control, tool control, lockout/tagout, and hazardous-material procedures; isolate stored energy and stop unsafe work.

• Keep work areas organized; control spills, fluids, batteries, and waste. Support mission deployments, shift turnovers, and other assigned duties with integrity.

QUALIFICATIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

REQUIRED

• 3+ years maintaining aviation GSE, gasoline or diesel fleet vehicles, industrial equipment, or comparable military equipment.

• Demonstrated troubleshooting and repair skills with gasoline and diesel engines, fuel and cooling systems, brakes, drivetrains, and steering.

• Ability to diagnose electrical systems and wiring, batteries, starting and charging systems, and generators using multimeters, load testers, and diagnostic equipment.

• Working knowledge of hydraulic and pneumatic pumps, compressors, valves, cylinders, hoses, pressure testing, contamination control, and safe depressurization.

• Ability to interpret technical manuals, wiring diagrams, schematics, and maintenance schedules; correctly use hand tools, torque tools, and calibrated test equipment.

• Experience performing inspections, preventive maintenance, and functional tests; accurate maintenance documentation and basic computer and work-order system skills.

• Knowledge of flight-line safety, FOD control, tool accountability, lockout/tagout, hazardous materials, safety data sheets, spill response, and safe lifting or jacking practices.

• Safe towing, load securement, and company vehicle operation skills; valid driver’s license, acceptable driving record, and ability to obtain required equipment authorizations.

• Ability to follow checklists, verify GSE output and interface requirements, recognize hazards, and communicate clearly by radio and during shift turnovers.

• Ability to work independently and across teams, prioritize changing needs, and report limitations; availability for flexible shifts, weekends, and occasional mission travel.

PREFERRED

• Aviation flight-line or flight-test GSE experience, including ground power, servicing equipment, and aircraft towing support.

• Welding and fabrication ability; safe use of welding and cutting equipment to build or repair components to approved requirements.

• Diesel, automotive, electrical, or industrial maintenance certifications; forklift, aerial lift, or computerized maintenance system experience.

EDUCATION

• High school diploma or equivalent required; related vocational, apprenticeship, or military technical training preferred.

Special remarks regarding work environment, if applicable

• This position is located in Mojave, CA. Shop, hangar, and flight-line work includes desert heat and cold, wind, dust, noise, exhaust, fuels, oils, and moving equipment.

• Must stand and walk for extended periods; bend, kneel, crouch, climb, reach, and work in restricted spaces; use tools and move items up to 50 pounds with lifting aids or team assistance as appropriate, with or without reasonable accommodation.

• Must use required PPE, communicate around operating equipment, and recognize gauges, indicators, markings, and hazards, with or without reasonable accommodation.

• 4/10 schedule

• 4-6 years experience: $31.00-$39.86

• 6+ years experience: $34.60-$45.85

Base salary and leveling are established on a case-by-case basis. We consider several factors to ensure a competitive offer, including your location, educational background, and a comprehensive assessment of the skills and experience demonstrated during your interviews.

Benefits and our location(s):

• Healthcare (medical, dental, vision, prescription drugs)

• Paid Maternity and Parental Leave

• 50% company match per contributed dollar into 401(k) savings plan, up to $11,500

• Tuition reimbursement

This position may involve the operation of company vehicles as part of assigned duties.

Not much for the outdoors and prefer the city life? You’re within a half day’s drive or less of Los Angeles, San Diego, Las Vegas, and San Francisco where you can find a variety of live entertainment, museums, tours, and historical sight-seeing. Theme parks are in abundance, with Six Flags Magic Mountain, Disneyland, and Knotts Berry Farm ready to meet the needs of rollercoaster thrill seekers.

jobs.title: Assembly Integration & Test Technician III - A Shift
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

ASSEMBLY INTEGRATION & TEST TECHNICIAN III

Based onsite at Rocket Lab's global headquarters in Long Beach, CA the AIT Technician II is responsible for performing spacecraft assembly, integration, and test activities while maintaining the highest standards of safety, quality, and workmanship. This role builds and integrates flight hardware by following engineering drawings, work instructions, and manufacturing procedures. The technician is expected to demonstrate proficiency in electrical and mechanical assembly techniques, contribute to a collaborative production environment, and support the successful delivery of spacecraft hardware.

Our ideal candidate has a strong manufacturing foundation, takes pride in workmanship, and is eager to expand their technical skills within a fast-paced aerospace production environment.

(Please note: this position can be hired at the Assembly Integration & Test Technician II or Assembly Integration & Test Technician III level)

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

• Assemble, integrate, and test spacecraft hardware in accordance with engineering drawings, work instructions, and quality standards.

• Install electrical and mechanical hardware including harnesses, avionics components, heaters, RTDs, brackets, connectors, and other flight hardware.

• Utilize electrical and mechanical assembly tools, measurement equipment, and calibrated tooling safely and effectively.

• Perform functional checks, continuity testing, insulation resistance testing, and other production verification activities as required.

• Support spacecraft functional testing, comprehensive performance testing (CPT), and environmental test campaigns as required.

• Support spacecraft propulsion integration activities including hardware installation, pressure testing, leak testing, and system verification in accordance with approved procedures.

• Support critical spacecraft lifts utilizing overhead cranes, mobile gantries, and approve lifting fixtures while adhering to established safety and handling procedures.

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS AS A AIT TECHNICIAN III:

• 5+ years of relevant manufacturing experience or demonstrated subject matter expertise, preferably in aerospace.

• Demonstrated technical leadership on complex spacecraft assembly, integration, and test campaigns.

• Experience performing advanced mechanical rework including drilling, tapping, precision alignment, and bonded repairs.

• Experience with spacecraft propulsion systems including pressure testing, leak testing, propellant handling, vacuum systems, or thrust stand operations.

• Experience integrating spacecraft subsystems such as solar arrays, propulsion systems, payloads, deployable mechanisms, or equivalent flight hardware.

• Experience performing critical spacecraft lifts utilizing overhead cranes, mobile gantries, and approved lifting fixtures.

• Ability to lead troubleshooting efforts involving multiple engineering disciplines.

• Ability to identify manufacturing risks and implement process improvements that improve safety, quality, cost, or schedule.

• Ability to interpret engineering intent when drawings or work instructions require clarification.

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• Current IPC-WHMA-A-620 certification.

• Current J-STD-001 certification.

• NCCCO Certified Rigger.

• Experience developing or improving manufacturing work instructions.

• Experience supporting MRB, NCR, RCCA, or 5-Why investigations.

• Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement training.

• Experience with SAP, MES, ERP, or other manufacturing execution systems.

• GD&T interpretation.

• Experience supporting design for manufacturability (DFM) reviews.

• Experience supporting customer inspections or mission-critical hardware reviews.

• Cross-functional expertise across multiple spacecraft subsystems including avionics, propulsion, structures, harnessing, environmental test, and spacecraft integration.

• Demonstrated ability to perform work safely while maintaining quality, workmanship, and configuration control.

• Ability to work effectively within a cross-functional production team.

• Recognized as a technical subject matter expert in one or more spacecraft assembly disciplines.

• Demonstrated ability to mentor technicians across multiple skill levels while driving workmanship excellence and continuous improvement.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

• Willing to work A Shift (Monday – Thursday 5:00am - 3:30pm)

• Stand and walk for entire shift (8+ hours) on various work surfaces

• Climb ladders and work at elevated height small spaces, awkward positions, and tight areas as needed

• Perform repetitive motions including bending, twisting, reaching, grasping, pushing, pulling, and stooping

• Use hands with precision to handle, control, and operate tools, instruments, and equipment

• Lift, carry, push, and pull materials and equipment up to 25 lbs.

• Work in varied environments including production floors, equipment areas, and field locations with exposure to noise, temperature variations, and moving machinery

• Flexibility to work extended hours, weekends, and varied shifts as operational needs require

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.

Eligibility for benefits may vary based on employment status, please check with your recruiter for a comprehensive list of the benefits available for this role. Benefit programs are subject to change at the company’s discretion.

Hourly Pay Range (CA Only)

$28—$35 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important information:

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here.

Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY:

For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant.  These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.

jobs.description:
Description:

The Senior Manager, Electrical Engineering owns people leadership, electrical/electronic system architecture, and technical strategy in the development of a novel surgical robotic platform. In this role, the Sr. Manager leads the team directly responsible for board design and FPGA-based development and is accountable for translating clinical and market requirements into a coherent, multi-year architecture and technology roadmap.

The successful candidate is both a proven people leader and a recognized subject matter expert who can set technical direction, make sound architectural trade-offs under time pressure and incomplete information, and build the leadership pipeline needed to sustain a high-performing organization.

This person partners closely with cross-functional leaders (Software, Mechanical, Systems, Quality/Regulatory, Manufacturing) to align electrical engineering strategy with business unit and corporate priorities, and to ensure programs meet Intuitive's quality system and FDA regulatory requirements throughout the medical device development lifecycle.

Essential Job Duties

This position has organizational responsibility for people leadership, electrical/electronic architecture, planning across robotic surgical systems. The Senior Manager, Electrical Engineering will:

• Provide people leadership across a team of PCBA and firmware (FPGA) designers,Own hiring, promotion, and performance decisions for the organization; build and develop a strong leadership pipeline of managers and technical leadsCoach and mentor managers and senior engineers; create an environment that supports attraction, retention, and successful long-term careers at IntuitiveSet individual and team development goals, and proactively address underperformance in a timely way
• Define and drive electrical/electronic system architecture and multi-year technology roadmaps for novel robotic surgical platforms:Work with cross-functional leaders to translate clinical and market requirements into high and low-level architecture and design strategyServe as a recognized subject matter expert, guiding architecture-level design trade-offs for embedded, FPGA-based, analog, and high-speed digital systems, including cross-functional mechanical and software requirements.Guide the team through design, implementation, verification, qualification, and transfer to manufacturing of complete robotic surgery designs, that include robotic servo control, vision processing, electrosurgical energy control, advanced compute and networking capabilities
• Independently establish objectives, schedules, budgets, and resource plans for the organization; negotiate resources and priorities with other functional and resource managers:Set team and departmental goals aligned to business unit strategy; anticipate interdependencies and avoid surprises through proactive planning and risk managementReport status, risks, and resource needs to senior management and cross-functional program leadership
• Ensure the organization's programs comply with Intuitive’s quality system and statutory requirements for medical device development:Oversee Design History File documentation, design controls (design input/output, traceability, risk analysis), and support for quality and regulatory processes across the team's programsEnsure compliance with 60601 standards, with early identification of issues through methodical dry runs and testing at the sub-system and system levelProvide engineering oversight for resolution issues at all phases of the product lifecycle: design, verification and validation testing, and field support
• Represent Electrical Engineering to senior leadership and cross-functional partners; tailor communication of complex technical topics to both technical and non-technical audiences
• Drive process improvement, best practices, and new methodologies within and beyond the immediate organization

Required Skills and Experience

• Proven track record leading and developing engineering managers as well as individual contributors, with strong commitment to team members' professional growth
• Demonstrated experience independently managing budgets and resource plans for a large engineering organization
• Recognized subject matter expertise in complex embedded and FPGA-based systems integrating digital, analog, and sensor technologies, gained in a fast-paced, high-transaction development environment
• Experience defining cohesive electrical system architectures that combine mechanical and computational requirements in a cohesive manner.
• Experience in defining and delivering on multi-year technical roadmaps for complex products,
• Skilled at leading cross-functional teams and with cross-organizational negotiation; strong project management capability
• Deep proficiency across the product development lifecycle - design, implementation, debug, verification, qualification, and transfer to manufacturingStrong understanding of design controls, design input/output, traceability, and risk analysis in a highly regulated industryExperience working with FDA and international regulatory requirements for medical device products
• Working knowledge of schematic capture and layout tools, electronic test equipment, analog and digital circuit design, embedded systems, high-speed digital transmission lines, and complex PCB material stackups
• Significant hardware development experience in a fast-paced, high-visibility environment, preferably in medical, surgical, or therapeutic products
• Understanding of component selection criteria, design for reliability, manufacturability, test, and EMC compliance
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to tailor messaging for senior leadership, cross-functional partners, and non-technical audiences

Required Education and Training

• BSc degree in Electrical Engineering or adjacent technical field with at least 10+ years of relevant experience (preferably in the medical device field), including at least 3 years as a people manager; or Master's degree with at least 8 years of experience; or PhD with at least 4 years of experience, in each case including at least 3 years as a people manager

Working Conditions

• None

jobs.description:

At PMG, we’re transforming the marketing technology space by combining cutting-edge technology, industry expertise, and entrepreneurial energy to empower our clients in revolutionary ways.  As a Product Principal at PMG, you will lead innovative solutions for our proprietary operating system, Alli. In this role, you will be responsible for product management within our Alli Creative Insights Pillar, our solutions that use data to empower marketers to make better, faster, data-informed decisions. Working closely with the Creative and Media teams within PMG, you will help create the product strategy and the long-term product and feature roadmap for the entire product category. You will also collaborate with Engineering, Sales, Marketing, external Partners and Customers to advocate our product, maximize its potential and lead it to market success.
