jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About the company

At Swift Solar, our mission is to unlock the full potential of solar energy. We believe solar can provide affordable, reliable, resilient, clean energy to virtually anyone, anywhere. But while today’s solar technology is good, it’s not good enough.

Swift Solar’s breakthrough perovskite-silicon tandem technology will drive solar power to commanding new heights. Our tandem cells stack a perovskite layer on top of a heterojunction (HJT) silicon cell, delivering dramatically higher efficiency than traditional silicon alone. In 2026, we acquired Meyer Burger’s HJT intellectual property and manufacturing assets, giving us the world’s most extensive HJT patent portfolio and a clear path to gigawatt-scale domestic production.

This vertically integrated approach means we can design, manufacture, and scale next-generation solar solutions entirely in the United States—from silicon foundations to perovskite innovations. Our technology enables applications ranging from space solar to utility-scale power generation, creating American-made solutions for a world facing growing energy challenges.

Swift Solar is on a journey to bring revolutionary clean-energy technology to market. We’re in it for the long haul, with support from world-class investors. Join our extraordinary team building the cutting-edge solar technology that will power the future.

A day in the life

You'll build AI products that assist scientists and accelerate our technical progress towards next-generation solar solutions. Every experiment we run costs tool time, materials, and scientists' attention, so choosing what to run next is one of the biggest levers on how fast our cells improve. You'll build the AI that helps our scientists make those choices. Our systems read scientific literature and query our lab and manufacturing data, then propose experiment plans that an automated optimizer uses to execute them.  You will lead development of the planning and reasoning layer, which takes a research objective as input and uses a multi-agent system to guide our scientists and reach goals faster through the best selected experiment campaigns. Additionally, we need to measure what works and how frontier models and our own agents perform on problems our team has already worked through, so we can improve the system over time.

This is also a place to experiment. When a promising new paper, model, or agent design comes out in AI for science, you can try it here on real problems instead of benchmarks someone else chose. You'll work with scientists who have spent years on perovskites, who know which questions matter and can tell you quickly whether an agent's answer makes sense. Because we develop the process and make the devices ourselves, the data, tools, and people who understand them live in the same company, so an idea can go from your screen to a measured result without waiting on anyone outside.

Most of this is greenfield work, and speed matters. You'll get rough versions in front of scientists quickly, watch how they use them, and turn the ideas that hold up into production systems people rely on every day. Knowing when a prototype is ready to harden, and doing it without losing momentum, is a big part of the job.

Alongside the agent work, you will:

• Hold AI-written code to a high bar. Nearly all of our code is written with AI coding tools, so critically reviewing the output and keeping the codebase documented and tested matters.

• Help keep our existing data systems running, including the pipeline that brings instrument data into our database.

• Review code across the team, and help hire and mentor new engineers as the team grows.

• Write about what we learn for our public whitepaper series and, when the work holds up, publish it in papers and present it at conferences.

You might be a good fit if you...

• Have 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, including systems that real users depend on

• Have built full-stack web applications, with a Python backend and a TypeScript/JavaScript frontend (React, Vue, Svelte, or similar)

• Have built applications on frontier LLMs through their APIs, such as agents, multi-step orchestration (e.g., LangGraph), or systems where models call tools

• Can take an idea from a quick prototype to a production system that people depend on

• Use AI coding tools like Claude Code every day, and can tell when what they produce is wrong

• Have a CS degree or a comparable record of open-source or portfolio work

• Write documented, tested code and are comfortable working in a shared codebase with git

• Can explain technical tradeoffs to scientists who aren't software engineers

• Take initiative and work independently

• Are coachable and comfortable when priorities change quickly

• Are kind, empathetic, conscientious, and motivated to make an impact on climate change

A strong candidate might bring one or more of the following...

• Experience with multi-agent systems, especially ranking, review, or memory between runs

• Experience building evaluations or benchmarks for LLM agents

• Experience designing complex software architecture and leading projects end-to-end without much oversight

• Familiarity with Bayesian optimization, surrogate models, fine-tuning of open-weights models, or reinforcement-learning environments

• Experience analyzing and plotting scientific data

• An interest in science, shown through conferences, side projects, or papers (a science background is not required)

• Experience getting skeptical users to adopt internal tools

• Experience with SQL or database administration, AWS, Azure, or GCP, or CI/CD

• Experience working at a startup

The logistics

• Compensation: Competitive package including salary, equity, and benefits

• Expected Pay Range: $150,000 - $200,000 per year

• The actual offer, reflecting total compensation and benefits, will be determined by factors such as relevant experience, skills, and other qualifications

• Ideal start date: November - December 2026

• Job type: Full-time

• Location: San Carlos, CA (Swift Solar HQ), with some remote days possible

What you’ll love about Swift

• Work with purpose: Join our mission to unlock the full potential of solar energy and make a global impact.

• Lead with innovation: Be part of an extraordinary team building cutting-edge solar technology - growth mindset; culture

• Thrive with benefits: Have 100% of your monthly premiums for HMO / PPO group healthcare plan options and 75% of your dental and vision insurance premiums covered by us. Employees also benefit from 401(k) matching, clean commuter benefits, and meaningful equity.

• Invest in your career: You’ll grow your skills, your network, and your perspective at Swift. We’ll support you in attending conferences and taking online courses, as long as you share your new insights with the team.

We recognize that candidates from underrepresented backgrounds often hesitate to apply if they don’t meet all the criteria. If you’re excited about this role and believe you can contribute to our team, we encourage you to apply—even if you don’t meet every qualification listed. We're eager to meet people from all backgrounds, and your unique skills and experiences could be exactly what we need.

If you believe in our mission but this isn’t the right job for you, please explore other career opportunities on our website and email us at careers@swiftsolar.com with any questions. If you have a friend who would be a perfect fit, share this link with them. Thanks!

Swift is an equal opportunity employer. We value an inclusive work environment and welcome team members of all backgrounds and perspectives.

jobs.title: Loads and Dynamics Engineer II
jobs.description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team:

The Integrated Performance team owns the holistic view of how Terran R comes together, ensuring that every system on the vehicle and ground is capable of achieving our ambitious objectives. The team works across the full launch system, from trajectory design and aerodynamics to reliability analysis and beyond, with direct influence on all parts of the product lifecycle, from conceptual design to post-flight data review. Beyond analysis, team members engage hands-on with hardware and operations, with the mission and authority to drive meaningful programmatic change. With a unique organizational structure, the integrated performance team spans multiple technical domains and embeds directly with partner teams to solve the hardest multi-disciplinary problems. The team operates with a rare scale: large enough to support complex development, yet small enough that individual contributors have meaningful impact.

The Loads & Dynamics team works collaboratively with adjacent Flight Sciences teams including Dynamic Environments and Aerodynamics and across the Structures, Mechanisms, Fluids, GNCP, Launch and Test teams to develop robust vehicle, ground system, and component architectures, generate associated loads, maintain and improve related analysis tools, provide design and test guidance, and contribute to performance trades on time and budget while meeting our technical requirements. A high degree of autonomy along with an ability to prioritize work in our fast-paced environment is required.

About the Role:

• Drive maturation of hardware designs and ops decisions through analysis, understanding of vehicle and program needs, and proactive communication across teams

• Develop Dynamic loads, levels, and criteria from initial concept through data review for vehicle and supporting hardware for Terran R

• Inform primary structure design and customer load inputs through Coupled Loads Analysis

• Develop and validate random vibration and shock specifications and ensuring hardware across the vehicle is qualified to those specifications

• Build, validate, and document analytical models to generate component load predictions

About You:

• Undergraduate degree with emphasis on mechanics and vibrations. Graduate coursework preferred.

• Experience with Finite Element and/or other modeling approaches for dynamic response analysis

• Experience with relevant testing, instrumentation, and data analysis

• Fluency in Python, MATLAB, or similar programming languages for engineering analysis

• Familiarity with statistics and data analysis

Nice to haves but not required:

• Graduate degree in engineering or related field

• High-speed or modal data acquisition & signal processing experience

• Experience with NASTRAN, VA One, Wave6, LS-DYNA, or other domain-specific analysis tools

• Experience with coupled loads analysis (CLA) or multibody dynamics (MBD)

• Experience with liquid rocket engines, launch vehicle analysis, or similar in aerospace

At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors.

Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here.

Hiring Range:

$103,000—$155,000 USD

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

If you need a reasonable accommodation, please contact us at accommodations@relativityspace.com.

Please note: Relativity Space does not accept unsolicited resumes, candidate profiles, or referrals from recruitment agencies or search firms. Any unsolicited submission - via email, our website, social media, or directly to an employee - will be deemed the property of Relativity Space, and no fee will be owed absent a current, fully executed agreement with Talent Acquisition that specifically authorizes submissions for the applicable role.

jobs.title: General Ledger Accountant, Payroll
jobs.description:
About Etched
Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.



Job Summary
We are hiring a General Ledger Accountant, Payroll to own critical elements of our financial close and ensure accurate accounting for payroll, benefits, and related compensation expenses. This role sits at the intersection of People Operations and Accounting, with direct ownership over payroll accruals, reconciliations, compliance, and internal controls.



You will partner closely with People Ops and Finance to ensure compensation activity is accurately recorded in the general ledger and supported by strong documentation and controls. You will own the payroll and benefits close process while helping design systems and workflows that scale as the company grows across entities and jurisdictions. This is a hands-on role requiring strong attention to detail, comfort operating in a fast-scaling environment, and a clear understanding of how payroll and benefits activity impacts financial reporting.



Key Responsibilities

 - Own and lead the payroll and benefits accounting close process, ensuring accurate accruals, reconciliations, reporting, and strong internal controls over employee compensation and related expenses

 - Reconcile payroll reports from third-party providers to the general ledger

 - Prepare and post payroll journal entries, including accruals for bonuses, commissions, and PTO

 - Reconcile benefits portal data to payroll deductions

 - Review and reconcile carrier invoices to ensure accuracy of employer and employee contributions

 - Investigate and resolve discrepancies between HRIS, payroll providers, benefits portals, and ERP

 - Prepare payroll-related account reconciliations and maintain supporting documentation

 - Maintain organized payroll and benefits documentation to support internal reviews and audits

 - Ensure payroll changes, including new hires, terminations, compensation updates, and bonus payments, have proper approval and supporting documentation

 - Maintain up-to-date process documentation for payroll and benefits workflows

 - Support periodic internal control reviews and testing

 - Maintain accurate configuration of earnings codes, deduction codes, tax settings, and pay groups within payroll systems

 - Support integration between payroll platforms, HRIS, benefits portals, and other connected systems

 - Support system setup for new states, entities, and pay frequencies as the company expands

 - Standardize payroll processes to reduce manual intervention and improve efficiency

 - Maintain payroll tax registrations across federal, state, and local jurisdictions

 - Track and monitor payroll tax filings prepared by third-party payroll providers

 - Coordinate state unemployment insurance registrations and rate updates

 - Support new state registrations as the company expands into additional jurisdictions

 - Assist with year-end reporting processes, including W-2 reconciliation and distribution oversight

 - Coordinate responses to payroll tax notices from government agencies

 - Coordinate with HR on new hires, terminations, compensation changes, and benefit elections to ensure payroll accuracy

 - Review and validate HR-provided employee data prior to payroll processing

 - Assist in resolving employee payroll and benefits inquiries in collaboration with HR



You may be a good fit if you have

 - 3 to 5+ years of general accounting experience with ownership of payroll and benefits close processes

 - Proficiency with ERP systems such as NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, or equivalent, and experience scaling systems in a high-growth environment

 - Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field

 - Strong communication and relationship-building skills to work effectively across departments



Benefits

 - Medical, dental, and vision packages with generous premium coverage
   
   - $500 per month credit for waiving medical benefits

 - Housing subsidy of $2k per month for those living within walking distance of the office

 - Relocation support for those moving to San Jose (Santana Row)

 - Various wellness benefits covering fitness, mental health, and more

 - Daily lunch and dinner in our office

 - Unlimited compute budget subject to ROI justification


How we’re different

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson http://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.

 

We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

jobs.title: Vice President, Direct Marketing & Peer-to-Peer Fundraising
jobs.description:
Job Title: Vice President, Direct Marketing & Peer-to-Peer Fundraising

Department: Development

Location: Hybrid within Washington D.C. Metro area

Reports to: Chief Development Officer

Direct Reports: No

Classification: Exempt

Position type: Full-Time Employee

Anticipated Pay Range at Commencement of Employment: $128,000 - $177,000 per year

Blue Star Families

Blue Star Families is the largest nonprofit dedicated to making military life better for families. Each year, we support over 1.5 million military- and veteran-connected family members through a national network of 300,000+ members and local chapters in communities across the country.

Our mission is simple and bold: We make military life awesome for families.

We listen, share, partner, and act to deliver evidence-based, data-driven solutions that work for real people. We’re a lifestyle organization, a friend and neighbor, and a trusted partner. Our approach is collaborative, human-centered, and designed with the whole family in mind.

A Blue Star Family is one with an immediate family member — a spouse, parent, or child — actively serving in the U.S. Armed Forces, including the Guard and Reserves. These families face unique challenges: frequent relocations, deployments, career disruption, and isolation. We respond with research-informed programs that create connection, build resilience, and foster a true sense of belonging.

We serve with urgency but build trust over time — because change happens at the speed of trust. Whether we’re driving spouse employment, supporting caregivers, or helping communities welcome military families, we strive for upstream solutions.

Who We’re Looking For:

• Bold thinkers. Fast movers. Smart collaborators. People who want to build, lead, and drive measurable change — and who care deeply about making an impact that matters.

What You’ll Do Here:

• Solve complex challenges with data, heart, and humility

• Build cross-sector partnerships that get things done

• Help military families feel at home wherever they live

If you're ready to work in a high-performance, mission-driven environment — and to make life better for those who serve — Blue Star Families is where you belong.

General Description

The Vice President, Direct Marketing & Peer-to-Peer Fundraising leads the strategy and performance of Blue Star Families' direct response and peer-to-peer fundraising programs. This role grows BSF's broad base of individual donors through multi-channel direct marketing. It also builds scalable peer-to-peer and grassroots giving programs that engage volunteers, ambassadors, chapter members and community members as fundraisers on behalf of military families.

Reporting to the Chief Development Officer and directly supervising [direct report title(s)], this leader partners closely with Marketing, Development Operations and Chapters/Programs staff to integrate direct marketing and peer-to-peer fundraising into the organization's broader revenue strategy.

This role requires the ability to travel overnight several times per year to attend team offsites, leadership sessions, fundraising events and company-wide events. Attendance and participation in these gatherings is a non-negotiable component of the position.

Key Job Functions

Direct Marketing & Mass-Market Fundraising

• Oversee multi-channel direct response strategy, including donor acquisition, retention, reactivation, and upgrade pathways across direct mail, email, digital advertising, SMS, and other mass-market channels.

• Set annual revenue goals, budgets and performance benchmarks for direct marketing programs.

• Ensure rigorous segmentation, A/B testing, and performance-based ROI analysis to inform channel investment, with a bias toward rapid experimentation and scaling winning plays.

• Manage relationships with external direct marketing vendors and agencies (e.g., MissionWired), ensuring quality, timeliness, and cost-effectiveness; hold partners to the same high-performance standard as internal team members.

• Monitor campaign performance, donor acquisition costs, retention, and lifetime value metrics, adjusting strategy as needed.

• Build a clear pathway that moves donors from first-time gifts to recurring, mid-level and major gift potential.

Peer-to-Peer & Grassroots Fundraising

• Design and grow peer-to-peer fundraising programs (e.g., team and individual fundraising campaigns, DIY fundraising, ambassador programs) to diversify and expand BSF's donor base.

• Partner with Marketing to build compelling peer-to-peer campaign assets, digital fundraising pages, and participant communications.

• Develop toolkits, training and playbooks that equip volunteers, ambassadors and chapter leaders to fundraise effectively.

• Set and track participant recruitment, fundraising, and retention goals across peer-to-peer campaigns.

• Create a visible scoreboard and recognition program that celebrates top fundraisers and teams and fuels healthy competition.

• Launch, test, and iterate on new peer-to-peer concepts quickly, scaling winning approaches and retiring those that underperform.

• Convert peer-to-peer donors and participants into ongoing supporters through targeted direct marketing follow-up.

Team Leadership & Performance Management

• Supervise staff and provide leadership and coaching to expand the chapter fundraising support function.

• Develop, coach, and appraise staff to ensure high performance and professional growth, providing regular, candid feedback and addressing performance gaps promptly.

• Build a high-talent-density team in which every member understands the strategy, owns their results, and makes decisions quickly.

• Foster a collaborative, solutions-oriented culture aligned with BSF values across the chapter network, grounded in freedom, responsibility, and accountability.

Program Integration & Cross-Functional Coordination

• Partner with Marketing & Communications on donor messaging, campaign creative, branding and channel strategy.

• Coordinate with the Chapters/Programs team to engage chapter members and volunteers in peer-to-peer campaigns.

• Ensure alignment between direct marketing, peer-to-peer, major gifts, corporate and events strategies to build strong donor pipelines.

Systems, Data & Reporting

• Oversee accurate tracking of chapter and peer-to-peer fundraising activity within the CRM, ensuring data integrity and consistent reporting.

• Establish performance dashboards and revenue pacing for direct marketing and peer-to-peer channels, using them as a real-time scoreboard for the team.

• Provide regular reporting to the Chief Development Officer, and to the Board as needed, on channel performance, donor retention and revenue forecasts.

• Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Experience, Skills, Background

• 8+ years of progressive nonprofit development experience, including experience with chapter-based, affiliate, or peer-to-peer fundraising models.

• 3+ years of experience managing staff or leading a team.

• Demonstrated experience building or scaling peer-to-peer, grassroots, or volunteer-driven fundraising programs.

• A proven track record of meeting or exceeding ambitious revenue and participation goals, with specific, measurable wins you can speak to.

• An athlete's mindset: high energy, competitive drive, resilience after setbacks, and a hunger to keep improving.

• A coach's ability to motivate, hold accountable, and bring out the best in staff and volunteers alike.

• Comfort operating with a high degree of autonomy and accountability, and the ability to give and receive candid feedback.

• Experience developing training, toolkits, or resources to support a distributed or volunteer fundraising network.

• Strong relationship-building skills with the ability to motivate and support volunteer leaders across a geographically dispersed organization.

• Demonstrated success working with CRM systems (preferably Salesforce) and peer-to-peer fundraising platforms.

• Strong organizational, analytical, and communication skills.

• Ability to travel to chapters and organizational gatherings several times per year, including overnight travel.

• May be required to work nights, weekends, and holidays as necessary to carry out key job functions.

Desired Experience, Skills & Background

• Bachelor's degree in nonprofit management, business administration, or a related field.

• Experience in membership-driven, chapter-based, or affiliate nonprofit organizations.

• Familiarity with the military and Veteran-connected community.

• Experience with peer-to-peer fundraising software (e.g., Classy, GoFundMe Charity, OneCause).

• Experience in a high-growth, performance-driven culture (nonprofit or private sector).

More About Blue Star Families

Blue Star Families empowers military and Veteran families to thrive by connecting them with their civilian neighbors — both people and organizations — to create strong communities of mutual support. We believe we're all stronger when we take care of one another.

Our groundbreaking research is raising the nation's awareness of the unique challenges of military family life. With the help of neighbors across the country, Blue Star Families is overcoming the isolation and alienation of frequent moves, deployments, and reduced support from the government. Our innovative programs are solving specific challenges for military families, including fighting economic insecurity with resources that foster spouse career development, creating family strength with rich family programming, and providing critical peer support for caregivers, whose numbers are only increasing.

Blue Star Families is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

EEO Policy

Blue Star Families is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Why Blue Star Families?

• Mission-driven work supporting military service members and their families

• Flexible work options (remote, or hybrid depending on the role)

• Competitive salary

• Comprehensive benefits, including health, dental, and vision insurance

• 403(b) retirement plan with employer match

• Flexible Spending Accounts, life insurance, and disability insurance

• Communications allowance

• Professional development and career growth opportunities

• PCS leave for Active Duty military spouses

jobs.title: Principal Mission Systems Engineer, IPT Lead
jobs.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

Role Overview:

We are seeking an experienced Principal Mission Systems Engineer who will own the mission systems architecture and operational employment concept for the Massed Modular Aircraft (MMA) program, ensuring the platform is designed not just to fly, but to execute real U.S. Air Force (USAF) mission sets as operators actually employ them. This role translates USAF Concepts of Operations (CONOPS), tactics/techniques/procedures (TTPs), and mission planning/employment workflows into concrete mission systems requirements, driving design decisions across payload integration, sensor-to-shooter/sensor-to-decision chains, mission planning, and command-and-control (C2) interoperability. The ideal candidate brings direct experience with USAF mission operations — either as a former operator, mission systems engineer supporting operational units, or developer working closely with operational USAF customers — and can credibly bridge the gap between operational requirements and engineering design decisions.

Responsibilities:

• Own the mission systems architecture for the MMA platform, including payload/sensor employment, mission planning, mission execution logic, and data/information flow supporting the operational mission.

• Translate USAF CONOPS, TTPs, and operational employment concepts into traceable mission systems requirements and architecture decisions.

• Define mission system interfaces with onboard avionics, the Ground Control Station (GCS), payload/sensor subsystems, and relevant command-and-control (C2) networks.

• Lead mission-level trade studies (e.g., sensor coverage, mission endurance, payload employment timing, autonomy/automation level) balancing operational effectiveness against cost, weight, and producibility constraints inherent to a modular, mass-producible platform.

• Serve as the engineering team's primary interface to USAF operational stakeholders (e.g., operational units, Air Combat Command or relevant MAJCOM representatives, government mission systems leads) to ensure design decisions reflect real-world employment needs.

• Participate in or lead mission utility analysis, wargaming, and operational employment reviews to validate that system design supports intended mission outcomes.

• Develop and maintain mission threads/vignettes used to drive requirements, test planning, and design verification across the program.

• Identify gaps between stated requirements and actual operational employment needs, and drive resolution through the systems engineering/requirements management process.

• Define mission planning system requirements and workflows consistent with USAF mission planning practices and tools.

• Ensure mission systems architecture supports interoperability with relevant USAF/joint C2 systems, data standards, and tactical data links as applicable to the program's operational concept.

• Partner with the Avionics/GCS engineering team (who own the onboard avionics and Ground Control Station architecture) to ensure mission systems requirements are correctly reflected in air-ground interface design and GCS operator workflows.

• Support development of mission-level cybersecurity and information assurance requirements consistent with operational employment environments.

• Define the mission systems verification approach, including mission-level test scenarios, mission thread verification, and operationally representative test conditions.

• Support developmental test (DT) and operational test (OT) planning, ensuring test events adequately exercise real mission employment conditions.

• Partner with USAF test organizations and operational evaluators to plan and execute mission systems verification activities.

• Analyze test results against mission effectiveness criteria and drive design changes where mission performance gaps are identified.

• Serve as the senior technical authority for mission systems on the program, representing the discipline at Preliminary Design Review (PDR), Critical Design Review (CDR), and government technical interchange meetings.

• Partner with Systems Engineering, Avionics, Structures/Mechanical, Software, Program Management, and the government customer to align mission systems maturity with program schedule and cost targets.

• Identify and manage mission systems risks, including operational employment risk, interoperability risk, and mission performance risk relative to stated requirements.

Minimum Requirements:

• Bachelor's degree in Systems Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related discipline; advanced degree preferred.

• 15+ years of mission systems engineering experience, with direct, hands-on experience with USAF mission operations (e.g., prior USAF operational experience, mission systems engineering supporting operational USAF units, or sustained program experience working closely with operational USAF customers).

• Demonstrated experience translating operational CONOPS/TTPs into engineering requirements and design decisions.

• Strong understanding of mission planning, sensor/payload employment concepts, and command-and-control (C2) interoperability as applied to USAF operations.

• Experience supporting developmental and/or operational test planning and execution with operational stakeholders.

• Direct experience with unmanned aircraft system (UAS) mission operations, including remotely piloted or autonomous mission employment concepts.

Preferred Requirements:

• Former USAF operator background (e.g., pilot, sensor operator, intelligence/mission planning career field) is strongly preferred.

• Familiarity with relevant USAF/joint tactical data links and C2 systems.

• Experience supporting DOW/DoD proposal efforts, including mission utility analysis and CONOPS development.

• Experience with modular, attritable, low-cost, or mass-producible aircraft programs and the mission employment considerations unique to "mass" operational concepts (e.g., distributed operations, attrition tolerance,

• Ability to obtain/maintain Secret/Top Secret/SCI clearance

Why CHAOS?

• Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company

• Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more

• Our Perks: Free daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code

• Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses

• Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices

Salary Range: $198,000 - $300,000

The stated compensation range reflects only the targeted base compensation range and excludes additional earnings such as bonus, equity, and benefits. If your compensation requirements fall outside of the range, we still encourage you to apply. The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations.

Recruiting Agencies: CHAOS Industries does not accept unsolicited resumes or outreach. Unsolicited submissions will not be reviewed or compensated.

jobs.title: FPGA Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Who You’ll Work With

You will work closely with cross-functional hardware, software, and manufacturing engineering teams to innovate new system architectures and drive FPGA development from initial concept to final delivery.

What You’ll Do

Our Hardware Design Engineering team is at the forefront of developing high-speed networking and Ethernet products used in enterprise campuses, hyperscaler data centers, and bleeding-edge AI clusters. The team is responsible for the end-to-end design and development of advanced hardware solutions that meet the demands of modern networking environments.

As a core member of the FPGA Design and Verification team, you will drive the development of high-performance control path FPGAs powering Arista’s flagship data center platforms. You will own the full design lifecycle—from gathering architectural requirements and reviewing board schematics to executing rigorous verification, leading system bring-up, and supporting production deployment.

Responsibilities:

• RTL Development & Verification: Develop, integrate, simulate, and verify Verilog and SystemVerilog RTL code, including custom testbench creation.
• FPGA Flow Implementation: Execute the full FPGA development flow, including synthesis, place and route, timing closure, and in-system hardware debugging.
• System-Level Integration: Collaborate directly with hardware and software engineering teams to drive rapid bring-up and debugging of next-generation network switch platforms.
• Design & Architecture Reviews: Actively participate in peer RTL code reviews, as well as PCB schematic and board design reviews.
• Toolchain Automation: Develop AI-skills, Python, Tcl, or shell scripts to streamline data processing and automate FPGA design workflows

Concepts & Skills You Will Gain

• Switching Architectures: Master data and control path architectures in modern Ethernet switches, alongside critical I/O interfaces (e.g., PCIe, Interlaken, Ethernet PHY/MAC, SMBus, SPI, MDIO, JTAG).
• Networking Protocols: Gain hands-on experience with Ethernet-based protocols, including PTP, sFlow, and PoE.
• Practical FPGA Engineering: Learn to navigate real-world design challenges, including tight timing closure, resource optimization, clock domain crossing, and complex state machine design.
• Multi-Vendor Ecosystems: Develop expertise across major vendor FPGA architectures, toolchains, and IDEs.
• Cross-Functional System Design: Build skills in interpreting complex PCB schematics, running advanced simulation frameworks, and solving multidisciplinary hardware/software challenges.

• 5 years or more of hands-on experience in Verilog/SystemVerilog RTL design.
• Proven background in Control Path design.
• Direct experience with On-Chip Bus interfaces (e.g., I2C, SPI, MDIO, PCIe, AXI).
• Local to the area

Preferred:

• Experience with Ethernet Data Path architecture and design.
• Hands-on experience with Streaming Bus interfaces (e.g., AXI-Stream).
• Background in FPGA resource management and timing closure.
• Proficiency in Python, Tcl, or general scripting for EDA tool automation.
• Lab Debugging & Validation: Utilize logic analyzers (LA), oscilloscopes, and vendor-specific debug tools for lab bring up, debug, and validation.

Arista Networks is an equal opportunity employer.  Arista makes all hiring and employment-related decisions in a non-discriminatory manner without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin or any other factor determined to be unlawful under applicable federal, state, or law law.  All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.description:

You will work with large-scale, multi-modal genomic datasets from clinical cohorts and partner closely with molecular biologists and clinical scientists. You will help advance the state-of-the-art and drive new methods from prototype, through scalable implementation, toward clinical validation and, ultimately, to patients.

jobs.title: Director, Revenue Accounting
jobs.description:
ABOUT SAVVY WEALTH:

Wealth management is a $545 billion industry that still runs on manual work. 75% of advisors offer no digital communication beyond email, and most still build financial plans by hand in Excel. Savvy is reinventing what it looks like to be a financial advisor. Founder Ritik Malhotra saw the fragmentation firsthand after seeking out his own advisor, and started Savvy to give independent advisors a modern, AI-native home.



Savvy is a registered investment advisor (RIA), and we partner with experienced financial advisors who want to grow without running the back office themselves. Advisors bring their book and join Savvy, running under their own brand (or ours), and Savvy earns a percentage of the assets they manage. In return, they get a true business-in-a-box: a proprietary tech platform and client portal, an in-house marketing team that helps them grow, a world-class investment management team, and a dedicated client services team that runs day-to-day operations and support. Advisors at Savvy service up to 50% more households and save 19 hours a week.



AI runs through everything we do. On the product side, Savvy Intelligence (released April 2026) is the only AI built for wealth managers that can see a client's complete financial picture. Internally, everyone at Savvy uses Claude and is encouraged to experiment with it, backed by a dedicated AI enablement team and a RevOps org building agents in-house.



The trajectory is steep and it's still early. We're a Series C company with 170+ people, $200M raised, and $100M ARR in sight this year. Inc. ranked us the No. 1 fastest-growing financial services company in America in 2026. Come build the next stage with us!



Recognition:

We're a Certified Great Place to Work and have been honored for our culture and our growth:

 - Newsweek's America's Greatest Startup Workplaces (2026)

 - Fortune Best Workplaces in New York™ (2026)

 - Great Place to Work Certified™ 
   
   


THE ROLE:

Savvy Wealth is seeking its first dedicated revenue accounting leader. In this position, you will drive revenue accounting operations, accounts receivable accounting, and financial reporting processes for a high growth fintech company ,Registered Investment Advisor (“RIA”) and broker-dealer.

You will design processes and policies, build the Campfire revenue module ensuring accurate revenue recognition, managing complex A/R processes and revenue share payments, and enhancing month-end close operations. The ideal candidate brings deep technical accounting expertise, leadership capabilities, and thrives in a fast-paced, tech-forward environment.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Manage daily revenue accounting operations, including high-volume transaction processing, and ensure accurate revenue recognition in compliance with ASC 606 for a RIA and broker-dealer

 - Own the month-end revenue close process by preparing revenue journal entries and revenue account reconciliations and journal entries for revenue, deferred revenue, and unbilled receivables

 - Manage comprehensive accounts receivable accounting functions, including custodian cash application, A/R reconciliations, and aging analysis

 - Ensure accurate commission calculations and recognition under US GAAP

 - Lead quarterly CECL aging analysis to ensure consistent application of ASC 326

 - Ensure compliance with SEC and FINRA rules and reporting

 - Perform regular month-end close flux analysis, identifying and explaining significant variances in revenue, commissions, and accounts receivable balances to ensure financial integrity and provide insights for management decision-making

 - Collaborate cross-functionally with Operations, RevOps, Sales, Legal, and other business partners on strategic processes and programs

 - Support revenue accounting system initiatives, including design, implementation, testing, and optimization

 - Serve as subject matter expert for revenue and A/R accounting questions across the organization

 - Lead audit coordination and serve as primary contact for external auditors during year-end audit

 - Maintain comprehensive documentation for all revenue, commissions and A/R processes




MUST HAVE:

 - CPA with a Bachelor's Degree in Accounting or Finance (or equivalent experience)

 - 8+ years of accounting experience, with at least 3 years in financial services industry

 - Direct experience at a wealth management firm, RIA or broker-dealer

 - You understand AUM fee billing, custodian cash flows and revenue share payout models

 - Strong knowledge of ASC 606 Revenue from Contracts with Customers & ASC 326 Credit Impairment

 - Experience with custodian cash application, accounts receivable accounting and financial reporting

 - Proficiency with mainstream ERP systems and revenue engines such as Netsuite, Campfire, Orion, AdvicePay, etc.

 - Experience in collaborating across departments to influence change

 - Attention to detail, excellent communication skills, and strong sense of teamwork

 - Ability to work independently and prioritize in a fast-paced environment

 - Strong sense of ownership and independence, with proven ability to identify issues, propose solutions, and drive initiatives to completion with minimal supervision
   


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Experience in a growing fintech business, preferably in startup or high-growth environments

 - Experience with SEC/FINRA regulated entities

 - Passion for data integrity, comfort with large datasets, and enjoyment of solving complex problems

 - Exceptional business acumen with ability to translate complex financial concepts into actionable insights for non-finance stakeholders


BENEFITS:

 - Competitive salary and equity package

 - Unlimited PTO + paid company holidays

 - Access to holistic medical, dental, and vision plans

jobs.title: Lead Technical Recruiter
jobs.location: New York, NY; Silicon Valley, CA
jobs.description:
Our Mission

You call. You wait. You call again. In every other part of your life, you book in seconds. In healthcare, you’re blocked.

We’re here to give power to the patient.

For nearly 20 years, we’ve built the leading healthcare marketplace - helping tens of millions of people find and book the care they need. Now, we’re going further: building our infrastructure beyond Zocdoc’s marketplace to power access to care wherever patients search, from provider websites and insurance directories to search engines, AI platforms, and more.

Healthcare still lacks something every other major consumer industry takes for granted: a seamless way to go from seeking to getting. We don’t want to own the front door to care; there isn't one. We want to make sure all of those doors open when patients are knocking.

Fixing healthcare starts with fixing access to it. And we're still just getting started.

Your impact on our mission

Zocdoc’s most important asset is our people.  As a Lead Technical Recruiter, you’ll play an essential role in our company’s growth by supporting staffing for our growing Technology teams. Your ability to think outside of the box to identify, attract, and close the nation’s best talent, paired with your passion for creating an efficient and highly personalized candidate experience, will impact our employees and patients for years to come.

You’ll enjoy this role if you are…

• A Senior Operational Partner: You view technical recruiting as a business problem to solve. You love sitting down with hiring teams to analyze funnel conversion, eliminate interview bottlenecks, and optimize the end-to-end hiring process.

• A Leader by Example: You take pride in demonstrating recruiting excellence. Peers look to you for advice on stakeholder management, candidate closing mechanics, and complex pipeline problem-solving.

• A High-Velocity Problem Solver: You thrive in a fast-paced, remote environment where you operate with high autonomy. You welcome ambiguity and proactively create order out of complex hiring demands.

• Passionate About Technical Talent & Metrics: You understand technical talent markets, role profiles, leveling, and candidate motivations. You use data to tell stories, manage pipelines, and influence hiring decisions.

• Grounded in Ownership and Humility: You hold yourself to an exceptionally high standard, operate with low ego, and treat candidates, peers, and executive stakeholders with equal respect and dignity.

Your day to day is…

• Operationalizing Technical Hiring: Partnering closely with engineering and technology leaders, hiring managers, and recruiting partners to audit and optimize recruitment workflows, ensuring interview loops are fast, structured, and friction-free.

• Senior Stakeholder Advisory: Acting as a trusted consultant to technology leadership—providing market intelligence, setting realistic pipeline expectations, and using data to solve hiring bottlenecks before they impact product and engineering goals.

• Executing High-Impact Searches: Directly owning end-to-end recruitment for critical positions across all levels, including senior individual contributors and leadership roles from Manager through Director.

• Mentorship & Process Rigor: Coaching and uplifting peers on the recruiting team. You will model best practices for structured interviewing, candidate evaluation, and ATS hygiene.

• Funnel Analytics & Pipeline Health: Leveraging recruiting metrics—such as pass-through rates, time-in-stage, and offer acceptance rates—to track pipeline health, forecast hiring output, and deliver clear reporting to technology leadership.

• Building Inclusive Pipelines: Proactively sourcing and building diverse talent slates, ensuring equal access and an exceptional, personalized candidate experience at every step.

You’ll be successful in the role if you have…

• 6+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, with a heavy focus on in-house technical recruiting across software engineering, infrastructure, data, security, product, or technology leadership.

jobs.title: Associate, Structuring (Debt Capital Markets)
jobs.description:
WE’RE FINANCING THE FUTURE OF ENERGY

Crux is the capital platform for the clean economy. We modernize capital raising and deployment for clean energy and critical infrastructure with solutions across advisory, investments, technology, and intelligence.

Our team of 120+ is composed of experts in energy, tax, finance, government, and technology. We have raised $77 million in capital from some of the best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Lowercarbon Capital, New System Ventures, Overture, Ardent Venture Partners, QED, Canapi, and others. These funds are joined by strategic investors including Pattern Energy, Clearway Energy, EDF Renewables, Intersect Power, LS Power, Orsted, Hartree Partners, Liberty Mutual Strategic Ventures, MassMutual Ventures, and OMERS Ventures.

 


AN INFLECTION POINT IN AMERICAN ENERGY AND MANUFACTURING

Energy demand is growing for the first time in decades, driving an urgent need for more affordable and reliable electricity. More electricity requires new clean energy infrastructure and strong domestic supply chains for minerals and components — as well as large amounts of capital.

Traditional project financing is opaque, fragmented, and analog. At Crux, we’re changing that. Through unmatched insights and expertise, white-glove service, purpose-built tools, and risk underwriting, we power a more prosperous, clean, and secure energy future.

We are scaling quickly and looking for team members who are eager to combine deep expertise with an AI-and tech-forward mindset. 

 


THE OPPORTUNITY

The Associate, Debt Capital Markets will be a core member of Crux's Structuring team, reporting to the Principal. The team delivers capital solutions across debt, tax equity, preferred equity, and advisory services to sponsors, developers, and investors. This work spans project-level and corporate-level transactions in renewable energy and energy transition infrastructure.

This is a hands-on execution role for a financially rigorous analyst with foundational knowledge and a strong desire to grow within renewable energy finance. The Associate will support the structuring, origination, and execution of financings across the capital structure.

The role requires strong financial modeling skills, exposure to renewables and energy transition markets, and the ability to operate in a fast-paced startup environment

This position is ideal for candidates with at least 2 years of relevant experience in investment banking, renewable energy, structured finance, infrastructure investing, or a closely related field who are people who looking to deepen their structuring expertise in a fast-moving, technology-forward environment.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Support transaction structuring execution across debt mandates, including modeling, diligence coordination, and documentation. Prepare client-facing materials, including financing presentations, credit memos, investor marketing materials, and internal approvals

 - Support advisory mandates, including financing alternatives analysis, capital raising strategy, and process management for sponsors and developers.

 - Conduct capital structure, pricing, and credit analysis across renewable energy asset classes.

 - Participate in strategic meetings with clients on financing alternatives, market positioning, and structuring considerations.

 - Interface directly with capital providers, developers, sponsors, and external advisors.

 - Work closely with senior members of the Structuring team to drive transactions from intake through term sheets, and maintain active market intelligence.

 - Leverage technology and AI-enabled tools to increase accuracy and efficiency in modeling, diligence, and reporting.

 - Contribute to process improvements and template standardization (models, memos, term sheets) across the Structuring team.

 - Support platform initiatives to scale capital markets workflows and develop new tech-enabled products and solutions for financing processes.
   
    


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering, or a related field; MBA or MS a plus.

 - Minimum 2+ years of experience in renewable energy, structured finance, infrastructure investing, investment banking or a closely related field.

 - Demonstrated exposure to capital markets and/or project finance transactions.

 - Strong financial modeling and structuring skills, with mastery of core valuation and credit concepts.

 - Strong Excel skills, including comfort building and navigating complex financial models; VBA or Python skills a plus.

 - Experience preparing transaction materials and conducting due diligence.

 - Familiarity with capital markets instruments used in clean infrastructure (term loans, private credit, structured debt, project-level financing, etc.)

 - Exposure to tax equity underwriting a plus.

 - Experience in a transaction-focused environment with client interaction responsibility is a plus.

 - Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams in a fast-paced environment.

 - Self-directed, highly organized, and detail-oriented.

 - Comfortable adopting new technology platforms and integrating AI tools into daily workflows.

 - FINRA SIE, Series 79, and 63, or willingness to obtain them under Crux's broker-dealer sponsorship.
   
    


WHAT WE BRING

 - Backing, traction & brand:
   
   - We have raised $77 million in capital from some of the best venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Lowercarbon Capital, New System Ventures, Ardent Venture Partners, Pattern, Clearway, EDFR, Intersect, LS Power, Orsted, Hartree Partners, Liberty Mutual Strategic Ventures, MassMutual Ventures, and OMERS Ventures.
   
   - $500m debt warehouse facility from Nuveen to invest in clean energy.
   
   - Have been profitable and are growing exponentially
   
   - We have closed over 120+ transactions in just the last 2 years, facilitating billions of dollars of capital flowing into renewables projects

 - Culture & working dynamic
   
   - Remote-first operating model: Work from anywhere in the US and Canada, or work out of our optional offices in DC, NYC, & SF. Optional co-working opportunities with co-workers in, Seattle, Denver, Boston, LA, and beyond.
   
   - High growth & high ownership culture: We grow quickly by giving extremely talented people a lot of responsibility.
   
   - Best of financial services & technology: We have brought together a team that are experts in clean energy finance, and the best technologies. Use your expertise while getting to be on the cutting edge of applying AI to your day and your clients’ experience.
   
   - Regular team offsites: We sustain culture by bringing the entire company together 2 times a year. Individual teams may also meet up more frequently.

 - Benefits
   
   - Healthcare: We cover 100% of premiums for employees with a variety of plans on Aetna (nationwide) and Kaiser (WA and California) and subsidize 70% for dependents (total as a group), if relevant.
   
   - Dental & vision: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and 50% for dependents (each), if relevant.
   
   - Holidays: 10 company holidays per year.
   
   - Paid time off: 20 days per year.
   
   - 401k: We support a 401k account but don't have a matching program set up at this time (typical for an early-stage startup).
   
   - Parental leave: 16 weeks for birthing parents and 12 weeks for non-birthing parents.

 - Compensation:
   
   - Compensation: $150,000s - $200,000s, depending on years of exp. & revenue scope, not inclusive of equity value.
   
   - Stock options in a rapidly growing company.

 - Values
   
   - Care for each other: We want to work on a team where people support each other - in their growth, in their work, and towards our shared mission. When we do that, we have fun.
   
   - Build and improve rapidly: We move quickly. To do that, we focus, consistently ask ourselves if we are prioritizing the right things, and execute them as best as possible.
   
   - Focus unremittingly on customers: Our first obligation is to our customers and partners, and we keep their needs front and center in everything we do.
   
   - Demonstrate ownership: We are all owners of Crux. This is our team, our company, our product and we show that to each other.
   
   - Convene a team that reflects the breadth of experiences in the country: We’re building a team with a wide range of backgrounds and a culture where everyone can thrive.

jobs.title: Principal Configuration Management Specialist
jobs.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

Role Overview:

We are seeking an experienced Senior Configuration Management (CM) Specialist who will lead configuration management activities across development, qualification, and production programs supporting Massed Modular Aircraft (MMA) program. This role owns the integrity of product baselines throughout the system lifecycle — ensuring that design, documentation, and as-built/as-maintained configurations remain accurate, traceable, and compliant with contractual, regulatory, and internal quality requirements. The ideal candidate has deep familiarity with defense industry CM practices, engineering change processes, and the unique configuration control challenges of complex, safety-critical hardware/software systems. This position is located in Los Angeles and may require travel to other sites or the customer for reviews and audit.

Responsibilities:

• Establish, maintain, and audit product baselines (functional, allocated, and product) across hardware and software configuration items throughout the program lifecycle.

• Manage the Engineering Change Proposal/Request (ECP/ECR) process, including impact assessment coordination, Configuration Control Board (CCB) support, and disposition tracking.

• Maintain configuration status accounting and traceability across requirements, design documentation, drawings, software builds, and test/qualification records.

• Ensure as-designed, as-built, and as-maintained configurations remain synchronized and auditable.

• Apply configuration management practices in accordance with applicable standards (e.g., EIA-649, MIL-STD-973/MIL-HDBK-61, SAE-EIA-649, ANSI/EIA-649-B) and contract-specific CM plans (CMPs) or Data Item Descriptions (DIDs).

• Support compliance with customer and regulatory requirements relevant to aircraft, missile, or sUAS programs (e.g., AS9100, DO-178C/DO-254 configuration aspects, ITAR/EAR documentation control).

• Prepare for and support internal audits, customer configuration audits (Functional Configuration Audits/Physical Configuration Audits — FCA/PCA), and government reviews.

• Set up and administer configuration management tools/systems (e.g., PLM/PDM systems such as Teamcenter, Windchill, or similar; DOORS or other requirements management tools) to control engineering data and change records.

• Coordinate cross-functionally with design engineering, systems engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and program management on change impacts, effectivity, and implementation.

• Manage configuration item (CI) identification, numbering schemes, and revision control across hardware, software, firmware, and technical documentation.

• Support release management for engineering drawings, specifications, interface control documents (ICDs), and software version control.

• Serve as the senior CM point of contact for one or more programs, representing CM in program reviews, technical interchange meetings, and customer engagements.

• Support proposal efforts with CM plan development, staffing estimates, and lessons-learned input.

Minimum Requirements:

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical field

• Minimum 10 years of configuration management experience within the defense/aerospace industry, with direct exposure to aircraft or UAS programs.

• Strong working knowledge of CM standards (e.g., EIA-649, MIL-HDBK-61) and demonstrated experience running or supporting CCBs.

• Hands-on experience with PLM/PDM and/or requirements management tools.

• Experience managing configuration baselines across the full program lifecycle (development through production/sustainment).

• Experience with FCA/PCA support and customer/government configuration audits.

• AS9100 quality system experience.

Preferred Requirements:

• Familiarity with UAS-specific configuration challenges (rapid iteration cycles, COTS component tracking, frequent software updates).

• Ability to obtain/maintain Secret/Top Secret/SCI clearance

Why CHAOS?

• Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company

• Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more

• Our Perks: Free daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code

• Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses

• Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices

Salary Range: $160,000 - $266,000

The stated compensation range reflects only the targeted base compensation range and excludes additional earnings such as bonus, equity, and benefits. If your compensation requirements fall outside of the range, we still encourage you to apply. The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations.

jobs.title: FPGA Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Who You’ll Work With

You will work closely with cross-functional hardware, software, and manufacturing engineering teams to innovate new system architectures and drive FPGA development from initial concept to final delivery.

What You’ll Do

Our Hardware Design Engineering team is at the forefront of developing high-speed networking and Ethernet products used in enterprise campuses, hyperscaler data centers, and bleeding-edge AI clusters. The team is responsible for the end-to-end design and development of advanced hardware solutions that meet the demands of modern networking environments.

As a core member of the FPGA Design and Verification team, you will drive the development of high-performance control path FPGAs powering Arista’s flagship data center platforms. You will own the full design lifecycle—from gathering architectural requirements and reviewing board schematics to executing rigorous verification, leading system bring-up, and supporting production deployment.

Responsibilities:

• RTL Development & Verification: Develop, integrate, simulate, and verify Verilog and SystemVerilog RTL code, including custom testbench creation.
• FPGA Flow Implementation: Execute the full FPGA development flow, including synthesis, place and route, timing closure, and in-system hardware debugging.
• System-Level Integration: Collaborate directly with hardware and software engineering teams to drive rapid bring-up and debugging of next-generation network switch platforms.
• Design & Architecture Reviews: Actively participate in peer RTL code reviews, as well as PCB schematic and board design reviews.
• Toolchain Automation: Develop AI-skills, Python, Tcl, or shell scripts to streamline data processing and automate FPGA design workflows.

Concepts & Skills You Will Gain

• Switching Architectures: Master data and control path architectures in modern Ethernet switches, alongside critical I/O interfaces (e.g., PCIe, Interlaken, Ethernet PHY/MAC, SMBus, SPI, MDIO, JTAG).
• Networking Protocols: Gain hands-on experience with Ethernet-based protocols, including PTP, sFlow, and PoE.
• Practical FPGA Engineering: Learn to navigate real-world design challenges, including tight timing closure, resource optimization, clock domain crossing, and complex state machine design.
• Multi-Vendor Ecosystems: Develop expertise across major vendor FPGA architectures, toolchains, and IDEs.
• Cross-Functional System Design: Build skills in interpreting complex PCB schematics, running advanced simulation frameworks, and solving multidisciplinary hardware/software challenges.

• 5 years or more of hands-on experience in Verilog/SystemVerilog RTL design.
• Proven background in Control Path design.
• Direct experience with On-Chip Bus interfaces (e.g., I2C, SPI, MDIO, PCIe, AXI).
• Local to the Bay area

Preferred:

• Experience with Ethernet Data Path architecture and design.
• Hands-on experience with Streaming Bus interfaces (e.g., AXI-Stream).
• Background in FPGA resource management and timing closure.
• Proficiency in Python, Tcl, or general scripting for EDA tool automation.
• Lab Debugging & Validation: Utilize logic analyzers (LA), oscilloscopes, and vendor-specific debug tools for lab bring up, debug, and validation.

Compensation Information:

The new hire base pay for this role has a pay range of $110,000 to $170,000. Arista offers different pay ranges based on work location, so that we can offer consistent and competitive pay appropriate to the market. The actual base pay offered will be based on a wide range of factors, including skills, qualifications, relevant experience, and work location. The salary range provided reflects base pay only. As described above, this position may also be eligible for discretionary Arista bonuses and equity. US- based employees are also entitled to benefits including medical, dental, vision, wellbeing, tax savings and income protection. The recruiting team can share more details during the hiring process specific to the role and location.

Arista Networks is an equal opportunity employer.  Arista makes all hiring and employment-related decisions in a non-discriminatory manner without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin or any other factor determined to be unlawful under applicable federal, state, or law law.  All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Director, People Operations and Total Rewards
jobs.description:
Santa Clara, CA | Reports to the Head of People and Culture

LeanData helps the world’s fastest-growing companies automate, simplify, and accelerate revenue.

As our business evolves, we’re building the People infrastructure to support what comes next. We’re looking for a Director of People Operations and Total Rewards who can strengthen our foundation, simplify how work gets done, and build programs that help us attract, retain, and support exceptional talent in our championship culture.

You’ll own People Operations, compensation, and benefits, partnering closely with Finance, IT, and our People Business Partner. You’ll join a small, collaborative People team with the opportunity to shape the function, influence business decisions, and see the impact of your work directly. We share responsibility for the team’s success, support one another through competing priorities, and step in where we can make a difference.

Some of our systems and processes were built for an earlier stage. Your opportunity is to determine what to keep, what to improve, and what to reimagine, creating capacity through better systems, clear ownership, and thoughtful automation.

This is a hybrid role, with 3 days onsite (M/W/Th) in our Santa Clara office.




WHO WILL THRIVE HERE

You’re a builder who enjoys turning complexity into something practical and easy to use. You can set a direction, make a recommendation, and get into the details to deliver it. You take pride in both the quality of your decisions and the reliability of everyday operations.

You understand that People Operations is part of how the business performs. You bring financial discipline and employee empathy to decisions, explain trade-offs clearly, and build trust through sound judgment and follow-through.

You’re curious about what’s possible with AI and automation, and are thoughtful about where human judgment matters. You challenge processes that no longer serve their purpose, learn quickly, and move improvements forward without waiting for perfect conditions.

You’re a strong teammate who listens before making changes, respects the expertise others bring, and builds solutions with the people who will use them. You share information openly, welcome feedback, and work through disagreements directly and respectfully. You’re comfortable leading an initiative, supporting someone else’s, and rolling up your sleeves when the team needs help.

Our values should feel familiar in how you work:

● Champion Customers: Understand the needs of the employees and leaders you support and make their experience better.

● Wonder Why: Ask questions, investigate root causes, and stay open to a better approach.

● Own It: Take accountability from identifying a problem through delivering a lasting solution.

● Build Bold: Test new approaches and turn ideas into measurable improvements.

● One Team: Work with low ego, share context, and build solutions across functions. Follow through on commitments, address challenges together, and put shared outcomes ahead of individual credit.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN


PEOPLE OPERATIONS AND SYSTEMS

● Set and execute the People Operations roadmap, prioritizing improvements based on business needs, employee experience, risk, and available resources.

● Own reliable operations across onboarding, offboarding, employee records, leaves, accommodations, policies, and employee changes.

● Partner with Finance on payroll, establishing clear responsibilities, accurate inputs, reconciliations, and timely resolution of issues.

● Improve our HR technology stack, integrations, workflows, documentation, and data quality. Use AI and automation to reduce manual work while protecting sensitive information and validating results.

● Establish service standards, controls, and escalation paths, and personally resolve complex operational issues.

● Partner with the People Business Partner on performance-cycle operations, organizational changes, and program rollouts, with clear ownership and coordinated employee communication. Build a close working partnership that connects operational improvements with what employees, managers, and the business need.

● Coordinate immigration matters with external counsel and internal stakeholders, ensuring dependable tracking, communication, and follow-through.




TOTAL REWARDS

● Develop and evolve our compensation and benefits strategy with the Head of People and Culture, People Business Partner, and Finance, balancing competitiveness, internal equity, affordability, and business priorities.

● Lead market benchmarking, job architecture, leveling, salary ranges, pay equity analysis, and compensation review cycles.

● Advise leaders on offers, promotions, incentives, and retention decisions, using market data and clear decision frameworks.

● Partner with Finance and Legal on equity program administration, approvals, and employee communications.

● Translate complex analysis into clear recommendations and help managers communicate compensation decisions with confidence.




BENEFITS AND WELLBEING

● Own benefits strategy and delivery, including renewals, plan evaluation, cost modeling, open enrollment, and employee communications.

● Manage brokers, carriers, and vendors, holding partners accountable for service, accuracy, and value.

● Use employee feedback, utilization, and market insights to recommend improvements that balance employee needs with cost.

● Make benefits and leave programs understandable and accessible to employees.




COMPLIANCE, ANALYTICS, AND BUSINESS PARTNERSHIP

● Maintain compliant People practices across applicable employment requirements, with strong working knowledge of California and federal requirements and sound judgment about when to involve counsel.

● Own operational audit readiness, records management, access controls, and documentation; identify and address risks proactively.

● Partner with Finance, IT, Legal, and business leaders on workforce data, budgeting, systems, and operational priorities.

● Build useful reporting on workforce trends, compensation, benefits costs, and operational performance.

● Measure whether improvements reduce errors, save time, strengthen controls, and improve the employee experience.




WHAT YOU BRING

● 7+ years of progressive experience across People Operations, total rewards, or related HR disciplines, with accountability for a broad portfolio.

● A track record of building or improving People infrastructure in a lean, changing environment.

● Direct ownership of compensation programs, including benchmarking, salary structures, compensation cycles, and advising leaders on decisions.

● Experience owning benefits renewals, broker relationships, program costs, and enrollment.

● Strong HR systems and payroll process knowledge, including integrations, reporting, data quality, and controls.

● Practical experience managing employment compliance and sensitive operational issues.

● Financial and analytical confidence, including building cost models, evaluating market data, and making clear recommendations.

● Evidence of delivering measurable process improvements through technology, automation, or simpler ways of working.

● Strong communication, prioritization, and cross-functional leadership skills, with the willingness to stay hands-on.




EXPERIENCE THAT WOULD BE HELPFUL

● B2B SaaS or technology company experience.

● Experience supporting a primarily California-based workforce, with smaller teams in other locations, and coordinating immigration matters with external counsel.

● Experience with BambooHR, ADP Workforce Now, Lattice, Pave, Radford, or comparable platforms.

● Relevant HR, compensation, or benefits certifications.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Employees and managers experience accurate, responsive support. Our systems require less manual work, our data is dependable, and responsibilities across People and Finance are clear. Leaders have practical frameworks for compensation decisions, and the People team has more capacity to support the business as it evolves.
