jobs.title: SMT Process Engineer (Greenfield Factory)
jobs.description:
ABOUT ETCHED

Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest-growing industry in history.




JOB SUMMARY

Etched is seeking an SMT Process Engineer to help establish our first PCB assembly (PCBA) manufacturing facility. You will be part of the core team selecting, installing, qualifying, and launching our first SMT production line, with hands-on ownership of manufacturing readiness from initial setup through volume production.

This role spans equipment programming, process development, tooling, operator training, and engineering build support. You will also provide technical direction to one SMT Engineering Technician, ensuring equipment and lab readiness to support new product introduction and production schedules. This is an opportunity to build an SMT operation from the ground up and establish the processes and standards that support future growth.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Launch our first SMT line: Support equipment selection, define technical specifications and acceptance criteria, and coordinate installation with vendors and facilities teams.

 - Qualify equipment for production: Support Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT) and Site Acceptance Tests (SAT), and develop and execute equipment startup, validation, and qualification plans.

 - Own SMT programming and process development: Develop and optimize programs for solder paste printers, SPI, pick-and-place, AOI, AXI where applicable, and depanelization equipment. Maintain component libraries, machine databases, and standard setup procedures.

 - Establish tooling readiness: Define, procure, and qualify stencils, PCB support tooling, carrier pallets, vacuum fixtures, and depanelization and rework fixtures ahead of engineering builds.

 - Support builds from prototype through production: Lead SMT support for prototype, EVT, DVT, PVT, and production builds. Troubleshoot process and programming issues, support engineering changes and product transfers, and minimize downtime.

 - Develop manufacturing standards: Create equipment operating procedures, standard work instructions, and process controls. Support facility readiness, including utilities, ESD controls, and traceability.

 - Train and certify operators: Develop training materials and train operators and technicians on equipment operation, feeder setup, program selection, changeovers, basic troubleshooting, and process controls.

 - Provide technical leadership: Coach and prioritize work for one SMT Engineering Technician covering preventive maintenance, calibration, spare parts, vendor service, equipment qualification, and engineering lab support.

 - Ensure process and lab readiness: Guide reflow profile verification, process characterization, and sample preparation for failure analysis to support engineering and production needs.

 - Drive continuous improvement: Improve first-pass yield (FPY), throughput, and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE). Reduce setup and changeover time, optimize placement strategies, and standardize best practices across SMT operations.




YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE (MUST-HAVE QUALIFICATIONS)

 - A bachelor’s degree in engineering or equivalent practical experience.

 - 10+ years of SMT manufacturing engineering experience.

 - Demonstrated experience supporting SMT line installation, commissioning, or factory startup.

 - Experience with equipment acceptance testing, qualification, and production ramp-up.

 - Hands-on experience programming and optimizing SMT equipment.

 - Experience supporting PCBA manufacturing from prototype builds through high-volume production.




STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO HAVE EXPERIENCE WITH (NICE-TO-HAVE QUALIFICATIONS)

 - Leading technicians or small technical teams.




BENEFITS

 - Medical, dental, and vision packages with generous premium coverage.

 - $500 per month credit for waiving medical benefits.

 - Housing subsidy of $2,500 per month for those living within walking distance of the office.

 - Relocation support for those moving to San Jose (Santana Row).

 - Various wellness benefits covering fitness, mental health, and more.

 - Daily lunch and dinner in our office.

 - Unlimited compute budget, subject to ROI justification.




HOW WE’RE DIFFERENT

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system, betting early on transformer and transformer-like architectures and on increasing model sizes. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.

We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row) and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

jobs.title: Director of Student Engagement at Boston University Hillel
jobs.description:
Director of Student Engagement

Boston University Hillel

Role Overview

Make your mark on Jewish student life by joining Boston University Hillel as its Director of Student Engagement. This is a big, exciting job for BU Hillel, working at the largest private university for Jewish students in the world. This position will work on major aspects of undergraduate student engagement, serving 4,000 Jewish undergraduate students. We welcome candidates who are thirsty for being in relationship with Jewish people – from students to alumni, parents, donors, and other partners. If you’re team-oriented, never give up, and truly believe that you must “be the change you wish to see in the world,” then this is the position for you! This position reports to the Executive Director and works closely with the CEO, Campus Rabbi, and COO.

What You’ll Do

Undergraduate Student Life Work

The role brings a professional with talent, passion, and skills to Boston University to imagine and implement Jewish undergraduate student life. As the Director, you will serve as both the architect of a comprehensive, strategic, and robust undergraduate engagement plan and the primary practitioner implementing this plan with 4,000 Jewish undergraduate students. You’ll have the opportunity to impact thousands of students—Boston University is home to over 17,000 undergraduate students across 10 undergraduate schools and colleges thirsty for resources, engagement, and care from BU Hillel.

This position has significant responsibility overseeing key student engagement areas for BU Hillel, including: student engagement outreach strategies, mentoring projects, advising student leaders, leading cohorts around Boston and trips to Israel, and more. You also contribute to religious activities such as Shabbat services/dinner, holiday programs, Israel events, and more. You will teach in our award-winning Jewish learning seminars with Jewish text at the center of each class. You will partner with BU Hillel’s senior rabbinic leadership on strategy and content for each of these programs, and receive guidance.

You’ll receive training from BU Hillel and Hillel International professionals, and learn from Jewish leaders on how to seamlessly weave Judaism into your work as a Hillel engagement professional. Each day you will be charged with empowering students to engage in meaningful and joyous Jewish lives, weaving in Jewish values, texts, and history.

Student Engagement and Outreach

• Manage Hillel’s marketing and outreach to all undergraduate colleges and residence halls—working with individual college partners and student groups.

• Director strategies for outreach and relationships with undergraduate students, conducting daily 1x1 initial and follow-up meetings.

• Strengthen and support student leadership cohorts ranging from engagement interns, to marketing interns, and career focused fellowships.

• Mentor various students in their desire to bring passion projects to campus.

• Grow Hillel’s capacity to meet engagement goals through detailed management and analysis of the CRM Database.

• Drive key insights on undergraduate student engagement and population for further growth of the program.

• Works with Hillel’s staff and student leaders to identify micro-communities and opportunities for students to engage within those micro-communities. These include but are not limited to: class years, majors, Jewish Greek life, Jewish residence hall life, arts and culture, volunteerism, and social justice.

Jewish Life and Learning

• Develop, lead, and recruit 1-2 Jewish learning fellowship classes and 1-2 experience groups in Boston per semester

• Weave Jewish education into social and cultural programs across campus.

• Co-lead immersive travel trips to Israel or community service trips to international destinations weaving Jewish content, text, and learning into each day of travel.

• Co-lead experience groups around Boston that have 3-5 parts to each group focused on fun, friendship, Jewish identity, and exploration. These cohorts attend fun events like Celtics games, fitness studios, best restaurants of Boston, musical concerts, theater shows, and more.

On a day to day basis you will

• Meeting with a group of students or individual students over coffee or a meal to understand which issues are most important to them and developing a plan of action together.

• Designing and executing a strategic engagement plan for undergraduate students, including planning educational, social, cultural, holiday, or Shabbat programs across a wide variety of undergraduate schools, students, and disciplines.

• Participating in a conversation with student leaders of all types of faith, ethnic, and racial backgrounds to build key relationships and partnerships.

• Developing key insights through 1x1 conversations on how to create an engagement program with high levels of reach and depth.

• Working Shabbat, holidays, and otherwise supporting the rest of your Hillel team—sometimes on nights and weekends.

• Participating in a professional development webinar.

• Teaching and facilitating Jewish learning through an undergraduate student lens.

What You’ve Accomplished

• 3–5 years of experience

• Bachelor's degree required; master's or advanced degree preferred (could be rabbinic, Jewish education, business, social work, or other relevant fields to this work).

• Significant computer skills, including Microsoft Office, Google Docs, CRM, and social media

• Must be willing to work nights and occasional weekends

• Requires discretion and independent judgement in performing all aspects of the position.

• An entrepreneurial spirit, willingness to take risks and the ability to learn from efforts that don’t work out as planned

What You’ll Bring to the Job

We are most interested in someone who is organized, driven, and mission-focused. The most important experience we are looking for is the ability to be a Jewish leader, organize people and projects, and inspire commitment and action. In terms of prerequisite requirements, we are open to candidates with the following:

• We are interested in people with backgrounds in PR, Communications, Marketing, Communal Engagement, For Profit Business, Customer Service and/or

• Significant Jewish communal life experience in any of the following: Hillel, Jewish nonprofit, Jewish camping, Jewish education, or Rabbinic leadership. and/or

• Significant experience with relationship-based work in areas such as: student engagement, community partnerships, nonprofit management, corporate social responsibility, or arts management. and/or

• Significant experience in for-profit environments that is relatable to this work, alongside a very strong Jewish lay leadership background.

What You’ll Receive

• High-level professional development to help develop core skills and gain expertise from changemakers, engagers, and Jewish life experts.

• Mentoring and career coaching to help you during and after your position.

• A network of terrific colleagues from across the Hillel movement.

• Travel opportunities, both domestically and internationally, multiple times per year.

• A comprehensive benefits package, including health insurance, Tax Deferred Retirement Plan, Life, AD&D, and Long-Term Disability insurances, Flexible Spending Plan, generous vacation/sick time, and parental leave.

• A salary of $55,000–$65,000 depending on level of experience.

About Boston University Hillel

Boston University Hillel is at the hub of a world-class university, in the thriving city of Boston, right near Fenway Park. Home to 4,000 Jewish undergraduates and 2,000 Jewish graduate students, BU Hillel’s mission is to inspire, educate, and empower BU students to lead meaningful and joyous Jewish lives. We engage 4,000 students per year, 600 of whom qualify as in-depth relationships. 200 students travel with BU Hillel each year. We have 160+ student leaders and 120+ lay leaders.

Boston University Hillel is affiliated with Hillel International. Hillel International enriches the lives of Jewish students so they may enrich the Jewish people and the world, and envisions a world where every student is inspired to make an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning and Israel.

About Hillel International

In 1923, Rabbi Benjamin Frankel started Hillel with humble means, a noble mission and a breathtaking vision: to convey Jewish civilization to a new generation. Today, Hillel International continues to enrich the lives of Jewish students and is the largest Jewish campus organization in the world at nearly 1,000 colleges and universities across North America and around the world. As Hillel evolves as an organization, the mission remains steadfast: to create lasting connections with every Jewish student that foster an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning, and Israel and train them to become the next Jewish leaders.

Hillel is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an accepting and inclusive environment for all.

Software runs the world and the pace is faster than ever. Sentry helps developers fix errors and performance issues before users notice, so teams can spend less time firefighting and more time building.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Billing team sits at the intersection of product, finance, and infrastructure. They're responsible for ensuring every observable event—errors, logs, traces, tokens—gets accurately measured, priced, and billed. Their work directly impacts company revenue and customer trust, requiring distributed systems expertise, attention to financial accuracy, and deep understanding of product usage patterns. The team works cross-functionally with product, engineering, BizOps, marketing, and sales to build systems that enable new products and pricing models.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will architect and scale the core systems that power Sentry's billing infrastructure, ensuring accuracy and reliability at massive scale.

 

 - You will collaborate on building the next generation of Sentry’s usage tracking pipeline, processing hundreds of billions of events daily with low latency and financial-grade accuracy.

 - You will help design flexible pricing primitives that support everything from per-event usage billing to complex enterprise contracts, enabling product and sales teams to experiment rapidly while maintaining revenue accuracy and reduced time-to-market for new products.

 - You will contribute to technical decisions on data consistency challenges unique to billing—like handling event delays, retroactive pricing changes, and distributed count reconciliation across our infrastructure.




YOU'LL LOVE THIS JOB IF YOU

 - Want to solve the "easy to explain, hard to build" problems—like ensuring a customer's bill matches their usage perfectly, even when processing hundreds of billions of events daily across distributed systems.

 - Thrive on constraints that force elegant design: financial accuracy is non-negotiable, customer trust depends on billing transparency, and the system must scale with Sentry's user and product growth without rearchitecting every year.

 - Enjoy partnering across the organization—from BizOps and sales to marketing and leadership—where your code directly impacts ARR and your architectural decisions show up in board-level metrics.

The Director is expected to operate with a high degree of autonomy and sound judgment while maintaining strong alignment with executive leadership, effectively leading the Business Development team, adhering to company policies and processes, and delivering measurable business results.

Essential Duties/Responsibilities

Strategic Planning: Develop and execute business development strategies to drive growth and achieve company objectives. Collaborate with executives to develop, articulate, and execute a business development strategy with short-, mid-, and long-term goals by providing input from industry, market, and competitive analysis, customer needs assessments, customer feedback, product definition feedback, and future mission requirements.

Sales and Revenue Growth: Drive sales initiatives and achieve revenue targets through effective business development strategies. Coordinate with executives to define and execute strategies to grow product segment market share and profitability through market opportunity evaluation and segmentation, value proposition development, product positioning, pricing strategy, branding and channel strategy, and communications strategy development.

Client Relationships: Establish and maintain strong relationships with key clients, including government agencies, defense contractors, and commercial aerospace companies. Establish and nurture customer relationships to understand current and future needs and promote alignment of the company’s current and future capabilities to meet those needs.

Team Leadership: Lead, coach, and develop members of the Business Development team to build a high-performing and accountable organization. Establish clear priorities, expectations, and ownership across the team; provide regular feedback and coaching; monitor performance and workload; and ensure team members have the direction, resources, and support necessary to successfully execute their responsibilities. Maintain an appropriate level of engagement and presence with the team to support collaboration, development, and effective execution of business development priorities.

Cross-functional Collaboration: Work closely with the leadership team, engineering, business capture, and product development teams to align business development efforts with company goals. Align with the capture team to define technical, strategic, and business insight for RFI, ROM, whitepaper, and proposal responses.

Market Analysis: Identify and analyze market trends, customer needs, and the competitive landscape to uncover new business opportunities. Supervise marketing execution, including content for SEAKR’s website, product and marketing literature, trade show presence, trade journal articles, white papers, press releases, presentations, and datasheets. Represent the company at appropriate industry events, conferences, trade shows, and customer engagements to promote products and services.

Business Development Execution and Delegation: Establish clear ownership and accountability for business development activities across the team. Effectively delegate customer engagements, opportunity development, and other business development responsibilities to ensure appropriate coverage, develop team capabilities, and maximize organizational effectiveness. Maintain visibility into team activities, customer engagements, pipeline development, and key opportunities to ensure alignment with company priorities.

Policy and Expense Management: Demonstrate consistent compliance with company policies, procedures, and internal controls, including all Travel and Expense requirements. Utilize the company’s designated travel and expense management system (Concur) for business travel booking and expense reporting, as required by company policy, and ensure expenses are accurately documented and submitted in a timely manner. As a people leader, reinforce these expectations with members of the Business Development team and model appropriate stewardship of company resources.

Travel: Must be available to travel for business approximately 30%–50% of the time based on customer, program, and business needs. Travel should be purposeful and aligned with business development priorities, customer engagement requirements, and company objectives, while maintaining appropriate availability and presence to effectively lead and support the Business Development team. The Director is expected to exercise sound judgment in determining when in-person travel is necessary and when business objectives can be effectively accomplished through other means.

Supervisory Duties

• Provide direct leadership and oversight of members of the Business Development team.
• Establish individual and team priorities, goals, and performance expectations aligned with company objectives.
• Provide ongoing coaching, feedback, performance management, and professional development to team members.
• Effectively delegate responsibilities and customer engagements to develop team capabilities, ensure appropriate coverage, and maximize organizational effectiveness.
• Monitor team performance, workload, customer engagement, and execution against business development priorities.
• Assess organizational capabilities and resource needs and support the continued development and growth of the Business Development function.
• Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, communication, and compliance with company policies and processes.

Education or Formal Training

• The ideal candidate will have a technical background and a Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, with an emphasis in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
• A Master’s degree in Engineering Management or Program Management, or an MBA, is preferred.

Experience

• At least 15 years of technical business development experience, with demonstrated experience in the aerospace and/or space markets preferred.
• Demonstrated experience developing and executing business development and growth strategies within a technical environment.
• Proven experience developing and maintaining relationships with government, defense, aerospace, and/or commercial space customers.
• Demonstrated leadership experience, including managing, coaching, developing, and holding team members accountable for performance and results.
• Experience managing multiple business development opportunities, customer engagements, and capture activities simultaneously.

Security Clearance The candidate will either possess a TS/SCI with polygraph clearance or be capable of obtaining the required clearance.

Skills  Demonstrate strong analytical, negotiation, leadership, and communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively under pressure.

Compensation: Base salary range is $225,000-275,000, depending on qualifications. SEAKR has very rich medical, dental and vision insurance plans, along with a generous 401(k) retirement plan. In addition to base salary, employees are eligible for a year-end bonus. SEAKR offers a variety of paid leave, such as vacation, sick, bereavement, and FMLA.

SEAKR is an Equal Opportunity Employer - All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

US Citizenship Required

Applications will be accepted until 10/23/26.

jobs.title: Senior Channel Field Marketing, South Central
jobs.description:
Get to Know Us

Horizon3 is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find and fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs. 

We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

 

What You’ll Do

We are seeking a Senior Channel Field Marketing Manager to own co-marketing strategy and execution with Horizon3's channel partners in the South Central region. You will drive partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline through high-signal field programs, working alongside Horizon3's Partner Business Managers to build account coverage, accelerate deals in market, and hold every program to a CPO and ROI threshold.

You will be the senior marketing partner to Horizon3's VAR, reseller, alliance, and distribution partners in the region, and to the Partner Business Managers who cover them. You own the co-marketing motion end to end: which partners get investment, joint program design, MDF management, execution, follow-up, and pipeline attribution.

Channel is a critical growth lever for Horizon3, and partner-driven pipeline needs an owner who understands both the field motion and the partner ecosystem. If you have spent your career running co-marketing programs with one eye on the partner relationship and the other on pipeline ROI, this role was built for you.



This role will be responsible for…..



Channel Co-Marketing Strategy and Planning

 - Own the South Central channel field marketing strategy, covering the region's partners and partner events, and a co-marketing portfolio built to generate net-new partner-sourced pipeline and accelerate partner-influenced deals already in motion.

 - Decide where co-marketing investment goes. Prioritize partners and programs by pipeline opportunity, not by who asks for budget.

 - Own the channel marketing calendar, aligned to partner priorities, regional sales plays, and company campaign themes, so partner programs ladder up to integrated demand gen motions.

 -  Define and enforce pipeline ROI standards as the gate for all channel field investment. Every program needs a pipeline hypothesis going in and a pipeline outcome coming out.



Partner Programs and MDF

 - Design and execute joint field programs with VARs, resellers, alliance partners, and distributors: co-hosted events, partner-led roundtables, joint conference activations, roadshows, and CISO-focused experiences.

 - Own MDF end to end: allocation strategy, partner alignment, execution oversight, budget tracking, and attribution reporting. MDF is an investment with an expected return, not a partner benefit to be dispersed.

 - Build repeatable co-marketing playbooks that scale across partners without rebuilding each program from scratch.

 -  Coordinate SDR, Partner Business Manager, and partner seller follow-up for every program, with defined SLAs.



Partner and Sales Alignment

 - Serve as the senior marketing counterpart to the region's Partner Business Managers and partner marketing contacts, and run joint planning and business reviews with priority partners.

 - Work with regional field marketers so partner programs and direct programs cover the same accounts without colliding.

 - Partner with partner marketing and product marketing on joint messaging and proof points.



Pipeline Accountability and Reporting

 - Own partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline reporting: meetings booked, pipeline created, stage progression, and ROI by partner and by program.

 - Partner with marketing operations to keep partner attribution clean in Salesforce.

 - Report to field marketing and channel leadership on a regular cadence, with clear recommendations on which partners and programs to scale and which to cut.

 - Mentor Channel Field Marketing Managers and Specialists. This role has no direct reports.



What You’ll Bring

 - 6+ years of B2B channel or field marketing experience, with ownership of partner co-marketing programs and measurable pipeline contribution.

 - Proven track record building and executing co-marketing programs with VARs, resellers, alliance partners, or distributors, with the pipeline data to back it up.

 - Experience owning MDF budgets, including allocation decisions, partner alignment, and ROI reporting.

 - Strong understanding of the B2B technology channel ecosystem: how partners sell, what motivates them, and how to design programs that drive joint pipeline rather than just partner satisfaction.

 - Financial fluency: comfortable building CPO and ROI cases and recommending investment trade-offs to leadership.

 - Proficiency with Salesforce for pipeline tracking, partner attribution, and co-marketing performance reporting.

 - Strong cross-functional collaboration skills across Partner Business Managers, channel sales, direct field marketing, demand gen, digital, ABM, and product marketing.

 - Highly organized, able to manage multiple partner relationships, programs, and timelines at once without losing accountability or momentum.



What Sets You Apart?

 -  Experience in cybersecurity, DevSecOps, or adjacent B2B security markets.

 - Familiarity with Federal or Public Sector channel marketing, including distribution ecosystems like Carahsoft and compliance frameworks such as FedRAMP and CMMC.

 - Familiarity with intent data and ABM tools such as ZoomInfo or Reachdesk in support of partner-led account coverage.

 - Familiarity with Pardot, Marketo, or HubSpot for co-marketing campaign setup and attribution.



Travel Required

This role requires applicants to be based in the South Central region of the United States and willing to travel up to 40%.

 

Perks of Horizon3

 - Inclusive Team: We value diversity and promote an inclusive culture where everyone can thrive.

 - Growth Opportunities: Be part of a dynamic and growing team with numerous career development opportunities.

 - Innovative Culture: Work in a collaborative environment that encourages creativity and out-of-the-box thinking.

 - Hybrid & Remote Work: We embrace a mix of remote and hybrid work models depending on role and location, including our Chicago office, where some roles require regular in-office presence.

 - Competitive Compensation: We offer competitive salary, equity and benefits. Our benefits include health, vision & dental insurance for you and your family, a flexible vacation policy, and generous parental leave.



Compensation and Values

At Horizon3, we believe that our people are our greatest asset, and our compensation philosophy reflects this core value. We are committed to fostering an environment where all employees feel valued, respected, and rewarded for their contributions. Our compensation structure is designed to be fair, competitive, and transparent, ensuring that every team member is recognized and compensated equitably across roles, levels, and locations.

In accordance with various State’s transparency regulations, we provide the following salary range information for this position:

 - Base salary range: $145,000 - $185,000 annually. The exact salary will be determined based on the selected candidate’s location, qualifications, experience, and relevant skills.

 - Additional compensation: All full-time roles are eligible for an equity package in the form of stock options.



You Belong Here

Horizon3 is not just an equal opportunity employer - we are a community that values diversity, equity, and inclusion as fundamental principles of our culture and success. We are dedicated to fostering a workplace where everyone feels welcome and respected, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, hair length or any other legally protected status by law.

Our commitment to diversity and inclusion means we strive to attract, develop, and retain a workforce that reflects the varied communities we serve. We believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation and strengthen our ability to create cutting-edge cybersecurity solutions. At Horizon3, every team member is valued and supported in an environment that encourages personal and professional growth.

We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and experiences, and we encourage all qualified individuals to apply. Come be a part of Horizon3, where your unique contributions are recognized, and your potential is limitless.



Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice. 



Application Note

In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.

jobs.title: Operator III (Onsite)
jobs.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

As a Line Lead, Operator III (L3), you will help lead daily manufacturing execution by supporting production goals, quality and safety standards, and operator performance. You will independently manage day-to-day needs within your assigned area, resolve routine issues, and partner with L5/L4 Leads to support the broader operation. This role builds leadership, manufacturing process knowledge, and cross-functional communication skills.

What You’ll Do

Location: Onsite at Axon manufacturing facility - Pinnacle

Reports to: L5/L4 Line Lead and/or Manufacturing Supervisor

Direct Reports: Operators assigned to the production area

• Support daily production plans by understanding output goals, staffing needs, quality requirements, and changing floor priorities.

• Monitor assigned work areas, identify bottlenecks or downtime, and take appropriate action to keep production moving safely and efficiently.

• Follow manufacturing procedures and understand when to initiate or support NCMRs, escalations, and Engineering Work Orders (EWOs).

• Support EWO execution by communicating approved instructions, confirming the team follows the required process, and raising questions or concerns.

• Provide operators with clear direction, coaching, and timely feedback while reinforcing safety, quality, attendance, and performance expectations.

• Communicate professionally with operators, technicians, engineers, and L5/L4 Leads to resolve routine issues and share relevant production updates.

• Maintain accurate handoffs and follow through on assigned actions, open issues, and shift priorities.

• Identify recurring problems and improvement opportunities, and bring recommendations or concerns to the L5/L4 Lead or supervisor.

What You Bring

• Manufacturing or production experience with a strong understanding of floor procedures, quality, and safety expectations.

• Experience providing work direction, training, coaching, or support to teammates; prior leadership experience is beneficial.

• Working knowledge of production goals, basic performance metrics, NCMR processes, escalation paths, and EWO requirements, or the ability to learn them.

• Strong communication, organization, problem-solving, and prioritization skills; able to recognize when an issue needs additional support.

• Demonstrates Axon Values through ownership, teamwork, candor, quality-focused decisions, and a willingness to pursue improvements.

Benefits that Benefit You

• Competitive salary and 401k with employer match

• Discretionary paid time off

• Paid parental leave for all

• Medical, Dental, Vision plans

• Fitness Programs

• Emotional & Mental Wellness support

• Learning & Development programs

• Employee Resource Groups (ERGs)

• And yes, we have snacks in our offices

Benefits listed herein may vary depending on the nature of your employment and the location where you work.

Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Important Notes

The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. The job description may change or be supplemented at any time in accordance with business needs and conditions.

Some roles may also require legal eligibility to work in a firearms environment.

We collect personal information from applicants to evaluate candidates for employment. You may request access, deletion, or exercise other CCPA rights at axongreenhousesupport@axon.com or via our Axon Privacy Web Form. For more information, please see the Your California Privacy Rights section of our Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice.

Axon’s mission is to Protect Life and is committed to the well-being and safety of its employees as well as Axon’s impact on the environment. All Axon employees must be aware of and committed to the appropriate environmental, health, and safety regulations, policies, and procedures. Axon employees are empowered to report safety concerns as they arise and activities potentially impacting the environment.

We are an equal opportunity employer that promotes justice, advances equity, values diversity and fosters inclusion. We’re committed to hiring the best talent — regardless of race, creed, color, ancestry, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances — and empowering all of our employees so they can do their best work. If you have a disability or special need that requires assistance or accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please email recruitingops@axon.com.  Please note that this email address is for accommodation purposes only. Axon will not respond to inquiries for other purposes.

Phishing alert:  Axon will never ask you to pay for any part of the hiring process, including training, equipment, or background checks. We do not make job offers via text message, WhatsApp, or instant messaging platforms without a formal interview process.  All legitimate job openings are listed on our official careers page at https://www.axon.com/careers.  If you receive a suspicious offer or outreach from an email address that is not @axon.com, or if you are asked for sensitive personal information (bank details, Social Security Number) prematurely, please ignore the message and report it to recruitingops@axon.com.

jobs.title: Commercial Counsel
jobs.description:
Our healthcare system is the leading cause of personal bankruptcy in the U.S. Every year, over 50 million Americans suffer adverse financial consequences as a result of seeking care, from lower credit scores to garnished wages. The challenge is only getting worse, as high deductible health plans are the fastest growing plan design in the U.S.

Cedar’s mission is to leverage data science, smart product design and personalization to make healthcare more affordable and accessible. Today, healthcare providers still engage with its consumers in a “one-size-fits-all” approach; and Cedar is excited to leverage consumer best practices to deliver a superior experience.

The Role

Cedar is seeking a Commercial Counsel to join our Legal & Compliance Team. This role is ideal for a technology transaction with 4-6 years of enterprise cloud and technology experience who is a skilled drafter and capable dealmaker and is excited to help build how a modern legal team works with AI. You will join a highly collaborative Cedar Legal & Compliance team and serve as a go-to legal partner to Cedar’s growth, client management, sales, strategic partnerships, and vendor contracting teams, owning a portfolio of complex deals from structuring to signature. You will also help shape the playbooks, templates, and AI-enabled workflows the rest of the team relies on. Growth opportunities in the role based on your skills, experience, and interests may include product counseling, privacy, compliance, marketing, and general corporate matters, with guidance from experienced colleagues.

At Cedar, we offer customizable, enterprise solutions to leading health systems aimed at improving the healthcare financial experience for Americans, so our commercial agreements are large, complex and highly negotiated. This is a unique opportunity for you to work on high-stakes deals while helping curate the tech- and AI-forward tools and practices that help our team scale. You will have real latitude to improve our contracting process, grow your skills, get regular coaching and feedback, put new tools into practice, and see the direct impact of your work on deal velocity and our business.

Responsibilities

• Commercial Transactions: Structure, draft, and negotiate complex sales, vendor, and strategic partnership agreements, including Master Services Agreements (MSAs), HIPAA Business Associate Agreements (BAAs), license agreements, and consulting agreements. Own a portfolio of assigned matters from intake through execution, manage competing deadlines, and partner with product, privacy, and compliance legal colleagues for specialist support.

• Business Counseling: Serve as a trusted and pragmatic legal advisor to sales, finance, procurement, and business development teams on deal structures and commercial terms, including AI, technology licensing, data rights, and go-to-market activities.

• Technology, Ops, & AI Enablement: Partner with legal colleagues to identify and implement ongoing improvements of Cedar’s standard contract templates (MSA, BAA, NDA, Order Form, and Service Descriptions.), deal intelligence and playbooks, and legal processes to ensure they remain streamlined and "plain English." Collaborate with Legal & Compliance Operations to maintain and improve contract templates, playbooks, CLM tools, and technology-enabled contracting workflows. Use approved technology and AI tools to improve drafting, contract review, and access to contract information, with appropriate attention to confidentiality, accuracy, and team guidance. Measure and share results, such as cycle time and business self-service.

• Team: Contribute as a team player to help further the status of the Legal & Compliance team as an effective, respected, and valued resource within the company. Collaborate with the Legal Product, Regulatory, and Compliance team to understand relevant product and regulatory developments and incorporate agreed updates into Cedar’s agreements, templates, and guidance.

• Knowledge Sharing: Share practical learnings, business direction, and market insights with teammates. Seek and incorporate feedback, and support the onboarding and development of colleagues as appropriate.

• Outside Counsel Collaboration: Collaborate with specialized outside counsel and supplemental legal resources on assigned technology transactions and other matters, with attention to quality and budget.

• Periodic travel to New York and other locations for company and team meetings.

Required Skills & Experience

• JD Degree from an accredited law school and license in good standing to practice law in at least one state bar.

• 4-6 years of relevant legal experience at a leading law firm and/or in-house (a combination is a plus), including substantial experience drafting and negotiating technology transactions and enterprise SaaS agreements. Experience with AI, healthcare technology, and HIPAA is a strong plus, but not required.

• Legal Operations & AI Fluency: Hands-on experience improving how legal work gets done, from systems to tools, such as building playbooks or clause libraries, configuring workflows, or using AI tools for drafting and contract review, along with the judgment on how to use these tools inside and outside of the legal team.

• Adaptability and Growth Mindset: Thrives amidst shifting priorities and ambiguity, bringing clarity and direction where information or processes are still evolving. Eager to ask questions, incorporate feedback, learn new areas, and experiment with practical and AI-enabled improvements to legal workflows. Previous experience in technology or high-growth companies is preferred.

• Negotiation and Communication Skills: Demonstrated ability to lead assigned commercial negotiations with sophisticated organizations and their legal teams, partnering with senior counsel on novel, unusually complex, or material risks. Ability to explain complex terms and tradeoffs clearly to business stakeholders, develop pragmatic solutions, negotiate convincingly, and manage multiple matters with competing deadlines.

• Drafting Excellence: Strong contract drafting skills. Demonstrated ability to draft in plain English and write clear legal guidance that business partners can understand and apply. Experience identifying and contributing improvements to contract templates and playbooks.

• Business and Legal Judgment: Sound judgment in spotting product and commercial risks, weighing business objectives, and recommending pragmatic solutions. Comfort making risk calls independently within established guidelines, and knows when to escalate, seek input, or consult a colleague.

• Collaborative Mindset: A self-starter who takes ownership of assigned matters, follows through reliably, and builds effective relationships with Sales, Finance, Product, and other business partners. Works collaboratively within Legal & Compliance and seeks and shares expertise as needed.

Compensation Range and Benefits

• Salary/Hourly Rate Range*: $195,500 - $230,000

• This role is equity eligible

• This role offers a competitive benefits and wellness package

*Subject to location, experience, and education

#LI-REMOTE

What do we offer to the ideal candidate?

• A chance to improve the U.S. healthcare system at a high-growth company! Our leading healthcare financial platform is scaling rapidly, helping millions of patients per year

• Unless stated otherwise, most roles have flexibility to work from home or in the office, depending on what works best for you

• For exempt employees: Unlimited PTO for vacation, sick and mental health days–we encourage everyone to take at least 20 days of vacation per year to ensure dedicated time to spend with loved ones, explore, rest and recharge

• 16 weeks paid parental leave with health benefits for all parents, plus flexible re-entry schedules for returning to work

• Diversity initiatives that encourage Cedarians to bring their whole selves to work, including three employee resource groups: be@cedar (for BIPOC-identifying Cedarians and their allies), Pridecones (for LGBTQIA+ Cedarians and their allies) and Cedar Women+ (for female-identifying Cedarians)

• Competitive pay, equity (for qualifying roles), and health benefits, including fertility & adoption assistance, that start on the first of the month following your start date (or on your start date if your start date coincides with the first of the month)

• Cedar matches 100% of your 401(k) contributions, up to 3% of your annual compensation

• Access to hands-on mentorship, employee and management coaching, and a team discretionary budget for learning and development resources to help you grow both professionally and personally

About us

Cedar was co-founded by Florian Otto and Arel Lidow in 2016 after a negative medical billing experience inspired them to help improve our healthcare system. With a commitment to solving billing and patient experience issues, Cedar has become a leading healthcare technology company fueled by remarkable growth. "Over the past several years, we've raised more than $350 million in funding & have the active support of Thrive and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z).

As of November 2024, Cedar is engaging with 26 million patients annually and is on target to process $3.5 billion in patient payments annually. Cedar partners with more than 55 leading healthcare providers and payers including Highmark Inc., Allegheny Health Network, Novant Health, Allina Health and Providence.

jobs.title: Filson Seasonal Retail Sales Associate - Naperville
jobs.description:
Seasonal Retail Sales Associate

In 1897 C.C. Filson began outfitting prospectors headed for the Gold Rush with tools and apparel strong enough for the toughest spots on earth. More than 100 years later, Filson remains committed to providing pioneers of all fields around the world with unfailing goods made from the highest quality materials available.

Filson recognizes that it takes a world-class team to make a world-class product. As we build on the Filson legacy of American craftsmanship, we are looking for individuals who share our dedication to innovation, excellence, and superior customer service.

A Seasonal Sales Associate is responsible for supporting the Team through peak business times for a temporary predetermined amount of time. They will support the store business with personal selling achievements and the store's day-to-day operations. The Filson brand is built on a reputation of excellent product quality, performance and associate knowledge, and this position serves to provide exceptional customer service and team empowerment.

What you'll do:

• Ensure consistent Filson Way Guest Experience standards are met.

• Ensure Visual and Operational Standards are met.

• Greeting guests, answering phones, engaging guests daily.

• Gift Wrapping, as needed.

• Support the team during peak holiday months, November - January

• Achieve daily and weekly selling goals

• Occasionally support store events (in-store or offsite) outside of store posted operating hours, if needed

• Keeping all areas of the store clean, presentable, and stocked; perform duties related to opening and closing the store
