Your safety and security are important to us. Thank you for staying vigilant.

jobs.title: FP&A Manager
jobs.description:
Fortera is transforming one of the world’s largest industries by reinventing how cement is made. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, Fortera has developed next-generation cement technology that delivers high performance while reducing CO₂ emissions by up to ~70%. By mineralizing CO₂ and turning it into a productive feedstock, Fortera converts emissions into a valuable building material, creating a more sustainable path for modern construction.

With our commercial ReCarb® plant operating in Redding, California, and a growing global project pipeline, Fortera is moving from first-of-a-kind deployment to scaled commercialization. Our technology is already being used in real-world infrastructure applications, bringing next-generation cement into use today while expanding toward broader adoption.

At Fortera, you’ll work alongside scientists, engineers, operators, and industry experts who are turning cutting-edge materials science into real-world impact. We’re looking for curious thinkers, builders, and problem-solvers who want to help tackle one of the biggest challenges facing our planet.

This is more than a job. It’s an opportunity to help shape the future of sustainable construction.

Build What’s Next.

Visit www.forteraglobal.com to learn more.

THE ROLE:

We're hiring an FP&A Manager to help build the financial planning and reporting foundation Fortera will rely on as it scales from a single plant to a portfolio of them. You'll own the annual operating budget process, build the forecasts leadership relies on, and bring that same discipline to the capital budgets behind the plants we finance and build.

This is a small team, so you won't be maintaining someone else's process. You'll be setting up the systems, templates, models, and cadences that the rest of the business plans and reports around. You'll work with department heads to pull budgets together, track spend against plan with the Capital Projects team, and turn that analysis into monthly reporting packages, board materials, investor reporting, and lender reporting.

This role is a great fit for someone who enjoys that kind of environment. You know your craft, but you're also curious about the business beyond the numbers. You don't need everything handed to you. You see something that could work better and think, "I can fix that." You're comfortable asking questions, getting into the details, and building structure where it doesn't exist yet. Experience with capital-intensive or scaling businesses is a plus, but just as important is the ability to learn quickly, take ownership, and see your work make a real impact as Fortera grows.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

Operating Budgets

• Lead the annual operating budget process across departments.

• Build and maintain monthly and quarterly forecasts.

• Consolidate departmental inputs into a full company P&L, cash flow, and balance sheet outlook.

• Track actuals versus budget and forecast, and explain the key drivers behind variances.

• Work with department heads to understand business drivers and develop realistic financial assumptions.

Capital Project Budgets

• Develop and maintain detailed capital project budgets by project, phase, and cost category.

• Track committed costs, actual spend, forecast to complete, and total project cost.

• Monitor budget changes, contingencies, change orders, and timing shifts.

• Produce capital spend forecasts by month, quarter, and project lifecycle.

• Identify cost overruns, schedule-related budget impacts, and funding risks early.

• Prepare budget, forecast, and reporting packages required by lenders for capital projects.

• Maintain reporting support for draw requests and budget-to-actual reporting.

• Work closely with the Capital Projects team to understand project progress and its financial impact.

Reporting & Forecasting

• Prepare monthly reporting packages for leadership.

• Support executive presentations for leadership, the board, investors, and lenders.

• Build short-term and long-term cash flow forecasts.

• Provide financial analysis and modeling to support business decisions and planning.

Systems & Process

• Leverage SAP S/4HANA data and reporting structures to prepare budgets, forecasts, variance analyses, and capital project spend reports, and ensure planning outputs are aligned with financial actuals.

• Establish standardized templates and timelines for business partners to submit budget requests and project updates, and build and improve the processes and reporting cadence that support the full FP&A lifecycle as Fortera grows.

• Work closely with Accounting, Capital Projects, R&D, Engineering, and other teams to understand the business and its financial drivers.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

Required:

• Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, economics, or a related quantitative field.

• 5+ years of experience in FP&A, corporate finance, accounting, or a related analytical role.

• Experience owning a budgeting or forecasting process across multiple departments or stakeholders.

• Advanced Excel and financial modeling ability. You can build a budget or forecast model from a blank sheet, and you can explain and defend every assumption in it.

• Strong analytical judgment. You know when a number looks wrong, and you chase it down before anyone asks.

• Comfort with ambiguity. We're a scaling company. You can take a loosely defined question, scope it yourself, know what questions to ask, and come back with a structured answer.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to work closely with both financial and non-financial stakeholders.

• Able to communicate and work closely with technical teams, including R&D and engineering, and build a working understanding of the company's technology and production process.

• High level of ownership, attention to detail, and sound financial judgment.

Nice to Have:

• Experience with capital project budgeting or project finance in a capital-intensive industry such as manufacturing, industrials, energy, or infrastructure.

• Experience with SAP S/4HANA or a comparable ERP system.

• Experience preparing budget, forecast, or diligence materials for lenders, investors, or a board.

• Experience supporting capital project financing, draw requests, or lender reporting.

• Experience building FP&A processes and systems in a scaling or growth-stage company.

• Comfortable with AI and have incorporated it into your work.

WHY THIS ROLE:

• Build something that doesn't exist yet. You'll have real ownership in building Fortera's FP&A function, including the processes, models, and reporting infrastructure the company will rely on as it scales.

• Be close to the decisions. You'll work directly with the CFO, Controller, and executive team and see how financial analysis translates into real business decisions.

• Work at the intersection of finance and technology. You'll partner with R&D, Engineering, and Capital Projects and develop a firsthand understanding of the technology and plants we're building.

• See the impact of your work. The budgets and forecasts you build will help inform decisions about capital investments, new plants, and how Fortera scales.

• Have a voice. We're a small team, which means your ideas, judgment, and initiative can have an outsized impact on how we work.

• Join us while we're still building. If you like figuring things out, creating structure, rolling up your sleeves, and seeing your work make a tangible difference, you'll have plenty of opportunity to do that here.

Fortera is building a fundamentally different approach to cement, and we're doing it at a stage where the work you do today can shape what the company looks like tomorrow.

COMPENSATION:

The compensation package for this role includes a competitive base salary commensurate with experience of $140,000 - $175,000.

Fortera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other status protected by applicable law. Diverse candidates are encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: AI Delivery Lead
jobs.description:
AI Delivery Lead

eClinical Solutions is transforming clinical development with elluminate®, our Clinical Data Cloud, helping life sciences organizations unify, analyze, and unlock the value of their data faster than ever before. By combining a modern cloud platform with expert data services, we empower smarter decisions across the clinical trial lifecycle—accelerating innovation that ultimately improves patient outcomes.

Our engineering teams build enterprise-grade, revenue-generating products at the intersection of cloud, data, analytics, and emerging AI technologies. If you’re excited about building sophisticated software that makes a real-world impact on healthcare, this is the place to do it.

You will make an impact:

As an AI Delivery Lead, you will help transform how eClinical Solutions Engineering teams plan, build, test, and deliver software by driving adoption of AI-enabled software development practices across the organization.

You will work closely with Engineering, SQA, Product Management, Architecture, and DevOps to embed AI-assisted development and automation throughout the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC). You will help teams identify opportunities to eliminate manual activities, improve delivery predictability, strengthen automated quality, and demonstrate measurable improvements in engineering productivity and software delivery.

This role is ideal for someone who combines strong software delivery and Agile experience with a practical understanding of AI-assisted development and enjoys working directly with teams to turn new technologies and processes into repeatable engineering practices.

Your day to day:

• Drive adoption and continuous improvement of AI-assisted development and AI-DLC practices across Engineering teams.

• Work directly with Engineering, SQA, Product, Architecture, and DevOps throughout planning, development, testing, and release.

• Partner with teams during backlog refinement and sprint planning to improve story readiness, identify dependencies, and ensure development and automated testing are considered together.

• Identify opportunities to use AI and automation to reduce manual activities across requirements analysis, development, testing, documentation, and delivery.

• Help teams incorporate AI-assisted workflows into their day-to-day engineering practices using company-approved tools.

• Drive stronger integration between software development and test automation, including API and UI automation as part of feature delivery.

• Identify delivery bottlenecks, dependencies, and process gaps and work with teams to resolve them.

• Establish repeatable AI-enabled delivery practices and help scale successful approaches across multiple Engineering teams.

• Define and track meaningful delivery metrics, including cycle time, rework, automation coverage, manual test reduction, quality, and AI adoption.

AI & Modern Engineering Focus

We’re actively incorporating AI-powered capabilities into our platform, and you’ll help shape how this is done responsibly and effectively in an enterprise environment. This includes:

• Integrating and building LLMs and AI services into .NET- and Python-based systems

• Designing and implementing AI-assisted workflows, copilots, or intelligent automation features

• Working with agentic AI patterns (e.g., task orchestration, tool-using agents, workflow automation)

• Applying prompt engineering, evaluation techniques, and guardrails to ensure reliability and compliance

• Collaborating with data and platform teams to operationalize AI—not just prototype it

Deep ML expertise is not required—we’re looking for strong engineers who understand how to apply AI capabilities in real products.

Take the first step toward your dream career.  Here is what we are looking for in this role.

Qualifications:

• Experience leading software delivery across cross-functional Engineering, Product, SQA, Architecture, and DevOps teams, including Agile planning, execution, release management, and dependency management.

• Demonstrated experience introducing or scaling AI-assisted development, AI-enabled delivery, or AI-SDLC practices and translating those capabilities into measurable improvements.

• Experience driving Agile and engineering process transformation, including improvements to cycle time, delivery predictability, automation, quality, and team operating models.

• Experience leading complex initiatives across multiple teams and communicating delivery status, risks, dependencies, and measurable outcomes to senior leadership.

• Strong understanding of the Software Development Lifecycle, including requirements, software development, CI/CD, automated testing, release management, and software quality practices.

• Practical understanding of modern AI-assisted software development tools, agents, and workflows, with the ability to identify where AI and automation can safely improve or replace manual processes.

• Strong Agile delivery capabilities, including backlog readiness, refinement, sprint planning, risk and dependency management, and using delivery metrics to identify and remove bottlenecks.

• Ability to operate as a hands-on change and delivery leader, working directly with engineers, SDETs, Product Managers, architects, and DevOps rather than functioning primarily as a project coordinator or Scrum ceremony facilitator.

Nice to Have:

• Experience introducing AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or similar technologies within software engineering organizations.

• Experience with automated software quality practices, including API testing, UI automation, CI/CD, and continuous testing.

• Experience driving software delivery transformation in life sciences, healthcare, regulated SaaS, or other regulated environments.

• Experience developing dashboards and metrics that provide visibility into engineering productivity, quality, delivery flow, and AI adoption.

AI Use Statement

Employees are expected to appropriately leverage company-approved AI tools to improve productivity and quality while adhering to company policies, protecting confidential information, validating AI-generated content, and exercising sound professional judgment. AI is intended to augment—not replace—professional judgment, critical thinking, accountability, and decision-making. Accountability for all work remains with the employee.

Accelerate your skills and career within a fast-growing company while impacting the future of healthcare. We have shared our story, now we look forward to learning yours!

eClinical is a winner of the 2025 Top Workplaces USA Award for Remote Work! We have also received numerous Top Workplaces Culture Excellence Awards celebrating our exceptional company vision, values, and work-life balance. See all the details here: https://topworkplaces.com/company/eclinical-solutions/

eClinical Solutions is a people first organization. Our inclusive culture values the contribution that diversity brings to our business. We celebrate individual experiences that connect us and that inspire innovation in our community. Our team seeks out opportunities to learn, grow and continuously improve. Bring your authentic self, you are welcome here!

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer that values diversity. Our management team is committed to the principle that employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, culture fit and business need.

jobs.title: Site Reliability Engineer, Provider Operations
jobs.description:
ABOUT OPENROUTER

OpenRouter is the leading AI routing and infrastructure layer that enterprises use to access, manage, and optimize the best large language models across providers—without lock-in, capacity constraints, or unnecessary cost. We power the most advanced AI teams in the world by giving them the flexibility to move fast, scale confidently, and stay future-proof as models evolve.



As enterprise adoption of AI accelerates, OpenRouter sits at the center of how organizations operationalize LLMs across research, product, and production workloads.





ABOUT THE ROLE

OpenRouter routes almost a billion requests and more than 20 trillion tokens a day, across 80+ providers and thousands of endpoints. Every one of those providers can degrade, rate-limit, change behavior, or go down without warning. Our customers count on us to absorb that chaos so their apps never notice.

We're hiring our first AI Inference SRE to own the operational health of our provider supply. You'll make sure every endpoint we route to is fast, correct, and available, and that we detect and route around problems before customers do. You'll sit on the Provider Operations team, reporting to the Provider Operations Manager.





WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Provider health and observability. Build and own monitoring for every provider and endpoint: latency, throughput, error rates, uptime, and output correctness. Set SLOs per provider tier and alert on them.

 - Detection and failover. Improve how quickly we detect degraded endpoints, and work with the routing team so traffic shifts away from them automatically.

 - Incident response. Own on-call for provider incidents: triage, mitigate, communicate with providers, run postmortems, and drive follow-ups to closure.

 - Provider accountability. Turn telemetry into scorecards and SLO reporting that providers act on, and be the technical escalation point when a provider's endpoint is misbehaving.

 - Quality regression detection. Build continuous canaries and evals that catch silent regressions (quantization changes, broken tool calling, truncated streams, pricing or usage-reporting mismatches), not just outright downtime.

 - Automate the toil. Replace manual provider-ops work (disabling endpoints, capacity changes, deprecations, rate-limit tuning) with safe, auditable tooling.

 - Capacity and launch readiness. Build tooling to load-test endpoints before big launches so day-zero traffic doesn't take them down.


ABOUT YOU

 - 4+ years in SRE, production engineering, or infrastructure roles running high-traffic, customer-facing systems.

 - Strong with observability tooling and practice: metrics, tracing, logs, SLOs/error budgets, alerting that is always actionable.

 - Capable software engineer who prefers writing tools over executing runbooks. TypeScript and/or Python.

 - Experienced with distributed systems failure modes: timeouts, retries, backpressure, partial outages, noisy neighbors.

 - Calm, clear incident commander who communicates well with external partners under pressure.

 - Understands, or is eager to learn deeply, how LLM inference is served: streaming, tool calling, prompt caching, throughput/latency tradeoffs, and how provider APIs differ.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience at an inference provider, model lab, GPU cloud, or API gateway/CDN company.

 - Experience with our stack: TypeScript, Cloudflare Workers, Postgres, ClickHouse, GCP, Vercel.

 - Background in routing, load balancing, or traffic management systems.

 - Experience with evals or synthetic monitoring for ML systems.

jobs.title: Head of Product - SLS
jobs.description:
About Formlabs:

Do you want to change how the world creates?

At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before.

We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us.

The Opportunity:

We are looking for an exceptional hardware product leader to own and grow our SLS hardware business, and to be the architect of what comes next. Reporting directly to the CPO, you’ll step into an established business with a strong foundation and an exciting new chapter to shape. The role is becoming available as our current leader moves to take on new responsibilities within our growing R&D organization.

This isn't your typical product management role. You will operate with the autonomy of a startup founder, backed by the resources, brand, and manufacturing capability of a scaled company. You'll lead major hardware programs from concept to launch, lead a team of product managers, define roadmap strategy for an entire product line, and make the calls that determine how Formlabs competes and succeeds in additive manufacturing.

We're looking for someone who has done hard things: Founded a company, shipped physical products, and competed seriously to be #1. A background in 3D printing is not required. We build complex systems that span materials, robotics, and software, with a GTM engine that spans prosumer through industrial sales. The successful candidate has technical ability to dive deep across domains, commercial sense to understand what customers want and how to make it work for the business, marketing chops to communicate a compelling vision, the data skills and customer obsession required to support an opinionated point of view, and strong leadership traits: drive, grit, and desire to win.

Your Impact:

Your mandate is to define and drive the vision and strategy for the SLS business - identify where the market is going, build the roadmap to get there first, build the buy-in to execute across the organization, and lead the cross-functional teams that make it real. We value a bias for action, comfort with ambiguity, and deep ownership over outcomes. A successful leader has both a sharp understanding of what customers actually value, and a clear-eyed view of what's technically and commercially feasible, with the poise required to make challenging trade-offs required to build exceptional products, fast.

What You’ll Do:

• Own the full hardware product roadmap for the SLS business, across discovery, definition, development, and delivery, supported by strong customer insights and market analysis, through program execution and launch.

• Lead multi-disciplinary teams across engineering, design, manufacturing, and commercial functions. You are the connective tissue that ensures we ship exceptional products that customers love and drive strong financial results for the business.

• Make high-stakes decisions on product positioning, hardware architecture tradeoffs, and go-to-market timing. Understand the customer value behind every major call, not just the technical rationale.

• Represent the voice of the customer inside the building, and the voice of the product in front of customers. Be the person who actually knows how our hardware gets used, why, and by whom.

• Partner deeply with engineering leadership: know enough to pressure-test what's feasible, identify what smells wrong, and find solutions from adjacent domains when the obvious path is blocked.

• Operate with urgency. You don't wait for permission. You don't confuse activity with progress. You find a way.

About You:

We hire divergent people. Founders, athletes, people who've done something genuinely hard and come out the other side knowing what they're made of. If your path has been linear and comfortable, this is probably not the right fit.

• You've built real hardware - multiple generation products, major programs, or an entire company. You know what it takes to ship hardware that works reliably for the customer and for the business.

• You have previously led a significant business or founded a hardware venture. The experience of owning vision,P&L, roadmap, results, and team simultaneously is not new to you.

• You aren't just a "product person." You understand how roadmap strategy, technical hardware decisions, customer acquisition, and manufacturing operations must work in harmony.

• You possess the builder's mindset: the creativity to imagine what is possible, and the ability and the willingness to do whatever it takes to make it real - whether that's pitching a major customer, reviewing an engineering spec, or personally unblocking a production issue.

• You've gotten results without enough money, time, or people. You don't fold when the work gets difficult.

Bonus Skills:

• Experience in 3D printing, additive manufacturing, or adjacent physical product categories. (Having domain knowledge does not make you good at this job - but not having it will slow you down.)

• Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical discipline.

• MBA or equivalent experience owning a P&L or leading a high-growth GTM motion.

• Familiarity with hardware manufacturing standards and compliance (ISO, medical, aerospace, etc.).

• Strong proficiency with data - exploration, extracting signal from noise, sizing markets, and presenting findings in a way that drives decisions.

Our Benefits & Perks:

• Robust equity program to build future wealth through RSUs

• Comprehensive healthcare coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)

• 401K matching and access to financial advisors

• Generous paid Parental Leave (up to 16 weeks)

• Tenure-based paid Sabbatical Leave (up to 6 weeks)

• Flexible Out of Office Plan – Take time when you need it

• Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits

• Healthy on-site lunches, snacks, beverages, & treats

• Regular sponsored professional development opportunities

• Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community

• And of course… unlimited 3D prints

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company.  We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing.

Our Candidate AI Guidelines are available here. Please give them a read.

Compensation

Every Formlabs employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. You’ll have the opportunity to share financially in the value we create together, with a shared incentive to build a business that succeeds over the long term. Equity will be a significant portion of your total compensation, and will increase over time in proportion to your impact. The base pay will be determined by your skills, qualifications, experience, location, and expected impact on the organization.

The annual base pay range for this role is:

$160,000—$280,000 USD

jobs.title: Laser Process Engineer
jobs.description:
Atomic Machines is building the Matter Compiler™, the first in a new class of AI-native, all-digital manufacturing systems that build working machines directly from code. The Matter Compiler™ is aimed at micro-machines: motors and gears the size of a grain of sand, robots small enough to work inside the body, cooling built directly into the chips that run AI, and the many devices like them that have been waiting on a way to build them. Its first product is PrimeSwitch™, an electromechanical power relay the size of a button battery that carries 150 amps continuous current and opens in 50 microseconds, about a thousand times faster than a conventional contactor. Founded by Jeff Holden — serial entrepreneur, ex-Amazon SVP and Uber’s first Chief Product Officer — the company has raised $250 million to date.

Atomic Machines is based in the San Francisco Bay Area, with offices in Emeryville and Santa Clara.

About The Role:

We are seeking a technical leader to shape the future of our laser-based manufacturing processes, from development to scaled production. This role bridges advanced micromachining, materials physics, and optical systems, operating at the nexus of hardware, software, device design, and process. In this capacity, you will lead laser process development and optimization efforts to deliver rapid and precise operations, including cutting, milling, selective ablation, and welding using a suite of in-house-built pulsed-laser machines. You will champion innovative metrology methods to analyze laser–material interactions, including in situ probes, feeding AI-enabled learning and process optimization. Additionally, this role involves solving complex tool path optimization problems leveraging both commercial and custom CAD and CAM software packages. The ideal candidate is capable of carrying a laser processing technology through its entire life cycle—from first principles to experimentation and prototyping, and finally translating it to our digital, autonomous manufacturing platform at scale.

What You’ll Do:

• Lead the development, optimization, and scaling of pulsed-laser manufacturing processes, including cutting, milling, selective ablation, and welding.

• Design, implement, and analyze experiments to understand laser–material interactions across metals, ceramics, and polymers, and document and standardize processes to ensure reproducibility and support scale-up.

• Develop and refine tool paths and machine programs using CAD/CAM software and G-code to maximize precision and efficiency.

• Apply advanced metrology and materials characterization techniques to evaluate process outcomes and guide improvements.

• Work with laser system design engineers to translate process learnings into system usability, performance, and feature development.

• Partner with Design, AI, Hardware/Software, and Manufacturing teams while mentoring engineers and technicians to champion best practices and drive process quality and efficiency.

• Ensure safe operation of high-power laser systems, adhering to industry standards and internal safety protocols.

What You’ll Need:

• A master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Applied Physics, Materials, or a related field, and 10+ years of industry experience.

• Exceptional foundational knowledge of pulsed-laser physics (e.g., pulse duration, beam profile control), heat transfer, and materials science.

• Hands-on experience operating and troubleshooting pulsed-laser processing equipment and material responses, including nanosecond and femtosecond laser systems.

• Proficiency in CAD/CAM and machine tool programming, including G-code, for laser machining.

• Proficiency in design of experiments (DOE) and statistical process control (SPC), with fluency in tools like JMP, Minitab, SAS, or Python-based analytics.

• Experience with metrology tools, including optical imaging and profilometry, CMM, SEM/EDS/EBSD, XRF, X-ray CT, and IR imaging and spectroscopy.

• Exceptional communication and leadership skills, with a passion for mentorship, team building, and organizational scaling.

• Familiarity with AI/ML-enabled manufacturing and comfort collaborating with AI and software development teams is a plus.

The compensation for this position also includes equity and benefits.

Salary Range

$220,000—$250,000 USD

Atomic Machines is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity and does not discriminate based on characteristics protected by applicable law. We are committed to an inclusive interview experience, including for individuals with disabilities. To request an accommodation, contact rc@atomicmachines.com. To help our recruiting team manage application volume and respond to candidates more efficiently, Atomic Machines may use AI-assisted tools.

jobs.title: Software Product Manager
jobs.description:
Why LeoLabs?

At LeoLabs, we’re building the living map of activity in space. Through our proprietary global radar network and AI-enabled analytics platform, we collect millions of measurements each day on more than 25,000 objects in low Earth orbit (LEO). Our radar-powered intelligence helps protect critical assets, characterize activity in orbit, monitor emerging threats, and enable safer and more effective operations for commercial and government missions.

We’re not just building technology—we are redefining global security, safety, and transparency in space. As orbital activity accelerates and the operating environment becomes increasingly complex, LeoLabs is a trusted partner for Space Domain Awareness, Space Traffic Management, satellite operations, and national security missions around the world.

If you're looking to work on mission-critical challenges at the intersection of aerospace, national security, software, data, and AI, your impact starts here. This position is contingent upon final approval, with an anticipated hiring timeline beginning as early as January 2027. We are beginning the search in advance of the anticipated hiring timeline.

LeoLabs is seeking a Software Product Manager to join our Product organization and lead the continued development, commercialization, and growth of our SDA software product , one of LeoLabs’ core software products.

Our SDA software product transforms LeoLabs’ radar data and space-domain information into operational intelligence, analytics, alerts, and mission workflows that help customers understand what is happening in orbit and act with greater speed and confidence.

This role sits at the intersection of customers, market needs, product strategy, engineering, and business objectives. You will be responsible for understanding customer missions and market opportunities, defining where our SDA software product should compete, translating those needs into differentiated product capabilities, and helping turn those capabilities into products customers can adopt and buy.

The ideal candidate is a strong product thinker with both commercial and technical judgment. You should have experience working in the space industry or in a closely related aerospace or national-security environment, be comfortable engaging directly with sophisticated commercial and government customers, and be able to translate complex mission problems into clear product and business direction.

What You’ll Do

• Own the product and business strategy for our SDA software product, including product vision, roadmap, market positioning, prioritization, packaging, and execution

• Develop a deep understanding of our SDA software product customers, users, missions, workflows, operational challenges, and buying behavior

• Work directly with commercial and government customers, operators, analysts, internal stakeholders, and subject-matter experts to identify unmet needs, validate product opportunities, and understand where LeoLabs can create differentiated value

• Identify and prioritize market segments, use cases, and customer problems where Our SDA software product can create meaningful mission impact and business growth

• Translate customer, mission, and business requirements into clear product requirements, capabilities, user experiences, and prioritized development work

• Partner closely with Engineering throughout the product lifecycle, from discovery and definition through development, testing, release, and iteration

• Make product investment decisions based on customer value, strategic differentiation, revenue potential, technical feasibility, scalability, and company priorities

• Define how our SDA software product capabilities are packaged and positioned so customers can clearly understand what they are buying, why it matters, and how it supports their mission

• Partner with Sales, Business Development, Marketing, and Customer Success to support customer engagements, product demonstrations, proposals, strategic pursuits, pilots, and go-to-market activities

• Help shape pricing, packaging, and commercial models for our SDA software product offerings in partnership with Product leadership and other business stakeholders

• Maintain and communicate a clear product roadmap and ensure alignment across Product, Engineering, Sales, Business Development, Customer Success, Operations, and company leadership

• Define and monitor product and business metrics that measure adoption, usage, customer outcomes, time-to-value, retention, expansion, revenue impact, and overall product performance

• Lead product launches and internal enablement, ensuring that Sales, Customer Success, and other customer-facing teams can effectively communicate and sell new our SDA software product capabilities

• Continuously evaluate competitors, adjacent markets, customer acquisition trends, emerging technologies, and changes in the space and national-security environment to identify new opportunities for our SDA software product

• Distinguish between individual customer requests and repeatable market needs, ensuring our SDA software product evolves as a scalable product rather than a collection of one-off solutions

• Help establish and improve product management practices as LeoLabs continues to scale its product organization

What We’re Looking For

• 5+ years of product management experience, preferably with software, data, analytics, enterprise, or other highly technical products

• Professional experience working in the space industry, or in a closely related aerospace, defense, or national-security environment, with demonstrated understanding of space missions, customers, operators, or technologies

• Demonstrated experience owning products or major product areas from market discovery and product strategy through development, launch, adoption, and iteration

• Strong business judgment and the ability to connect product decisions to customer outcomes, competitive differentiation, revenue opportunities, and company strategy

• Strong customer orientation and experience engaging directly with customers to uncover needs, validate opportunities, and translate feedback into scalable products

• Demonstrated ability to translate complex technical, operational, or customer problems into clear product direction and priorities

• Experience working closely with software engineering teams and technical leaders throughout the product development lifecycle

• Ability to make informed prioritization decisions across competing customer requests, business opportunities, strategic priorities, and technical constraints

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with engineers, customers, executives, operators, and other technical and non-technical audiences

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to use both quantitative and qualitative information to make product decisions

• Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving environment where customer needs, technology, and market conditions can evolve quickly

• Curiosity and willingness to develop deeper expertise in complex space, technical, and mission domains

• Ability to operate with a high degree of ownership and independently drive product decisions while building alignment across multiple organizations

• Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally to engage directly with customers, partners, and internal teams. LeoLabs is a global company with customers and users around the world, and this role will require periodic travel to understand customer missions, support key engagements, and represent the product in-market

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience building and commercializing products for government, aerospace, defense, intelligence, or other highly technical markets

• Direct experience with Space Domain Awareness, Space Situational Awareness, Space Traffic Management, satellite operations, orbital analysis, command and control, or related space missions

• Experience working with satellite operators, space mission operators, U.S. government space organizations, allied defense organizations, or commercial space companies

• Familiarity with orbital mechanics, tracking data, conjunction assessment, maneuver detection, satellite behaviors, or other space-domain concepts

• Experience supporting government acquisition processes, strategic pursuits, proposals, demonstrations, pilots, or customer evaluations

• Experience working with data-intensive products, APIs, analytics platforms, event detection, visualization tools, or operational decision-support systems

• Experience defining product packaging, pricing, positioning, or go-to-market strategy

• Experience working directly with government and commercial customers in complex enterprise sales environments

• Technical background or demonstrated experience working closely with highly technical engineering, data science, scientific, or aerospace teams

• Experience working in markets where customer requirements may be ambiguous, procurement cycles are complex, and product managers must identify common product needs across multiple customer missions

• Active U.S. Government security clearance, or the ability and willingness to obtain and maintain one, is preferred

What Success Looks Like

In this role, success means:

• Our SDA software product has a clear product and market strategy that is aligned with LeoLabs’ broader business objectives and differentiated from competing offerings

• The organization has a strong understanding of our SDA software product ’s target customers, priority missions, use cases, value propositions, and commercial opportunities

• Our SDA software product capabilities are packaged and positioned in ways that are easy for customers to understand, evaluate, purchase, and adopt

• Engineering has clear product direction, well-defined priorities, and a strong understanding of the customer and business outcomes behind the work

• Customer and market feedback consistently inform product decisions without allowing one-off customer requests to derail the broader product strategy

• Our SDA software product delivers measurable improvements in customer mission outcomes, adoption, usage, retention, and overall customer value

• Our SDA software product contributes meaningfully to LeoLabs’ revenue growth through new customer acquisition, expansion, strategic programs, and increased product adoption

• Sales and Business Development teams have compelling products, demonstrations, messaging, and supporting materials that allow them to confidently take our SDA software product to market

• Cross-functional teams have clear visibility into product priorities, upcoming capabilities, market positioning, and product launches

• Our SDA software product continues to evolve based on customer outcomes, market demand, competitive dynamics, product data, and LeoLabs’ long-term strategy

Compensation

This position is benchmarked to Denver, CO with a base salary range of $171,000–$194,000, plus bonus and equity. Actual base salary will be determined based on the candidate’s work location, experience, skills, and other applicable factors

Perks and Benefits

• 100 USD monthly wellness benefit to support your health and well-being

• $300 USD home office setup stipend, available for use within your first six months

• $75 USD monthly home internet allowance, paid directly through your regular paycheck

• Individual Development Fund to support training, learning, and professional development

• Employee Recognition Program to celebrate contributions and achievements across the team

• Employee Referral Program so you can help us connect with great talent

• And much more!

ITAR Requirements

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. More information regarding ITAR can be found at DDTC’s website.

jobs.title: Accounting Operations Contractor
jobs.description:
We are looking for talented professionals to be a part of a dynamic team. We place a focus on professionalism, kindness, integrity, and a high level of confidentiality, with the goal to deliver best in class service while providing a positive working experience for its staff.

Accounting Operations Contractor

About the role

We are a private family office managing a diverse portfolio and operations across multiple entities and departments. Our accounting operations are currently outsourced to an external firm, and the function's rapid growth has created an opportunity to strengthen internal processes and structure.This role is here to ensure close runs on time, coding is consistent and accurate and deliverables SLA and process are documented and adhered to. The contractor will not redesign the function, instead will have the ability to make the current one run on a clock and put it on paper. • Tighten the AP process, cadence, with QC and review built in

• Bring close timing down month over month to T+14 by month 6 and document what moves it

• Own internal accounting process such as credit card, travel log and reimbursements, payroll and benefits booking, and allocations

jobs.title: Senior / Staff Software Engineer, Internal Tools
jobs.description:
ABOUT SUNO

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).



Listen to the Suno version of this role! https://suno.com/s/JVtvqMYdNoW6fffg



About the Role

AI is changing how software gets built and how companies run, and we’re at the front of it. We're hiring a Senior / Staff Software Engineer to own direction and architecture on our AI Operations Engineering team. Suno is scaling incredibly fast and our job is to unlock growth for operations areas like music ops, support, legal, finance, and beyond with workflows, tooling, and intelligent agents.



What You'll Do

 - Build agents, workflows, and custom tools that let non-engineering teams handle more without adding headcount

 - Evaluate and integrate third-party tools, making the call on what to buy and what to build

 - Contribute to and empower stakeholders on our self-service app deployment platform

 - Design and implement new patterns for internal APIs, auth and MCP building and extending beyond our Django monolith.

 - Integrate and scale customer experience systems built around third parties like Zendesk.

 - Partner with customer experience, legal, finance, people, and content ops to source new challenges



What You'll Need

Must-Haves

 - You bring 5–7+ years of full-stack software engineering experience

 - You have a proven track record of building, maintaining, and supporting internal tooling or systems that streamline engineering or business operations

 - You’re eager to learn and share agentic coding best practices and tools

 - You thrive in an early-stage, 0→1 environment where the problem space is still being defined



Nice-to-Haves

jobs.title: Radar Product Manager
jobs.description:
Why LeoLabs?

At LeoLabs, we’re building the living map of activity in space. Through our proprietary global radar network and AI-enabled analytics platform, we collect millions of measurements each day on more than 25,000 objects in low Earth orbit (LEO). Our radar-powered intelligence helps protect critical assets, characterize activity in orbit, monitor emerging threats, and enable safer and more effective operations for commercial and government missions.

We’re not just building technology—we are redefining global security, safety, and transparency in space. As orbital activity accelerates and the operating environment becomes increasingly complex, LeoLabs is a trusted partner for Space Domain Awareness, Space Traffic Management, satellite operations, and national security missions around the world.

If you're looking to work on mission-critical challenges at the intersection of aerospace, national security, sensing, software, data, and AI, your impact starts here. This position is contingent upon final approval, with an anticipated hiring timeline beginning as early as January 2027. We are beginning the search in advance of the anticipated hiring timeline.

LeoLabs is seeking a Radar Product Manager to lead the continued development, commercialization, and growth of our transportable radar product, our radar-based space domain awareness product.

Our transportable radar product combines advanced radar sensing, software, data processing, and operational capabilities to provide customers with persistent, high-quality information about objects and activity in low Earth orbit. Our transportable radar product extends LeoLabs' ability to deploy sensing capability where customers need it and enables a range of commercial and government missions.

This role sits at the intersection of customers, product strategy, radar technology, engineering, operations, deployment, and business objectives. You will be responsible for understanding customer missions and market opportunities, defining where our transportable radar product should compete, shaping the capabilities and configurations customers need, and helping turn advanced radar technology into scalable products and services customers can buy, deploy, and operate.

The ideal candidate is a strong product thinker with both commercial and technical judgment. You should have experience working in the space industry or in a closely related aerospace or national-security environment, be comfortable working with complex hardware and software systems, and be able to translate customer missions and technical capabilities into clear product and business direction.

What You’ll Do

• Own the product and business strategy for our transportable radar product, including product vision, roadmap, market positioning, prioritization, packaging, configurations, and execution

• Develop a deep understanding of our transportable radar product customers, users, missions, workflows, operational environments, procurement considerations, and buying behavior

• Work directly with commercial and government customers, operators, mission partners, internal stakeholders, and subject-matter experts to identify unmet needs, validate product opportunities, and determine where our transportable radar product can create differentiated value

• Identify and prioritize market segments, mission areas, use cases, deployment models, and customer problems where our transportable radar product can create meaningful mission impact and business growth

• Translate customer, mission, and business requirements into clear product requirements, system capabilities, configurations, interfaces, and prioritized development work

• Partner closely with radar, hardware, software, systems, data, infrastructure, and operations teams throughout the product lifecycle, from discovery and definition through development, integration, testing, deployment, operation, and iteration

• Make product investment decisions based on customer value, strategic differentiation, revenue potential, sensor performance, technical feasibility, operational complexity, scalability, and company priorities

• Define how our transportable radar product capabilities, configurations, service levels, and access models are packaged and positioned so customers can clearly understand what they are buying, what mission outcomes it enables, and how it differs from other LeoLabs offerings

• Partner with Sales, Business Development, Marketing, and Customer Success to support customer engagements, technical discussions, demonstrations, proposals, strategic pursuits, pilots, and go-to-market activities

• Help shape pricing, packaging, service models, and commercial structures for our transportable radar product offerings in partnership with Product leadership and other business stakeholders

• Develop a strong understanding of the tradeoffs between radar performance, deployment location, coverage, capacity, tasking, reliability, availability, maintainability, cost, and customer mission outcomes

• Partner with Engineering and Operations to understand radar performance and identify opportunities to improve sensing capability, data quality, coverage, availability, operational efficiency, and customer value

• Help define requirements for how customers interact with and task our transportable radar product, how measurements and data products are delivered, and how our transportable radar product integrates with customer and LeoLabs software systems

• Maintain and communicate a clear product roadmap and ensure alignment across Product, Engineering, Radar Operations, Sales, Business Development, Customer Success, and company leadership

• Define and monitor product, business, and operational metrics that measure customer outcomes, radar performance, availability, utilization, adoption, reliability, deployment effectiveness, revenue impact, and overall product performance

• Lead product launches and internal enablement, ensuring that customer-facing teams can effectively explain, demonstrate, position, and sell our transportable radar product capabilities

• Continuously evaluate competing sensing solutions, emerging radar and sensor technologies, customer acquisition trends, market developments, and evolving space and national-security requirements to identify new opportunities for our transportable radar product

• Distinguish between one-off customer requirements and repeatable market needs, ensuring our transportable radar product evolves as a scalable product family rather than a collection of bespoke radar programs

• Help establish and improve product management practices as LeoLabs continues to scale its product organization

What We’re Looking For

• 5+ years of product management experience, preferably with products involving hardware, software, data, sensing, infrastructure, or other complex technical systems

• Professional experience working in the space industry, or in a closely related aerospace, defense, or national-security environment, with demonstrated understanding of space missions, customers, operators, or technologies

• Demonstrated experience owning products or significant product areas from market discovery and product strategy through development, deployment, launch, adoption, and iteration

• Strong business judgment and the ability to connect product decisions to customer mission outcomes, competitive differentiation, revenue opportunities, and company strategy

• Strong customer orientation and experience engaging directly with customers to uncover needs, validate opportunities, and translate feedback into scalable products

• Demonstrated ability to understand complex technical systems and translate technical capabilities, limitations, and tradeoffs into clear product direction and priorities

• Experience working across multidisciplinary engineering teams that may include hardware, software, systems, infrastructure, data, operations, or related technical functions

• Ability to make informed prioritization decisions across competing customer requests, market opportunities, engineering constraints, operational considerations, cost, schedule, and strategic priorities

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with engineers, operators, customers, executives, and other technical and non-technical audiences

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to use technical performance data, customer feedback, market information, and business considerations to make product decisions

• Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving environment where customer needs, technology, operational conditions, and market requirements can evolve quickly

• Curiosity and willingness to develop deeper expertise in radar, RF systems, space surveillance, orbital operations, and related technical domains

• Ability to operate with a high degree of ownership and independently drive product decisions while building alignment across multiple organizations

• Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally to engage directly with customers, partners, deployment teams, and internal stakeholders

• LeoLabs is a global company with customers, radar sites, partners, and users around the world, and this role will require periodic travel to understand customer missions, support key engagements and deployments, and represent the product in-market

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with radar, RF systems, remote sensing, ground-based sensors, satellite sensors, or other advanced sensing technologies

• Experience developing or commercializing products that integrate hardware, software, data, communications, infrastructure, and operational systems

• Direct experience with Space Domain Awareness, Space Situational Awareness, Space Surveillance and Tracking, satellite operations, orbital analysis, or related space missions

• Familiarity with missile warning, missile tracking, and integrated air and missile defense missions, including an understanding of how sensor performance, coverage, latency, tracking quality, and data delivery support operational warning and tracking architectures

• Experience working with satellite operators, U.S. government space organizations, allied defense organizations, intelligence organizations, or commercial space companies

• Familiarity with radar concepts such as detection, tracking, search, revisit rates, coverage, waveforms, beam scheduling, capacity, measurement quality, or sensor tasking

• Familiarity with orbital mechanics, tracking data, state vectors, conjunction assessment, maneuver detection, object characterization, or other space-domain concepts

• Experience with deployed products or infrastructure where reliability, availability, maintainability, logistics, site selection, and operational support are important product considerations

• Experience supporting government acquisition processes, strategic pursuits, proposals, demonstrations, pilots, customer evaluations, or major program captures

• Experience defining product packaging, pricing, configurations, service levels, or go-to-market strategy for complex technical products

• Experience working with products sold through multiple ownership, operating, or service models

• Experience working directly with government and commercial customers in complex enterprise sales environments

• Technical degree or background in engineering, physics, computer science, aerospace, electrical engineering, systems engineering, or a related field

• Active U.S. Government security clearance, or the ability and willingness to obtain and maintain one, is preferred

What Success Looks Like

In this role, success means:

• Our transportable radar product has a clear product and market strategy aligned with LeoLabs' broader business objectives and differentiated from competing sensing solutions

• The organization has a strong understanding of our transportable radar product's target customers, priority missions, deployment models, use cases, value propositions, and commercial opportunities

• Our transportable radar product capabilities and configurations are packaged and positioned in ways that customers can easily understand, evaluate, purchase, deploy, and use

• Our transportable radar product evolves from advanced radar technology into a scalable product family that can support multiple customer missions and business models without excessive customization

• Engineering and Operations have clear product direction, well-defined priorities, and a strong understanding of the customer and business outcomes behind the work

• Product decisions appropriately balance mission outcomes, radar performance, customer requirements, technical feasibility, deployment complexity, cost, schedule, and business value

• Our transportable radar product continues to improve in areas such as sensing performance, data quality, coverage, capacity, availability, reliability, deployability, operational efficiency, and customer usability

• Customers see measurable mission value from our transportable radar product and increasingly integrate its capabilities into their operational workflows

• Our transportable radar product contributes meaningfully to LeoLabs' revenue growth through new deployments, new customers, expansion opportunities, strategic programs, and increased adoption

• Sales and Business Development teams have clearly defined our transportable radar product offerings, compelling demonstrations, strong positioning, and supporting materials that allow them to confidently take our transportable radar product to market

• Product, radar, engineering, operations, and customer-facing teams remain aligned around priorities, product configurations, upcoming capabilities, deployments, and customer commitments

• Our transportable radar product continues to evolve based on customer outcomes, operational performance, market demand, competitive dynamics, technology advances, and LeoLabs' long-term strategy

Compensation

This position is benchmarked to Denver, CO with a base salary range of $171,000–$194,000 plus bonus and equity. Actual base salary will be determined based on the candidate’s work location, experience, skills, and other applicable factors

Perks and Benefits

• 100 USD monthly wellness benefit to support your health and well-being

• $300 USD home office setup stipend, available for use within your first six months

• $75 USD monthly home internet allowance, paid directly through your regular paycheck

• Individual Development Fund to support training, learning, and professional development

• Employee Recognition Program to celebrate contributions and achievements across the team

• Employee Referral Program so you can help us connect with great talent

• And much more!

ITAR Requirements

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. More information regarding ITAR can be found at DDTC’s website.

Vendor Notification

LeoLabs does not engage external staffing agencies or third-party recruiting firms for this role. Unsolicited candidate submissions will not be considered.

We are committed to maintaining a respectful and inclusive workplace where employees are valued for their skills, experience, and contributions. We are an equal opportunity employer and make employment decisions based on qualifications, skills, experience, and business needs, consistent with applicable law.

jobs.title: Clinical Supervisor, RDN (Part-time)
jobs.description:
About CookUnity:

Food has lost its soul to modern convenience. And with it, it has lost the power to nourish, inspire, and connect us. So in 2018, CookUnity was founded as the first-of-its-kind platform that connects the world with the source of truly great food: chefs. Today, CookUnity delivers 50 million meals a year from the industry’s best chefs to homes all over the country. Fresh. Ready-to-eat. And crafted with the passion that nourishes body and soul.

Unwilling to stop there, CookUnity is expanding beyond delivery to become an ever-innovating marketplace focused on our singular mission: empower Chefs to nourish the world.

If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting.

About the team:

The B2B team operates like a startup within CookUnity — entrepreneurial, fast-paced, and bold in its ambitions. We're building a new category at the intersection of food, healthcare, and outcomes-driven nutrition. Our Healthcare vertical is one of our highest-priority growth areas, and this role sits right at the center of it.

CookUnity is the leading chef-to-consumer platform connecting independent chefs with food lovers across the country. By combining culinary creativity with a powerful technology platform, we're redefining meal delivery and making chef-crafted meals more accessible than ever. Our mission is to empower chefs while delivering an exceptional food experience to customers nationwide.

About the Role:

CookUnity is building a clinical nutrition model to support the delivery of medically tailored meals (MTM) for members living with chronic conditions — primarily diabetes, cancer, weight management with GLP-1s, and cardiovascular disease. We work with a network of Registered Dietitian Nutritionists (RDNs), including 1099 contractors and subcontracted providers, to deliver nutrition assessments and nutrition education and counseling to members across diverse, medically complex populations.

The RD Supervisor will be the clinical anchor of this model. This is a part-time, fully remote role (~20 hours/week) for a seasoned RDN who brings deep clinical expertise, a passion for population health and food equity, and the judgment to translate evidence-based practice into scalable, culturally responsive care. You will work directly with CookUnity leadership and our two founding RDNs to co-develop the clinical framework, carry a focused direct-care caseload, and ensure every clinician in our network delivers consistent, high-quality care.

What You'll Do

This role ramps in three phases, though phases may overlap depending on contract timelines. The primary focus in the first 90 days is building the clinical model; direct patient care may begin concurrently if active contracts require it. Network supervision scales as the model and tools are in place.

Phase 1 — First 90 Days: Clinical Model Development (Primary Focus)

• Develop a framework for building and growing the CookUnity RDN network — defining the clinical competencies, disease-area specializations, and cultural and linguistic attributes required of network providers, and establishing a structured recruitment and vetting process to ensure every RDN added to the network is aligned with the CookUnity model of care.

• Co-develop disease-specific nutrition protocols for diabetes, oncology, weight management with GLP-1s, and cardiovascular conditions grounded in current evidence and clinical guidelines (ADA Standards of Care, ASCO, ACC/AHA, Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics Evidence-Based Practice Guidelines)

• Define the nutrition assessment framework — intake tools, flagging criteria, and escalation pathways for medically complex members

• Build structured visit frameworks for nutrition education and counseling (initial assessments, follow-up, and group modalities as applicable)

• Integrate behavior change methodology — including Motivational Interviewing, Stages of Change, and SMART goal-setting — into care delivery standards

• Establish culturally responsive practice standards to support care delivery across diverse patient communities

• Develop clinical documentation standards, quality metrics, and outcome tracking aligned with plan and regulatory requirements

• Build and curate a clinical resource library — including condition-specific patient education materials, counseling tools, and handouts — building on the existing nutrition assessment and education templates; the resource library will be the foundation for training and standardizing care delivery across the RDN network

Phase 2 — Direct Patient Care (May Begin Concurrently with Phase 1)

• Carry a defined direct-care caseload (target: 8–12 active members) spanning diabetes, cancer, weight management with GLP-1s, and cardiovascular conditions

• Conduct comprehensive nutrition assessments and develop individualized, person-centered care plans that incorporate medically tailored meal planning

• Deliver evidence-based nutrition counseling and education using behavior change frameworks

• Collaborate with health plan care teams and care coordinators on member care management and referral pathways

Phase 3 — Ongoing: RDN Network Supervision (As Model Matures)

• Provide clinical oversight and quality assurance for the CookUnity RDN network; scope of supervision calibrated appropriately for 1099 contractors (clinical quality and protocol fidelity) versus subcontracted providers

• Conduct regular chart audits and clinical case reviews to assess documentation quality, protocol adherence, and clinical appropriateness

• Facilitate monthly peer review or case consultation sessions with the RDN network

• Serve as the primary clinical escalation point for complex, high-acuity, or ethically sensitive cases

• Lead onboarding and training of contracted and subcontracted RDNs to the CookUnity clinical model — including use of the standardized nutrition assessment, the nutrition education template, and the clinical resource library — to ensure consistent, model-faithful care delivery across the network

• Identify individual and collective training needs; coordinate continuing education or skill-building resources for the network

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

• Active Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) credential in good standing with the Commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR)

• Active state dietitian licensure where required by state of practice (e.g., CDN in New York)

• 5+ years of clinical RD experience with a meaningful focus on chronic disease management — diabetes, cardiovascular disease, oncology, weight management, or combinations thereof

• Demonstrated experience delivering Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT) and nutrition counseling to vulnerable, medically complex, and/or diverse patient populations

• Familiarity with behavior change frameworks, including Motivational Interviewing

• Strong clinical documentation skills and comfort with telehealth or virtual care delivery

• Self-directed and comfortable building processes in a fast-moving, start-up environment

Preferred Qualifications and Certifications

• CDCES — Certified Diabetes Care and Education Specialist (strongly preferred; required for certain plan contracts)

• NBC-HWC — National Board Certified Health and Wellness Coach

• CSO — Board Certified Specialist in Oncology Nutrition

• CSOWM — Board Certified Specialist in Obesity and Weight Management (particularly relevant given GLP-1 meal line)

• Washington State Licensed Dietitian (LD) licensure, or willingness to obtain (preferred for current contract pipeline; licensure support available)

• FAND — Fellow of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics

• Formal Motivational Interviewing training or certification (MINT network or equivalent)

• Experience in medically tailored meal (MTM), food-as-medicine, or community-based nutrition programs

• Prior experience supervising or mentoring RDNs, dietetic interns, or clinical nutrition staff

Benefits:

🩺  Health Insurance coverage

🌅 401k Plan

⛱ PTO policy and paid sick day

🗓️ 5- year Sabbatical: After 5 years with CookUnity, you get a 4-week paid sabbatical

🐣 Paid Family leave

🕯 Compassionate Leave: 3-5 days each time the need arises

🥘 A generous amount of CookUnity credits to enjoy our amazing meals, added to your account, monthly

🤖 AI-forward workplace: enterprise access to ChatGPT and Claude to help you work smarter and grow faster.

🧘🏽‍♀️ Wellness perks: access to fitness subsidies to build a healthy lifestyle

👩🏾‍🏫 Personalized Spanish coach

🚀 Awesome opportunity to join a company that is looking to change how we eat and how chefs work!

If you’re interested in this role, please submit your application, and if we think you might be a fit, we'll get in touch with you. Thank you for your time!

CookUnity is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are dedicated to creating a community of inclusion and an environment free from discrimination or harassment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, citizenship status, protected veteran status, genetic information, or physical or mental disability.

A quick note for all candidates
We’ve recently seen an increase in recruitment scams across the industry, and we want to make sure you (and your data) stay safe while applying to CookUnity. We also want you to know that we take this seriously — sometimes, as part of our process, we may ask for a brief “proof of humanity” to confirm that we’re connecting with a real person, not an impersonator. Here are a few tips to help you protect yourself and know what to expect from us:

• Apply only through our official channels. All open roles are listed on our official careers page: careers.cookunity.com

• Our recruiters are real people — and easy to verify. You can always find them on LinkedIn with verified profiles. If you’re unsure, feel free to reach out to us on our official LinkedIn Company Page.

• We only communicate through official CookUnity channels. That means emails ending in @cookunity.com and interviews held through official company platforms (Google Meet or Zoom) — never WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS.

• We’ll never ask for payment or personal financial details. If anyone does, please don’t share any information and let us know right away.

If something ever feels off or you’re unsure about a message, we’d much rather you double-check with us. You can always contact us directly through any of our social media channels. We appreciate your interest in joining CookUnity — and we care about keeping your experience (and safety) as genuine as possible.

Lead the Crew. Own the Installation.

Bell Brothers is hiring an Electrical Lead Installer who combines residential electrical expertise with strong crew leadership and pride in workmanship.

You'll lead sold residential electrical installation projects from arrival through completion, taking responsibility for safe execution, code-compliant work, crew productivity, homeowner communication, and job closeout. This is a hands-on leadership role for an experienced electrician who can organize a project, solve field challenges, and develop the people working alongside them.

How We Work

At Bell Brothers, quality installation work means completing the approved scope correctly, respecting the homeowner's property, and keeping the crew safe and productive. You'll set the standard for workmanship, jobsite organization, and professional conduct.

We expect Lead Installers to coach less-experienced electricians and apprentices through clear instruction, thoughtful delegation, and field support. You'll assign work that matches each person's capabilities while remaining accountable for the finished installation.

You'll also know when to escalate. When site conditions, material needs, or technical concerns affect the approved plan, you'll work with Electrical leadership to resolve them rather than make unauthorized changes to scope, pricing, design, or customer commitments.

What You'll Do

• Lead residential projects including main panel replacements, service upgrades, subpanels, rewires, device replacements, dedicated circuits, system upgrades, and electrical work supporting other trades.

• Review the approved scope, material package, photos, notes, and installation requirements before starting work.

• Coordinate scope questions, technical concerns, material issues, and additional work requirements with the Electrical Field Supervisor or appropriate leader.

• Plan daily installation activities and assign tasks based on crew members' skills, project requirements, and safe work practices.

• Perform and oversee installations that meet applicable electrical codes, manufacturer requirements, company standards, and the approved scope.

• Coach apprentices and installers while maintaining responsibility for crew performance, conduct, and overall job execution.

• Keep homeowners informed about work progress, expected interruptions, project status, and completion.

• Monitor productivity and communicate potential delays or material shortages early, following department processes to keep work moving.

• Complete testing and quality checks before placing installed systems or equipment into service.

• Complete required ServiceTitan documentation, photos, invoice summaries, signatures, payment collection, financing paperwork, and work-completed acknowledgments.

• Identify and communicate return work, corrections, restoration, inspection items, and follow-up needs before closing the job.

• Maintain your assigned installation vehicle, tools, equipment, and company-issued property.

What You'll Bring

• Current California Residential Electrician Certification or higher electrical certification.

• Residential electrical installation experience sufficient to independently lead complex projects and direct a small crew.

• Strong knowledge of service upgrades, main panels, subpanels, rewires, device replacements, branch circuits, grounding and bonding, wiring methods, and residential electrical equipment.

• A strong understanding of applicable electrical codes and safe installation practices.

• Ability to lead, delegate to, and develop apprentices and other installation crew members.

• Professional communication with homeowners, crew members, and Electrical leadership.

• Ability to use ServiceTitan or similar field-service software and mobile technology.

Experienced residential installers, lead electricians, journeyman-level electricians, and residential service electricians with substantial installation and crew-leadership experience are encouraged to apply.

Working Conditions

This is a hands-on field role in residential properties, including occupied homes. You'll perform installation work while directing the crew, maintaining safe working conditions, and protecting the homeowner's property. Safe use of tools, equipment, and appropriate personal protective equipment is required.
